Frequently Asked Questions
01
Is this trip safe for solo women travellers?
Yes. Wovoyage is a women-led travel company founded in 2016 and based in Gurugram, India. Every women-only departure to Sikkim travels with a female trip leader, uses stays the team has vetted, and comes with 24/7 on-trip support. Most travellers join alone and share a twin room with another woman from the group.
02
Age Category
We don’t have any age policy. We have had 22-year-olds gel fantastically with 65-year-olds.
As long as you are fit to travel (get on flights, light walking), there is no restriction from our side.
03
Where will this trip start from?
The trip will start and end at Bagdogra Airport.
04
How group pickup & drop works?
A group pickup will be arranged; therefore, we recommend booking your flights only after consulting with us.

trips.title: Andaman Islands Tour with Port Blair Havelock and Neil Island

itinerary.title: Arrival in Port Blair – Cellular Jail & Light & Sound Show
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram) Airport, where the representative will welcome you and assist with your hotel transfer. After check-in and some time to relax, visit the historic Cellular Jail, followed by the Light & Sound Show in the evening, which narrates the stories of India’s freedom struggle. Overnight stay in Port Blair.
Notes
Cellular Jail remains closed on National Holidays.
Valid photo ID is mandatory for the Light & Sound Show.
Museum entry closes at 4:00 PM.
The English show operates on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
The show is subject to weather conditions.
AIrport pickup will be between 11-12 PM. If you arrive early you need to wait at the airport.

itinerary.title: Port Blair – Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep) – Radhanagar Beach
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed to the ferry terminal to board a premium ferry to Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep), enjoying the scenic journey across the Andaman Sea. Check in at the resort and later visit Radhanagar Beach, also known as Beach No. 7, famous for its white sand, turquoise waters and tropical surroundings. Spend a relaxing evening by the beach before returning to the resort. Overnight stay on Havelock Island.
Notes
Carry a valid photo ID for ferry boarding.
Report at the ferry terminal at least 1 hour before departure.
Ferry schedules are subject to weather conditions and Government approvals.

itinerary.title: Elephant Beach Excursion (Subject to Weather Conditions)
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, take a shared speedboat excursion to Elephant Beach, known for its turquoise waters, coral reefs and marine life. Enjoy the scenic surroundings, with optional water activities available at the beach, before returning to Havelock Island by boat in the afternoon. Overnight stay on Havelock Island.
Notes
Carry swimwear, a towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and a change of clothes.
If Elephant Beach remains closed due to weather conditions, an excursion to Kala Pathar Beach will be arranged.
Boat allocation is managed by the local boat association on a shared basis.

itinerary.title: Havelock Island – Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep)
itinerary.description: After breakfast, check out from the resort and board the ferry to Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep). Upon arrival, transfer to the resort and complete check-in. Later, explore Bharatpur Beach, known for its clear waters and scenic coastal views, followed by Laxmanpur Beach, admired for its peaceful atmosphere, white sandy shores and sunset views. Overnight stay on Neil Island.

itinerary.title: Neil Island – Port Blair
itinerary.description: After breakfast, check out and board the premium ferry back to Port Blair. Transfer to the hotel and complete check-in. The remainder of the day is at leisure, allowing you to relax at the hotel or explore nearby local markets and surroundings at your own pace. Overnight stay in Port Blair.

itinerary.title: Ross Island & North Bay Coral Island Excursion
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, proceed for a full-day excursion to Ross Island (Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Dweep) and North Bay Coral Island. Explore the historic ruins, old buildings and green surroundings of Ross Island, which reflect its colonial past. Later, visit North Bay Coral Island, known for its colourful coral reefs, clear waters and marine life. Optional underwater activities and water sports are available at an additional cost. Return to Port Blair for your overnight stay.
Notes
Ross Island remains closed every Wednesday.

itinerary.title: Departure from Port Blair
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out from the hotel and proceed to Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram) Airport for your onward journey. Bid farewell to the Andaman Islands, taking home memories of pristine beaches, turquoise waters, scenic islands and wonderful experiences. Tour concludes.
Notes
Airport Drop off will be between 11 AM - 12 PM.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Bagdogra Airport and transfer to Phuentsholing
Drive to Paro and visit Rinpung Dzong
Hike to Taktsang, or Tiger’s Nest Monastery
Drive to Punakha via Dochula Pass and visit Chimi Lhakhang
Travel to Thimphu, visit Bhutan Post Office and Tashichho Dzong, and celebrate New Year
Explore Thimphu, Buddha Dordenma, Takin Preserve and Simply Bhutan
Cross into Jaigaon and transfer to Bagdogra Airport
Welcome to Kerala
itinerary.description:
Cochin sightseeing Land at Cochin International Airport
— flights arriving by 11:30 am work best — where our trip leader will be waiting to welcome you and take you to the hotel in Fort Kochi. Check in, drop your bags and let it sink in:
Tea Hills to Tides has officially begun.
🇮🇳
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Land. Explore. Welcome to Kerala.
The afternoon is all heritage. Walk along the harbour to watch the centuries-old
Chinese fishing nets dip into the water exactly as they have for 500 years, then wander through the Naval Museum, St Francis Church, Santa Cruz Basilica and Mattanchery Palace with its striking Kerala murals.
💡 WHY TODAY IS EASY
It’s your first day in Kerala. Today you just need to arrive, settle in, and ease into Fort Kochi’s slow, salty charm.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Fragrant Nature Cochin or similar, Kochi

itinerary.title: Transfer to Munnar
itinerary.description:
Roadtrip and sightseeing After breakfast, set off on the drive to Munnar
— around 4 hours winding up through the Western Ghats as the coastal flatlands give way to forest and tea country. Break the journey at the Cheeyappara and Valara Waterfalls, twin cascades tumbling right beside the highway.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Waterfalls, spice, and cooler air.
Stop at an authentic Kerala Spice Garden, where cardamom, pepper, nutmeg and vanilla grow side by side, before continuing into Munnar. By the time you check in, the air has turned noticeably cooler — your first sign you’ve left the coast behind.
💡 WHY TODAY IS SCENIC
The drive itself is half the experience today — waterfalls, spice gardens and the Ghats rolling by are worth savouring, not rushing through.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
The Leaf Munnar or similar, Munnar

itinerary.title: Munnar sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Local exploration A full day to explore the highlands, starting with Eravikulam National Park
— home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr and tea plantations spilling down every hillside. Next, the Tea Museum, where you’ll see exactly how the leaves in your morning cup are grown and processed.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Green, as far as you can see.
The afternoon takes in Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point, and Kundala Lake with its own shikara rides, before the 2nd Mile Viewpoint and a quiet evening at the Botanical Garden to close out the day.
💡 WHY TODAY IS A FULL DAY
Munnar packs a lot into a small radius. Since there’s no onward drive today, we use the extra time to properly cover the hills instead of rushing past them.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
The Leaf Munnar or similar, Munnar

itinerary.title: Transfer to Alleppey
itinerary.description:
Alleppey sightseeing Drive 3 to 4 hours toward Alleppey, and watch the landscape change again — Kerala’s famous backwaters open up into a vast network of canals, lagoons and lakes where village life happens entirely on water.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Water, palms, and quiet.
This afternoon is the Shikkara boat ride — a slow glide through the backwaters past coconut groves and paddy fields. Round off the day at the historic Alleppey Lighthouse, one of India’s oldest and still operational, and a walk on Alleppey Beach.
💡 WHY TODAY IS THE HIGHLIGHT
The Shikkara ride is the single most-requested moment of this trip. Everything else today is paced around giving it the time it deserves.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Lake Canopy Alleppey or similar, Alleppey

itinerary.title: Transfer to Trivandrum
itinerary.description:
Kovalam sightseeing Drive 4 to 6 hours toward Kovalam, depending on traffic, with a stop at the Jatayu Earth’s Centre in Chadayamangalam — a cable car ride up for panoramic views across the Western Ghats.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Cliffs, temples, and the sea at last.
Next, the Azhimala Shiva Temple, dramatically positioned where the cliffs meet the sea. Arrive into Kovalam in time to soak in your first proper look at the Arabian Sea.
💡 WHY TODAY IS WORTH THE DRIVE
It’s the longest drive of the trip, but it’s also the one that takes you from backwaters to coastline — two stops along the way make sure it doesn’t feel like just a transit day.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Travancore Heritage Kovalam or similar, Kovalam

itinerary.title: Free Day and Departure
itinerary.description:
Group transfer to airport A calm last morning. Breakfast at a relaxed pace, with some free time before checkout — no early starts today.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
One last morning in Kerala.
Visit the Padmanabhaswamy Temple
— one of the wealthiest and most sacred Vaishnava temples in India (dress code applies: covered, traditional attire). Then a group transfer to Trivandrum International Airport for flights home.
💡 WHY TODAY IS RELAXED
After five full days, the last morning is kept deliberately light — one meaningful stop, then home, with no rush to the airport.
✈️ DEPARTURE
Book flights out of Trivandrum (TRV)
departing after 6:00 pm

itinerary.title: Arrive in Guwahati!
itinerary.description:
Transfer to Shillong (110 kms / 3hrs)
– Welcome to Northeast India! Arrive at Guwahati Airport and meet your fellow female travelers.
– Drive to Shillong (approx. 3–4 hours), the scenic capital of Meghalaya.
– If time permits, visit the stunning Umiam Lake (Borapani Lake) – one of the largest lakes in – – – Shillong, perfect for scenic photos and peaceful views.
– Enjoy a relaxed evening exploring Shillong at your own pace.
Accommodation: Shillong Centre Point Hotel or similar Note: Meeting Point- Guwahati Airport, 9:00am. Please feel free to call/WhatsApp for flights assistance from your respective city +919811454591

itinerary.title: Scenic Drive to Cherrapunji (52 kms / 2-3hrs)
itinerary.description:
Land of Rain and Caves
– After breakfast, head to Cherrapunji (Sohra) – one of the wettest places on Earth, famous for its unique natural beauty.
– Visit the gorgeous Elephant Falls – a must-see natural attraction.
– Explore the Mawsmai Caves, known for their limestone formations.
– Get a talk in Mawphlang Sacred grove, a forest protected by indigenous Khasi Tribe for over 800 years.
– Arrive in Cherrapunji by evening and unwind at your resort.
– Meals: Breakfast
Accommodation: Cherra Cafe or similar

itinerary.title: Trek to the Living Root Bridges
itinerary.description:
A Bucket-list Experience
– Start early for an unforgettable trek to the iconic Living Root Bridges, with a packed breakfast.
– The moderate hike leads you through local villages and lush green landscapes.
– Discover the stunning Double Decker Root Bridge, a natural marvel made from braided tree roots.
– The trek is challenging but absolutely worth it – a must-do for adventure-loving women travelers.
– Meals: Breakfast
Accommodation: Cherra Cafe or similar

itinerary.title: Explore Mawlynnong (80 kms / 3-4hrs)
itinerary.description:
Cleanest Village in Asia
– After breakfast, start your day trip to Mawlynnong Village (approx. 3–4 hours), a shining example of community-led cleanliness and sustainable tourism.
– Discover the charm of this peaceful East Khasi Hills village, known for its warm hospitality.
– Enjoy a cozy stay in a simple yet super-clean village home.
– Meals: Breakfast and dinner Accommodation: Village Homestay.

itinerary.title: Visit Dawki River
itinerary.description:
Transfer to Shillong
– Wake up to a serene Mawlynnong morning and begin your drive to Shillong.
– En route, stop at Dawki River, one of India’s cleanest and most transparent rivers.
– Optional: Enjoy a boat ride (at your own cost) and admire the crystal-clear waters where you can see the riverbed!
– Arrive in Shillong and settle into your hotel.
– Meals: Breakfast
Accommodation: Shillong Centre Point or similar

itinerary.title: Departure from Guwahati Airport
itinerary.description:
Bid Adieu
– Enjoy a relaxed breakfast and reflect on your amazing week of connection, culture, and adventure.
– Group airport drop-off at Guwahati Airport (please book flights after 2pm only).
– Meals: Breakfast
END OF TOUR

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL
itinerary.description:
KATHMANDU
Arrival & transfer — meet our representative on arrival and transfer to your hotel. Kathmandu, Nepal’s vibrant capital, blends ancient heritage with modern energy — a city of sacred temples, royal palaces and lively markets, from the holy banks of Pashupatinath to the iconic stupas of Swayambhunath and Bouddhanath.
Rest of the day free at your own leisure.
Overnight stay at Hotel Lo Mustang in Kathmandu

itinerary.title: KATHMANDU
itinerary.description:
SIGHTSEEING
After breakfast, enjoy sightseeing tour.
Patan Durbar Square A UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece of Newari architecture, packed with intricately carved palaces, temples and courtyards from the Malla dynasty — don’t miss the stone Krishna Mandir, crowned with 21 golden spires.
Swayambhunath Stupa One of Nepal’s oldest sacred sites, over 2,000 years old, perched on a hilltop with Buddha’s all-seeing eyes gazing over the valley. Nicknamed the “Monkey Temple,” it rewards visitors with sweeping panoramic views.
Kathmandu Durbar Square The historic royal heart of the city, with palaces and temples spanning the Malla and Shah dynasties — including Hanuman Dhoka and the Kal Bhairav statue — still alive with daily rituals and traditional markets.
Overnight stay at Hotel Lo Mustang in Kathmandu

itinerary.title: FLIGHT TO POKHRA
itinerary.description:
BOATING ON PHEWA LAKE
Fly to Pokhara
Boating on Phewa Lake Glide across the iconic lake with the Annapurna and Machha puchhre (Fishtail) ranges reflected in its calm waters, including a stop at Tal Barahi Temple on its small island.
Free time at Lakeside Wander the lively Lakeside promenade, lined with handicraft shops and cozy cafés — best enjoyed at sunset, when golden light spreads across the water.
Overnight stay at Temple Himalaya in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: POKHRA
itinerary.description:
EXPLORING POKHARA
Sunrise at Sarangkot A n early hilltop excursion for one of Nepal’s most spectacular sunrise views over the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre ranges, framed by terraced fields and village life.
Devi’s Fall & Gupteshwor Cave Watch a mountain stream thunder into a hidden canyon at Devi’s Fall, then descend into the sacred cave next door, home to a shrine to Lord Shiva and a glimpse of the waterfall from within.
Pumdikot Shiva Statue A grand hilltop statue of Lord Shiva with panoramic views over Phewa Lake and the Annapurna range — a popular spot for photography and quiet reflection.
Overnight stay at Temple Himalaya in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: FLIGHT BACK TO KATHMANDU
itinerary.description:
NAGARKOT
Fly back to Kathmandu
Pashupatinath Temple Nepal’s holiest Hindu temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, on the sacred banks of the Bagmati River — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with gilded roofs, ancient rituals and resident sadhus (holy men).
Drive to Nagarkot A peaceful hill station famous for sweeping Himalayan panoramas — on a clear day, spot eight of Nepal’s thirteen Himalayan ranges, including a distant glimpse of Everest.
Overnight stay at Temple Himalaya in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: DEPARTURE
itinerary.description:
HUGS & GOODBYES!
Himalayan sunrise Weather permitting A last early-morning look at the Himalaya from Nagarkot before heading out.
Bhaktapur Durbar Square A beautifully preserved showcase of Newar architecture, home to the 55-Window Palace, the Golden Gate and the towering five-tiered Nyatapola Temple — brick-paved lanes and centuries-old traditions still very much alive.
Transfer to Kathmandu Airport for departure.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Osaka
Land at Kansai Airport, where our coach will be waiting to take you to the hotel in Osaka. Check in (from 3 pm), drop your bags and let it sink in:
Konnichiwa Japan has officially begun.
🇯🇵
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Land. Bow a little. Look around. We’re in Japan.
The rest of the day is deliberately easy. Freshen up, take a walk around the neighbourhood, try something from a convenience store (trust us, it’s a Japanese experience on its own) or simply recover from the journey.
💡 WHY TODAY IS EASY
Because tomorrow Japan starts showing off. Today, you just need to arrive properly.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Holiday Inn & Suites Shin Osaka (4★) or similar, Osaka

itinerary.title: Osaka
itinerary.description:
World Heritage at Nara Deer Park
After breakfast we head to Nara, where hundreds of friendly deer roam free in Nara Deer Park and the giant Buddha waits inside Todai-ji Temple, one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Bow to a deer. Get bowed back to. Repeat.
Back in Osaka, we stop for photos at Osaka Castle before free time in Shinsaibashi and Dotonbori, Osaka’s glowing food and shopping district. Lunch and dinner are on your own, and this is the city to do it in: takoyaki, okonomiyaki and whatever smells best.
💡 TIP FOR TODAY
Nara’s deer bow when you bow to them, but they also know exactly where you keep the deer crackers. Hold them up high.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Holiday Inn & Suites Shin Osaka (4★) or similar, Osaka

itinerary.title: Kyoto Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Tea ceremony After breakfast we check out of our Osaka hotel. Today is Kyoto, Japan’s old capital. We start at Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion shining over its pond, then walk through the tall, whispering Arashiyama Bamboo Grove.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Slow down. Sip slowly. Kyoto doesn’t rush.
In the afternoon we join a traditional tea ceremony in the Gion district, where every movement has meaning and the matcha is whisked just for you. Lunch and dinner are on your own, then we check in to our hotel in Kyoto.
💡 WHY KYOTO MATTERS
This is the Japan of temples, gardens and lanterns. A day here balances out the neon still to come.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Miyako Hotel Kyoto Hachijo (4★) or similar, Kyoto

itinerary.title: Transfer to Hakone
itinerary.description:
Japanese Bullet Train and Hakone Sightseeing
We check out after breakfast and board the Shinkansen, Japan’s famous bullet train, for the journey from Kyoto towards Hakone, the mountain and hot-spring region near Mount Fuji.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Board on time. Blink. You’re there.
After lunch at an Indian restaurant (on your own), we sail across Lake Ashi on the pirate-ship cruise, then ride the ropeway up to Owakudani, a volcanic valley where the ground literally steams. Tonight we stay near Fuji in Mishima.
💡 TIP FOR TODAY
Try a black egg at Owakudani. They’re boiled in the volcanic springs, and legend says each one adds seven years to your life.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Fujisan Mishima Tokyu Hotel (4★) or similar, Mishima (near Mt Fuji)

itinerary.title: Mt Fuji to Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Mt Fuji Viewing
After breakfast we check out and visit Oshino Hakkai, a village of crystal-clear spring ponds fed by snowmelt from Mount Fuji. On a clear day, Fuji-san stands right behind it.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Look for Fuji. Fill the shopping bag. Head for the big city.
Next it’s
Gotemba Premium Outlets for some shopping, then the coach takes us into Tokyo. Lunch and dinner are on your own, and we check into our Tokyo Bay hotel for the next three nights.
💡 GOOD TO KNOW
Fuji is famously shy and often hides in cloud. If she shows up, consider it a gift.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Oriental Hotel Tokyo Bay (4★) or similar, Tokyo

itinerary.title: Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Tokyo Tour
A full day in Tokyo. We start with a photo stop at Tokyo Skytree, then walk through Senso-ji Temple and the snack-and-souvenir stalls of Nakamise Street in Asakusa.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Temples in the morning. Neon by night. Sakura in between.
Then it’s
Akihabara for electronics and anime, followed by Yoyogi Park and the Meguro River, two of Tokyo’s favourite places to see the cherry blossoms in early April. We finish with free time for shopping in Shinjuku. Lunch and dinner are on your own.
💡 WHY TODAY IS FULL
Tokyo is huge, and this is the day we see as much of it as we can. Tomorrow is all yours.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Oriental Hotel Tokyo Bay (4★) or similar, Tokyo

itinerary.title: Explore Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Free Day
Today is completely free, with no coach and no schedule. Sleep in, go back to the place you loved yesterday or explore a new corner of Tokyo at your own pace.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Your city. Your pace. Your Tokyo.
Maybe Harajuku and Shibuya Crossing, a museum, a sushi breakfast, more sakura or a day trip of your own. Your Jugni trip leader is happy to help with ideas and directions.
💡 WHY A FREE DAY
The best travel memories often come from the hours nobody planned. We leave room for yours.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Oriental Hotel Tokyo Bay (4★) or similar, Tokyo
The hotel is in Shin-Urayasu, about 30–45 minutes by train from central Tokyo, so plan your day out with travel time in mind.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.description:
Transfer to Tokyo Airport
After breakfast we check out and head to the airport for our flights home, bags full of souvenirs and phones full of cherry blossoms.
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Pack. Hug. Promise to come back.
Strangers on Day 1, travel sisters by Day 8.
Konnichiwa Japan ends here, but the group chat definitely doesn’t.
💡 UNTIL NEXT TIME
Sayonara means goodbye, but in Japan it’s often said with the hope of meeting again.
✈️ DEPARTURE
Check-out after breakfast, then a group transfer to Tokyo airport for flights home.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Srinagar
itinerary.description:
Shikara ride Land in Srinagar, settle into our base for the next few days, and ease into the city with a Shikara ride on Dal Lake as the sun goes down. The evening ends with a group dinner — first introductions, first stories. 🛶
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Land. Glide across Dal Lake. Meet your Kashmir family.
Flight timings are coordinated with the team in advance, so your airport transfer is ready the moment you land.
💡 WHY TODAY IS GENTLE
Because a Shikara ride at sunset is the softest possible introduction to Kashmir — no rush, just water, light and the Himalayas in the distance.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Ramada Incore Rajbagh, Srinagar (or similar)

itinerary.title: Srinagar - Gulmarg
itinerary.description:
Gulmarg
We drive up to Gulmarg, the “meadow of flowers,” for walks through alpine meadows with the Himalayas as a backdrop. St. Mary’s Church and the Gulmarg Golf Course are optional stops, weather permitting. 🏔️
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Mountain air, meadow walks, and views that don’t need a filter.
Gulmarg’s weather can shift quickly, so today’s plan stays flexible — the mountains set the pace, not the itinerary.
💡 WHY TODAY IS A CHANGE OF SCENE
Because Gulmarg’s altitude and meadows are a different Kashmir entirely — we leave the lake behind for the mountains before heading back down tomorrow.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Hilltop Gulmarg (or similar)

itinerary.title: Drive to Srinagar
itinerary.description:
Gandola Ride
An early Gulmarg Gondola ride lifts us into the Himalayas for views you’ll be talking about for years. Optional paid skiing is available before we drive back to Srinagar for a Wazwan feast. 🚠
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Above the clouds this morning, feasting on Wazwan by night.
The gondola is one of the highest cable cars in the world — we go early, before the lines build up and the light is at its best.
💡 WHY TODAY IS THE BIG MOMENT
Because the gondola is Gulmarg’s signature experience — and ending the day with a traditional Wazwan meal makes the comedown just as memorable.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Ramada Incore Rajbagh, Srinagar (or similar)

itinerary.title: Srinagar
itinerary.description:
Tulip Gardens & Markets
The day Kashmir shows off its colour — the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden (bloom permitting), the Mughal Gardens, and local markets for handicrafts and Pashmina shawls. 🌷
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
This is the day the whole trip is named after.
Tulip bloom timing is weather-dependent each year, but the Mughal Gardens and markets make today beautiful regardless.
💡 WHY TODAY IS THE HEADLINE
Because this is literally the Kashmir Tulip Festival — we build the whole trip around catching the gardens at their most colourful.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Ramada Incore Rajbagh, Srinagar (or similar)

itinerary.title: Day Trip to Sonmarg
itinerary.description:
Meadows and Tunnels
We drive past the Sind River and through the Z-Morh Tunnel to the meadows of Sonamarg
— “the meadow of gold.” An optional pony ride towards Thajiwas Glacier is available before we head back to Srinagar in the evening. 🐎
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Glacier views, golden meadows, one last mountain escape.
It’s a full day out and back, so we return to Srinagar in the evening — tired, happy, and ready to pack.
💡 WHY TODAY IS THE LAST ADVENTURE
Because Sonamarg’s glacier views are worth the drive — and it’s the perfect last big day before tomorrow’s quieter departure.
🏨 TONIGHT’S STAY
Ramada Incore Rajbagh, Srinagar (or similar)

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.description:
Bid Adieu
Breakfast, then a group transfer to Srinagar Airport. The suitcases are heavier with Pashmina and saffron, but the real souvenirs are the tulip fields and the women who shared this journey. ✈️
✨ TODAY’S MOOD
Goodbye, Kashmir. See you in another bloom season.
Six days, one unforgettable colour palette — thank you for trusting us with this journey.
💡 FROM TEAM JUGNI
We don’t take it lightly that you chose to spend this trip with us — safe travels home.
✈️ DEPARTURE
Journey home

itinerary.title: ACCLIMATISATION DAY
itinerary.description:
Arrival at Leh Airport (Transfer to hotel)
– Reach Leh Airport and enjoy your women only tour package to Ladakh & Turtuk
– Transfer to the hotel and check-in (15 mins travel)
– Take the day to rest and get acclimatised to the place – Since you are reaching an altitude of 4000mtrs approx from 200mtrs in just one hour’s time, you may be excited and would want to explore everything very first day. However your body needs to get acclimatized to such height and climate. We sincerely suggest that you rest on the first day for body acclimatization.
– Enjoy a group dinner and break the ice – Accommodation: Hotel Gyalpo Residency or similar class

itinerary.title: LOCAL SIGHTSEEING
itinerary.description:
Magnetic Hill
– Finish breakfast and leave for the day – After breakfast start our sightseeing with Hall Of Fame (Museum Constructed by India Army) near Leh
– Proceed further to Gurudwara Patthar Sahib at an altitude of 3600 Mtrs about 22 Kms from Leh (it was constructed in memory of Guru Nanak Dev ji) nestled deep in the Himalayas
– A drive of another 4 km took us to Magnetic Hill which defies the law of gravity. As you move ahead from Magnetic Hills, just before Nimmu town there comes a famous Confluence Of Two Rivers Indus River coming from Tibet (left) and Zanskar River coming from Zanskar Valley (right)
– In the evening we will visit shanty stupa – Accommodation: Hotel Gyalpo Residency or similar class

itinerary.title: KHARDUNGLA & NUBRA
itinerary.description:
Nubra Valley
– Finish an early breakfast and leave for the day – Early morning we will drive to Nubra valley, driving over the highest motored pass in the world. The exciting journey through serpentine roads leads us to the Khardungla Pass at an awesome height of 5550 meters.
– We stop at the pass to admire and click some photographs of the fantastic view, before driving down into the Nubra valley. The valley is situated on an old caravan route at the confluence of the Shyok and the Nubra rivers.
– We will drive to our fixed camp resort and later drive to visit the charming valley of Deskit – the tiny capital of Nubra. The capital is marked by a single file of shops that are put up on the main road.
– We will visit the Deskit Gompa, perched on a rocky spur above the village, with a commanding view of the entire valley.
– From Deskit we will drive to Hunder past an area of sand dunes and get acquainted with the famous Bactrian camels. This small population of shaggy double-humped animals, which in the old days, were used as pack animals on the Central Asian trade routes are now used as riding animals in the high deserts. In the late afternoon we will drive to the Hotel
– Accommodation: Hunder Resort or similar class

itinerary.title: NUBRA & TURTUK VILLAGE
itinerary.description:
Turtuk village walk – After a good breakfast, we drive to the village of Turtuk, where we will be spending a day – The day will be spent exploring the twin villages of Farol and Youl. Farol is perched on a plateau higher up while Youl is settled near the stream below. Both have their own mosques and both sides are quite distinct in their own way – In Farol, live the wafiBaltis and in Youl live the Nurbak or Sunni Baltis, primarily. I Farol has a Gompa (Buddhist monastery). Youl has one old mosque dated, 1690. And both sides keep asking, which one you like better – Youl or Farol – come join the women only tour package to Ladakh & Turtuk and make your choice!
– The village has its own irrigation system where glacial melt water is channeled throughout the village in an elaborate series of channels. A use for everything is found – flattened barrels are used as doors for closing the household courtyards.
– The village falls within the Karakoram Range, K2 being the highest peak, only 100 odd kilometers down the road.
– Accommodation: Hunder Resort or similar class

Nubra and Leh Nubra
– Finish breakfast and leave for the day – Roadtrip to Leh
– Soak in the views and live your ‘khwaabo ke parinde’ dreams – Accommodation: Hotel Gyalpo Residency or similar

We also explore the Museum of Himachal Culture and Folk Art, showcasing traditional artifacts, costumes, and the rich local heritage.

Arrive at Falna Railway Station at approximately 10:40 AM and transfer towards Jawai stay.
Afternoon
Check in at the hotel.
Freshen up and enjoy a delicious lunch.
Relax and recharge before the evening’s wildlife adventure.
Evening – Jawai Leopard & Adventure Jungle Safari
Experience the wild beauty of Jawai on an exciting evening safari in an open gypsy.
Safari Highlights: Jawai Hills Adventure Ride
– Enjoy an adventurous ride through Jawai’s spectacular rocky terrain.
Leopard Safari
– Explore leopard territory and look for the magnificent Indian leopard in its natural habitat.
Jawai Dam Visit
– Discover the beautiful surroundings of Jawai Dam.
Backside Dam & Crocodile Point
– Visit the crocodile habitat and enjoy the scenic wilderness.
Sunset Point
– End your adventure with breathtaking sunset views over the Jawai landscape.
Wildlife & Bird Watching
– Spot local wildlife and beautiful bird species along the way.
An unforgettable evening filled with thrilling off-road adventures, leopard tracking, scenic landscapes and the magic of Jawai’s wilderness!
Note: Leopard and other wildlife sightings depend on natural conditions and cannot be guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Jawai → Ranakpur → Kumbhalgarh

Enjoy breakfast at your Jawai stay, check out and depart for Kumbhalgarh.
En route, stop at Ranakpur for a visit to the magnificent Ranakpur Shwetambar Jain Derasar Teerth.
Explore the temple’s intricate marble architecture, beautifully carved pillars and peaceful surroundings.
After the visit, continue your journey towards Kumbhalgarh.
Afternoon – Arrival at Kumbhalgarh
Arrive at your Kumbhalgarh stay and complete the check-in formalities.
Enjoy a relaxed lunch at the property and spend some time resting and soaking in the beautiful natural surroundings.
Evening – Explore Kumbhalgarh Fort
Later, head out to explore the magnificent Kumbhalgarh Fort, famously known for its massive fortification walls, often referred to as the Great Wall of India.
Learn about its historical association with the birthplace of the legendary Maharana Pratap.
Enjoy breathtaking views of the surrounding Aravalli hills and lush landscapes.
Nature & Birdwatching Experience
Enjoy birdwatching in the surrounding natural habitats.
Late Evening – Return to Stay
Enjoy a relaxed evening, dinner and overnight stay at Kumbhalgarh.

itinerary.title: Departure from Mumbai – Begin the Bhakti Yatra

itinerary.title: Discover the Essence of Mathura & Gokul
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Mathura Jn – MTJ by 08:18 AM in the morning and transfer to your hotel in Vrindavan.
After breakfast and freshening up, begin your journey with a visit to Shri Krishna Janmabhumi, the sacred birthplace of Lord Krishna.
Visit
Nand Bhavan, Krishna’s childhood home, followed by quiet reflection at Raman Reti, the sands where Krishna played.
By evening, seek blessings at the Dwarkadhish Temple, enjoy a tranquil boat ride on the Yamuna, and witness the magical Yamuna Aarti at sunset.

Participate in the 21 km Govardhan Parikrama by Vehicle, a spiritually rewarding walk around the holy hill.
After lunch, head towards Barsana, the birthplace of Radha Rani.
Optional: Take part in the Barsana Parikrama, soaking in the spiritual atmosphere of the village.

Explore other nearby ancient temples including:
Radha Vallabh Temple
Radha Damodar Temple
Seva Kunj
– where Radha-Krishna’s Raas Leela is believed to have taken place Gopeshwar Mahadev Temple
– where Lord Shiva became a Gopi to join the Raas
Visit the serene ISKCON Vrindavan Temple to experience spiritual calm and devotion.
Enjoy a hearty lunch, pick up devotional souvenirs, and capture some last moments of this divine town.
Transfer to Mathura Railway Station and board the return train to Mumbai in BDTS GARIBRATH (12910)

itinerary.title: Explore Hampi – Major Heritage Sites
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, we head towards the heritage side of Hampi to explore its ancient marvels and rich architectural legacy. Our morning begins with visits to Kadle Kal Ganesh , Krishna Temple , Badavilinga, and the awe-inspiring Narasimha Temple, each site narrating stories from centuries past and showcasing the artistic grandeur of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Post lunch, we continue our exploration with visits to Queen’s Bath , Pushkarani , Hazara Rama Temple , and the iconic Stone Chariot at Vitthal Temple. We’ll also admire the intricate beauty of Lotus Mahal and the majestic Elephant Stables, followed by a stroll through the lively Hampi Bazaar and scenic Hemakuta Hills, offering glimpses into the daily life and royal elegance of the bygone era.
As the day winds down, we visit the sacred Virupaksha Temple, one of Hampi’s most revered sites. The day concludes with a mesmerizing sunset at Malyavanta Raghunatha Temple, painting the boulder-strewn landscape in golden hues. After soaking in the tranquil evening views, we return to our stay to relax and unwind.
Hotel Stay
Breakfast + Lunch

itinerary.title: Sunrise | Anjanadri Temple | Adventure | Checkout

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Ranachatti
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Dehradun → Ranachatti (~160 km, 6–7 hrs) | Altitude: 2,134 m (7,000 ft) | Stay: Homestay / guesthouse, Ranachatti
Day 1 is a travel day. You leave Dehradun in the morning and drive through Mussoorie and Naugaon, then up the Yamuna valley past Barkot. For much of the way the road follows the Yamuna River, with terraced villages on the slopes above. There is a lunch stop on the way. Barkot is the last place with an ATM, 1–1.5 hours before Ranachatti, so we recommend carrying the cash you need from Dehradun.
Ranachatti is a village on the road to Yamunotri, at about 2,134 m. It is known for its wood-carved Someshwar Mahadev temple, one of the finest examples of traditional carving in the valley. In the evening, walk through the village and visit the temple.
You stay in a homestay or guesthouse. Your trek leader holds a briefing and checks documents. Airtel and Jio work at Ranachatti, but there is little or no network on the trail after today. Tell your family you will be out of reach for the next three days.
What to Expect: Drive via Mussoorie, Naugaon and Barkot along the Yamuna River
Terraced villages on the slopes of the Yamuna valley The wood-carved Someshwar Mahadev temple in Ranachatti
Evening briefing and document check Last ATM at Barkot; little or no network beyond Ranachatti
Overnight: Ranachatti (2,134 m / 7,000 ft)

itinerary.title: Ranachatti to Bamsingh
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 2,134 m → 2,804 m (9,200 ft) | Distance: 4 km | Duration: 3–4 hrs | Terrain: terraced fields, then oak and rhododendron forest, with one steep and rocky stretch | Stay: Tents at Bamsingh
The trek begins right from the village. You walk out of Ranachatti on a path through terraced fields, and within a short while the fields give way to a forest of oak and rhododendron. The village sounds fade behind you as the trees close in. On paper this is a short day, 4 km and 3–4 hours, but the trail gains height for most of the way. Find an easy rhythm early and keep it.
Along the way you pass chhanis, the shepherd huts where local herders stay with their animals in the grazing season. There are streams on this lower part of the trail, but ask your trek leader before you refill your bottle from one. Lunch is packed and eaten on the trail, so you can stop wherever the group finds a good spot.
One stretch of the trail is steep and rocky. This is the part of the day to take slowly. Shorten your step, use your trekking poles for balance and place your feet on firm ground rather than loose stones. Near the top of the climb stands a large tree known locally as the Coin Tree'. It marks your first view towards the Dinnala meadows above, where you camp tomorrow.
Bamsingh, at about 2,804 m, is a forest clearing and your first campsite. You arrive early, and hot tea and snacks are waiting. The short day is deliberate. The free afternoon helps your body adjust to the height, so use it to rest, not to rush around. Dinner is served early in the dining tent. In the evening your trek leader checks everyone's oxygen level and pulse, a routine that continues every day of the trek. Forest nights are cool in summer and freezing in winter, so keep your thermals and woollen cap ready before the sun goes down.
What to Expect: Terraced fields above Ranachatti, then oak and rhododendron forest Chhanis (shepherd huts) used by local herders in the grazing season One steep, rocky

itinerary.title: Bamsingh to Dinnala Meadow
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 2,804 m → 3,277 m (10,750 ft) | Distance: 4 km | Duration: 4 hrs | Terrain: short drop to a stream crossing, then about an hour of steep forest climbing onto open meadow | Stay: Tents at Dinnala Bugyal
Do not be fooled by the distance. Today is only 4 km, but it holds the steepest climb of the trek so far. From Bamsingh the trail first drops a little to a stream crossing at Daloti Gad. This short downhill is a gentle start before the work begins. Cross where your trek leader shows you and take it one step at a time.
After the crossing comes the hardest part of the day: about an hour of steep climbing through the forest. Walk in a line behind your trek leader and keep a gap from the person in front. Step on solid ground rather than loose stones. Go slowly and take short breaks. In our experience, short and frequent pauses work far better on this climb than long stops.
Above the climb, the forest suddenly opens onto the wide Dinnala Bugyal (meadow), at about 3,277 m. After an hour inside the trees, the open sky feels very wide. This is one of the finest campsites on the trek. Bandarpoonch and Swargarohini rise to the north, and you can see across to Kedarkantha and Phulara Ridge. In summer the meadow is green and open. In winter it is under snow, and the camp is very cold at night.
Water is scarce at Dinnala. The team carries and manages it carefully and boils or treats what you drink, so please use it sparingly. Spend the afternoon resting and taking in the views. Whatever the season, the sunset over Bandarpoonch from here is one of the most memorable sights of the trek. In the evening your trek leader briefs the group on tomorrow's summit climb and checks everyone's oxygen levels. Fill your bottles at camp before you sleep, ready for the dry summit day. Eat a full dinner and go to sleep early. Summit day starts before sunrise.
What to Expect: Short drop to the stream crossing at Daloti Gad
About an hour of steep climbing through the forest,

itinerary.title: Summit Day - Dinnala to Aancha Camp via Aancha Top
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,277 m → 3,818 m (12,525 ft) → 3,475 m | Distance: 8 km | Duration: 6–7 hrs | Terrain: upper meadows, rhododendron patches and three small glacial lakes, then a narrow, rocky ridge | Stay: Tents at Aancha camp This is the longest and hardest day of the trek. The effort comes from two things: the length, about 8 km and 6–7 hours, and the ridge near the top. You start before sunrise, after a light breakfast. There is no water on the route today, so fill at least two litres from camp before you leave.
The trail first crosses the upper meadows and patches of rhododendron. Then it passes three small glacial lakes, still and clear on calm mornings. This part of the walk is open, and you can take it at an easy pace. Save your energy for the ridge above. In winter the summit ridge can be under deep snow, and every step takes longer.
The final climb to Aancha Top follows a ridge, and this is the section to respect. A few stretches are narrow, rocky and exposed, with loose stones underfoot. Your trek leader guides each step. Keep your hands free; if your trek leader asks, put your poles away on the rocky sections. In snow, we use microspikes and gaiters. Walk with a gap from the person in front so no one is crowded on the narrow parts. Move carefully, test each foothold and do not rush. The same care applies on the way down from the top, because the loose stones are just as loose in descent.
From the summit, at 3,818 m (12,525 ft), the view opens in every direction. Bandarpoonch and Kala Nag rise close by. Further away stand Swargarohini, the Gangotri group, and Srikanth and Jaonli. To the east you can see across to the Dayara and Gidara meadows. Take your time at the top. After that, you descend to the Aancha campsite at about 3,475 m, your last camp of the trek. Your trek leader runs the usual evening oxygen and pulse check, and an early night is well earned.
What to Expect: Start before sunrise; carry at least 2 litres, as there is no water on the

itinerary.title: Aancha Camp to Ranachatti
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,475 m → 2,134 m (7,000 ft) | Distance: 6 km | Duration: 5 hrs | Terrain: open meadows, then a long descent through pine, silver birch and oak forest, steep in places | Stay: Homestay / guesthouse, Ranachatti
This is your last day on the trail, and nearly all of it runs downhill. After breakfast the trail crosses open meadows and passes the clearing of Pokhari Thathar. The meadows are open at first, a gentle way to start the day. On clear mornings the summit ridge stands out behind you. It is a good moment to stop, turn around and look back on the route you have walked over the last three days.
Below the meadows, the trail drops steeply through pine, silver birch and oak forest back towards the valley. The descent is long and steep in places, so walk carefully and use your trekking poles. Shorten your step, keep your knees soft and let the poles take some of the load. Downhill is where tired legs make mistakes, so take a short break whenever your knees start to feel it. The forests here are full of birdsong. The trail passes a few shepherd huts and small clearings on the way down, where you may meet herders with their animals.
As you get lower, the sounds of the village and the river below grow louder. This is where attention tends to drop. Take care on the last steep section into the village. Many slips happen when people relax at the end, so keep the same slow, careful pace until you are on the flat ground of the village.
You reach Ranachatti by early afternoon. After three nights in tents, the hot water at the homestay is very welcome, and lunch follows the shower. The rest of the day is free. If you did not see the Someshwar Mahadev temple on Day 1, this is your chance; otherwise, simply rest. In the evening, the group celebrates the summit together. It is your last night in the valley before the drive home.
What to Expect: Open meadows and the clearing of Pokhari Thathar
Views back to the summit ridge on clear mornings Long, steep desc

itinerary.title: Ranachatti to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Ranachatti → Dehradun (~160 km, 6–7 hrs) | Altitude: 2,134 m → 640 m | Stay: Trip ends in Dehradun
This is a travel day. After breakfast you drive back down the Yamuna valley, through Barkot, Naugaon and Mussoorie to Dehradun. The drive takes about 6–7 hours with short stops. It is the same road you came up on Day 1, with the Yamuna River beside you for much of the way and terraced villages on the slopes above. With the trek behind you, it is a quieter ride to watch the valley go by.
Barkot is a good place to withdraw cash or pick up snacks on the way back. Keep water and a snack in your daypack as well, since the stops on the way are short.
You reach Dehradun in the late afternoon or evening. Please book your onward travel for the late night or the next day. Mountain roads can be slow, and a little margin keeps your train or flight safe. The trip ends on arrival in Dehradun.
What to Expect: Return drive down the Yamuna valley via Barkot, Naugaon and Mussoorie
About 6–7 hours on the road with short stops Barkot for cash and snacks on the way back Arrival in Dehradun in the late afternoon or evening Onward travel best booked for the late night or the next day Trek ends at Ranachatti on Day 5; drop at Dehradun Railway Station
How To Reach
By Air
By Train
By Bus
Nearest airport: Jolly Grant Airport (DED), Dehradun – about 25 km / 45–60 min from Dehradun city, with direct flights from Delhi and other metros. The cab to Ranachatti leaves Dehradun Railway Station at 6:30 AM, so fly in the day before and stay the night in Dehradun.
From Dehradun to Ranachatti:
about 160 km via Mussoorie, Naugaon and Barkot, 6–7 hrs by road. Transport is not included in the trek fee: we help the group book shared cabs, paid directly to the driver and split among trekkers. The cab costs about ₹6,500 one way per 5–6 seat vehicle. The cab leaves Dehradun Railway Station at 6:30 AM.
Return: On Day 6 a shared cab (not included in the trek fee) takes you from Ranachatti to D

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Lohajung
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Rishikesh → Lohajung (about 250 km, 8–10 hrs) | Altitude: 2,316 m (7,600 ft) | Stay: Guesthouse / homestay (triple or quad sharing)
The Ali Bedni Bugyal trek starts with a full day on the road. Set off from Rishikesh early, around 6:30 AM, and you reach Lohajung by evening without pressure. Transport is not included in the trek fee: we help the group book shared cabs, paid directly to the driver and split among trekkers. The cab leaves Jumping Heights, Tapovan at 6:30 AM.
The hill road runs via Devprayag, Srinagar, Rudraprayag, Gauchar, Karnaprayag, Tharali and Dewal, through forest, river valleys and remote Garhwal villages with terraced fields. Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Karnaprayag are three of the Panch Prayags, the holy confluences on the Alaknanda. Stop at Devprayag if you can; this is where the Alaknanda and the Bhagirathi join to form the Ganga.
Lohajung, at 2,316 m, is the base camp for Ali Bedni Bugyal, Roopkund and Brahmatal. You stay in a guesthouse or homestay, and dinner is served in the evening. The shops here are few and basic, so bring your trekking essentials with you. Withdraw cash at Dewal, the last reliable ATM, and make your calls at Lohajung, the last place with a stable mobile signal.
What to Expect: Early start from Rishikesh, around 6:30 AM
About 250 km hill drive past three of the Panch Prayags
Recommended halt at Devprayag, where the Ganga is formed Dewal: last reliable ATM; Lohajung: last stable mobile network Carry your essentials – Lohajung has only a few small shops Overnight: Lohajung guesthouse / homestay (2,316 m / 7,600 ft)

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Wan, then Trek to Ghairoli Patal
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Lohajung → Wan (15 km, ~1 hr) | Altitude: 2,438 m → 3,205 m (10,515 ft) | Distance: 6 km | Duration: 4–5 hrs | Terrain: steady climb to Ranka Dhar, then oak and rhododendron forest along the Neel Ganga | Stay: Tents at Ghairoli Patal
The morning begins with a 15 km drive from Lohajung to Wan, about an hour. Wan is the starting point of the trek and one of the largest villages in Chamoli. From here you walk 6 km to Ghairoli Patal, gaining about 767 m (2,515 ft) in 4 to 5 hours. It is a steady climb rather than a steep one, and the right way to walk it is slowly.
The first couple of kilometres climb steadily to Ranka Dhar, the ridge above Wan village, where the views open up for the first time. Pause here to catch your breath. The trail then continues into dense oak and rhododendron forest, full of diverse flora and fauna, and follows the lively Neel Ganga River, which you cross on wooden bridges.
The river is a good place for a short rest. In camp, drinking water is boiled or treated with chlorine tablets, and on the trail your trek leader or guide will tell you where to refill your bottle. Keep sipping through the day; steady hydration is the simplest help you can give your body at altitude.
By late afternoon you reach Ghairoli Patal at 3,205 m, a peaceful clearing in the forest surrounded by tall deodars. This is your first night in tents, and the trees keep the camp calm and quiet. Settle in, add a warm layer as the light fades and rest well. Tomorrow the forest opens onto the meadows.
What to Expect: 1-hour drive from Lohajung to Wan, the trailhead Steady climb to Ranka Dhar ridge above Wan village Oak and rhododendron forest along the Neel Ganga, with wooden bridge crossings 6 km and about 767 m (2,515 ft) of gain – an easy pace works best Ask your trek leader where to refill water; camp water is boiled or treated Overnight: Tents at Ghairoli Patal (3,205 m / 10,515 ft)

itinerary.title: Ghairoli Patal to Abin Kharak via Ali Bugyal
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,205 m → 3,450 m (Ali Bugyal ridge) → 3,410 m (11,185 ft) | Distance: 4 km | Duration: ~3 hrs | Terrain: steep stone-stepped forest climb, then open alpine meadow | Stay: Tents at Abin Kharak
Today is short, but it starts with work. For the first 30 minutes the trail climbs steeply out of Ghairoli Patal over stone-paved steps, through dense oak and rhododendron forest. Take it slowly. Short steps and a steady rhythm on the stones keep your breathing under control, and the steep part is over in about half an hour.
Then the forest clears and Ali Bugyal opens in front of you, a vast spread of alpine grassland running away in every direction. It is known as Asia's largest alpine meadow, and the change from closed forest to open sky is sudden. The gradient eases at once. You walk across gentle slopes dotted with wildflowers and colourful blooms, with a cool Himalayan breeze and wide mountain views on every side.
The climb continues gently to the ridge of Ali Bugyal at 3,450 m (11,320 ft), the high point of the day. From the ridge the views of the surrounding mountains open wide. Stop here for a while. With only about 3 hours of walking today, there is no reason to rush, and time spent at this height helps your body adjust for tomorrow's climb to Bedni Bugyal Top.
From the ridge it is less than a kilometre to Abin Kharak at 3,410 m, your campsite for the night. The camp sits among sweeping meadows, and because the day is short you arrive with plenty of daylight left. Use the afternoon to rest, drink water and enjoy the open space around you. On a clear night the sky over the meadows fills with stars.
What to Expect: 30-minute steep climb on stone steps through oak and rhododendron forest The forest opens suddenly onto Ali Bugyal, a vast alpine meadow Gentle meadow walking with wildflowers in season and wide Himalayan views Ridge of Ali Bugyal (3,450 m / 11,320 ft): the high point of the day Short 4 km day of about 3 hours – plenty of time to rest

itinerary.title: Abin Kharak to Ghairoli Patal via Bedni Bugyal Top
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,410 m → 3,658 m (12,000 ft) → 3,205 m (10,515 ft) | Distance: 5 km | Duration: ~4 hrs | Terrain: rolling meadow, moderate climb to Bedni Top, gradual descent into forest | Stay: Tents at Ghairoli Patal
This is the summit day of the trek, and a gentle one. From Abin Kharak the trail crosses the rolling green meadows of Ali and enters Bedni Bugyal, considered among the finest alpine meadows in Uttarakhand. The climb is moderate, about 248 m (815 ft) in all, and the grass underfoot makes for easy walking. Keep a steady pace and enjoy the open country.
Bedni Bugyal Top at 3,658 m (12,000 ft) is the highest point of the trek. On a clear day the big peaks stand in a line in front of you: Trishul (7,120 m), Nanda Ghunti, Chaukhambha and Neelkanth. Spend time here. This wide view across the meadows to the snow peaks is the one the trek is known for.
Close by is Bedni Kund, also called Vaitarni Lake, a sacred lake where Mt Trishul reflects on the water. It is a halting point of the Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra, a ritual procession held once every 12 years, and the area is known for the rare Brahma Kamal flower. Walk around it quietly; it is a place of worship as well as a viewpoint.
From Bedni Bugyal the trail descends gradually towards the tree line, a drop of about 453 m (1,485 ft). Use your poles and keep your steps short on the way down. After a couple of hours you re-enter dense oak and rhododendron forest and reach Ghairoli Patal at 3,205 m by late afternoon. It is the same deodar-ringed clearing you camped in two nights ago, and its shelter feels welcome after the open meadows.
What to Expect: Rolling meadows of Ali and Bedni Bugyal, with a moderate climb of about 248 m (815 ft)
Bedni Bugyal Top (3,658 m / 12,000 ft): the highest point of the trek Views of Trishul (7,120 m), Nanda Ghunti, Chaukhambha and Neelkanth
Bedni Kund (Vaitarni Lake), with Mt Trishul reflected on its surface Gradual descent of about 453 m (1,485 ft) back into oak and rhod

itinerary.title: Ghairoli Patal to Wan, Drive to Lohajung
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,205 m → 2,438 m (8,000 ft) | Distance: 6 km | Duration: 4–5 hrs | Terrain: forest descent, steep drop to the Neel Ganga, gentle climb to Ranka Dhar, gradual descent to Wan | Drive: Wan → Lohajung (15 km, ~1 hr) | Stay: Guesthouse / hotel at Lohajung
The last trekking day retraces the route you climbed on Day 2. From Ghairoli Patal you descend through dense oak, pine and rhododendron forest, on a trail alive with birdsong and fresh mountain air. In all you lose about 767 m (2,515 ft) over 6 km, so keep your poles out and let your knees work gently.
After a few kilometres the path drops steeply towards the Neel Ganga. This is the steepest part of the day. Slow down, shorten your stride and place your feet carefully. At the bottom the river makes a good rest stop, and you can take your boots off and soak your feet in its icy water before the last stretch.
From the river the trail climbs gently to Ranka Dhar ridge, where you get a final look at the high Himalaya before the trek winds down. Then a gradual descent leads into Wan at 2,438 m, one of the largest villages in Chamoli. Your trek on foot ends here, and the warmth of the village is a fitting close to the walk.
A shared cab, paid directly to the driver, takes you on the short drive of about an hour back to Lohajung. You stay in a guesthouse or hotel on triple or quad sharing. Freshen up, rest your legs and celebrate finishing the trek. Dinner is served in the evening.
What to Expect: Forest descent through oak, pine and rhododendron, about 767 m (2,515 ft) of height loss Steep drop to the Neel Ganga – a good place to rest and cool your feet Gentle climb to Ranka Dhar ridge for last views of the high Himalaya
Wan village (2,438 m / 8,000 ft), one of the largest in Chamoli
15 km, 1-hour drive from Wan back to Lohajung
Overnight: Lohajung guesthouse / hotel (2,316 m / 7,600 ft)

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Rishikesh
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Lohajung → Rishikesh (about 250 km, 8–10 hrs) | Altitude: 2,316 m → 340 m (1,115 ft) | End: Rishikesh by evening The trek closes with the long drive back to Rishikesh. The road retraces the way you came, via Dewal, Tharali, Karnaprayag, Gauchar, Rudraprayag, Srinagar and Devprayag, through valleys, along riverbanks and past mountain towns. Over the day you descend about 1,976 m (6,485 ft). Transport is not included in the trek fee: we help the group book shared cabs, paid directly to the driver and split among trekkers.
We recommend a short stop at Devprayag to watch the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet and form the Ganga. After days in the meadows, it is a good last look at the rivers of these mountains.
The cab reaches Jumping Heights, Tapovan (Rishikesh) by about 6:00 PM. Meals during the drive are not part of the trek, so carry snacks or plan a roadside stop. Leave a margin before any onward train, bus or flight; this is a full day on the road.
What to Expect: About 250 km drive back to Rishikesh, 8–10 hours Route via Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag and Srinagar
Halt at Devprayag for the confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda
Shared cab from Lohajung, not included in the trek fee Meals in transit are your own Trek ends at Lohajung; drop at Rishikesh (340 m / 1,115 ft) by about 6:00 PM
How To Reach
By Air
By Train
By Bus
Nearest airport: Jolly Grant Airport (DED), Dehradun – about 20–25 km / around 45 min from Rishikesh, with direct flights from Delhi and other metros. The cab to Lohajung leaves Rishikesh at 6:30 AM, so fly in the day before and stay the night in Rishikesh.
From Rishikesh to Lohajung:
about 250 km, 8–10 hrs by road. Transport is not included in the trek fee: we help the group book shared cabs (about ₹6,500 one way per 5–6 seat vehicle), paid directly to the driver and split among trekkers. The cab leaves Jumping Heights, Tapovan (Rishikesh) at 6:30 AM.
Return: On Day 6 the shared cab (not included in the trek fee; about ₹6,500

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Dehradun → Sankri (200 km, 8–9 hrs) | Altitude: 1,950 m (6,400 ft) | Stay: Guesthouse / homestay (triple or quad sharing)
Day 1 is a full day on the road. Aim to reach Dehradun early so the drive can start by 6:30 to 7:00 AM; that gets you to Sankri comfortably before dark. Transport is not included in the trek fee: we help the group book shared cabs at ₹1,000 per person each way, paid directly to the driver. The cab leaves Dehradun Railway Station at 6:30 AM.
The 200 km route runs through Mussoorie, Damta, Naugaon, Purola, Mori and Naitwar. You pass green valleys, pine forest, terraced fields and rivers, with distant glimpses of snow peaks, and the road runs through the Govind National Park region. Purola is the last reliable ATM on the way, so withdraw the cash you need there.
Sankri sits at 1,950 m in the Uttarkashi district. It is the last roadhead for the trek, the gateway to the Govind Pashu Vihar National Park and Sanctuary, and the base for Bali Pass, Har Ki Dun and Kedarkantha. You stay in a guesthouse or homestay, and dinner is served in the evening. Sankri is also the last place with a stable mobile signal, and even here only Jio works consistently.
What to Expect: Early start from Dehradun (6:30–7:00 AM) to reach Sankri before dark 200 km drive via Mussoorie, Purola, Mori and Naitwar
Last reliable ATM at Purola
Last mobile signal at Sankri (only Jio works consistently)
Dinner and a night's rest at Sankri, the trek base Overnight: Sankri guesthouse / homestay (1,950 m / 6,400 ft)

itinerary.title: Sankri to Taluka, Trek to Seema
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Sankri → Taluka (12 km, ~45 min) | Altitude: 2,107 m → 2,560 m (8,399 ft) | Distance: 12 km | Duration: 6–7 hrs | Terrain: forest trail along the Supin River, wooden bridges, gradual climb | Stay: Tents at Seema
After an early breakfast you drive about 45 minutes from Sankri to Taluka at 2,107 m. The road winds through forest and skirts the Supin River before it ends at Taluka, the real starting point of the trek. From here you walk 12 km, and with 6 to 7 hours on the trail it is a long first day. Carry a packed lunch and enough water, because there are few places to stop along the way.
From Taluka the trail follows the Supin through thick forest of walnut, chestnut, willow, chinar, pine and deodar. You cross wooden bridges and pass waterfalls. The height gain is modest across the day, so the test today is distance, not gradient. Settle into a pace you can hold for hours and eat a little at every break.
Partway along, the trail gives you a choice. You can take the steep climb via Dhaatmeer village for a harder workout, or follow the gentler path along the Karmanasha stream. We recommend the gentler route if you want to save your legs for the high camps later in the week. Both paths meet at Gangaar village, a scenic Himalayan settlement.
Beyond Gangaar you continue along the Supin and climb gradually to the campsite at Puani Seema, on the riverside opposite the traditional village of Osla. You sleep in tents on triple sharing tonight. Rest your legs, refill your water and get to bed in good time.
What to Expect: 45-minute drive from Sankri to Taluka, the trailhead Long 12 km walk along the Supin River through walnut, chestnut, chinar and deodar forest Wooden bridges and waterfalls along the way Choice of a steep route via Dhaatmeer village or a gentler path along the Karmanasha stream Packed lunch and full water bottles – few stop points on the trail Overnight: Tents at Seema (2,560 m / 8,399 ft)

itinerary.title: Seema to Devsu Thatch
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 2,560 m → 3,000 m (9,842 ft) | Distance: ~6 km | Duration: 4–5 hrs | Terrain: steep forest climb, then open alpine meadow | Stay: Tents at Devsu Thatch
Today is short but steep. From Puani Seema the trail climbs steadily into thick forest of pine, oak and rhododendron, and the gradient stays stiff for most of the way. The ascent is steep and humid under the trees. Carry plenty of water, drink before you feel thirsty, and break the climb into short stretches with brief pauses rather than long sit-downs.
The reward comes all at once. The trees open and you step onto Devsu Thatch, a vast alpine meadow at 3,000 m with 180 views of snow-clad peaks. Swargarohini, Kalanag (Black Peak) and Bandarpoonch line the skyline. In summer the meadow is carpeted with wildflowers, and dense tree lines frame its edges.
Camp is pitched on the meadow, and it is one of the most scenic campsites of the trek. With only 4 to 5 hours of walking you arrive with time to spare. The evening is at leisure. Sit out with the views of Swargarohini and Kalanag, then settle into your tent under a starry Himalayan night.
This is also your first night at 3,000 m. Keep drinking water through the afternoon and evening, eat a full dinner and tell your trek leader early if you notice a headache. Small habits now make the high camps easier later in the week.
What to Expect: Short, steep climb of about 6 km through pine, oak and rhododendron forest Humid ascent – carry plenty of water Forest opens onto the vast Devsu Thatch meadow with 180 views Swargarohini, Kalanag (Black Peak) and Bandarpoonch on the skyline Wildflowers carpet the meadow in summer; evening at leisure Overnight: Tents at Devsu Thatch (3,000 m / 9,842 ft)

itinerary.title: Devsu Thatch to Ruinsara Tal
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,000 m → 3,500 m (11,482 ft) | Distance: ~8–9 km | Duration: 5–6 hrs | Terrain: gradual forest descent to the Supin, then a gentle climb along the river | Stay: Tents near Ruinsara Tal
After breakfast you leave the meadows of Devsu Thatch and descend gradually through forest of rhododendron, pine and birch to rejoin the Supin River. Take the descent easy; it is a warm-up for the climb that follows, not a race.
Back at the river, the trail climbs gently along the Supin for most of the day. The gradient is kind and the walking is steady, with glimpses of snow-clad peaks in the distance. All four Swargarohini peaks, Kalanag (Black Peak) and Bandarpoonch are the ones to look for. In our experience this is one of the more relaxed days of the trek, and a good one to settle your rhythm before the high camps.
By afternoon you reach Ruinsara Tal at 3,500 m, a sacred glacial lake believed to be associated with the Pandavas of the Mahabharata. It sits among alpine pastures and snow peaks, and camp is pitched near the lake. Spend the evening walking around its surroundings or simply sitting by the water, watching the mountains reflected on its clear surface.
The weather near the lake changes quickly. Keep your warm layers and rain gear within reach, not packed at the bottom of your bag. Tomorrow the trail leaves the forest behind and climbs above 4,000 m for the first time, so rest well tonight and keep drinking water through the evening.
What to Expect: Gradual descent through rhododendron, pine and birch forest to the Supin River
Gentle climb along the river with views of the Swargarohini peaks, Kalanag and Bandarpoonch
Ruinsara Tal (3,500 m): a sacred glacial lake linked to the Pandavas
Lakeside camp among alpine pastures Fast-changing weather – keep warm layers and rain gear handy Overnight: Tents near Ruinsara Tal (3,500 m / 11,482 ft)

itinerary.title: Ruinsara Tal to Odari
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,500 m → 4,100 m (13,451 ft) | Distance: ~6 km | Duration: 5–6 hrs | Terrain: steady climb above the tree line, moraine and boulder fields, snow patches early in the season | Stay: Tents at Odari
After breakfast by Ruinsara Tal the trail leaves the forest behind and climbs steadily above the tree line into rugged high country. The walk is only about 6 km, but it takes 5 to 6 hours because the climb is steady and the ground is rough. This is the day the trek turns from forest walking into high mountain travel.
Above the trees the path crosses moraine and boulder fields, with snow patches early in the season. Watch your footing on the boulders, test loose rocks before you trust them and use your poles for balance. Move at a pace at which you can still talk. If you are gasping, slow down.
The views open with every step. Bandarpoonch, Kalanag (Black Peak) and the Swargarohini peaks stand close on the skyline, far nearer than they looked from the meadows below. Stop now and then to take them in; the pauses help your breathing as much as your photographs.
By afternoon you reach Odari at 4,100 m, a high, open campsite below the approach to Bali Pass. This is your first day and first night above 4,000 m. Walk slowly around camp, drink plenty of water and tell your trek leader straight away about any headache or nausea. Spend the evening resting and acclimatising; the next two days take you to Bali Pass Base Camp and over the pass itself.
What to Expect: Steady climb above the tree line from Ruinsara Tal
Moraine and boulder fields, with snow patches early in the season Close views of Bandarpoonch, Kalanag and the Swargarohini range First day above 4,000 m – slow pace, plenty of water, report any symptoms Open, high campsite at Odari below the approach to Bali Pass
Overnight: Tents at Odari (4,100 m / 13,451 ft)

itinerary.title: Odari to Bali Pass Base Camp
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 4,100 m → 4,600 m (15,092 ft) | Distance: ~5 km | Duration: 4–5 hrs | Terrain: steep ascents on rocky moraine and loose scree, barren high ground | Stay: Tents at Bali Pass Base Camp
The trail today is demanding. You climb steeply over rocky moraine and loose scree, and the short distance hides how hard the effort is at this height. On scree, kick small steps, keep your weight over your feet and follow the line of the person in front. Do not rush the loose sections; steady and careful is faster in the end.
As you gain height the vegetation thins out and gives way to barren, rugged ground. The snowline comes closer and the peaks begin to dominate the skyline. Take short pauses and keep drinking water as you climb. Then the Bali Pass ridgeline comes into view, your first close look at tomorrow's crossing.
By afternoon you reach Bali Pass Base Camp at 4,600 m, at the foot of the pass. It is a raw, high campsite with the Swargarohini massif, Kalanag and Bandarpoonch around it and the sharp ridge of Bali Pass right ahead. The weather here can be unpredictable. Keep enough layers on, stay hydrated and follow the trek leader's instructions strictly.
Spend the evening acclimatising and resting. Tomorrow is the toughest and most rewarding day of the trek, and it begins before dawn. Lay out your layers, gloves and water bottle before you sleep, so you are ready to move in the dark without fuss.
What to Expect: Steep ascents over rocky moraine and loose scree Vegetation gives way to barren, rugged high ground near the snowline First close-up view of the Bali Pass ridgeline Swargarohini massif, Kalanag and Bandarpoonch around camp Unpredictable weather – layers, water and the trek leader's instructions Overnight: Tents at Bali Pass Base Camp (4,600 m / 15,092 ft)

itinerary.title: Summit Day - Bali Pass Base Camp to Lower Dhamni via Bali Pass
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 4,600 m → 4,950 m (16,241 ft) → 3,400 m (11,155 ft) | Distance: ~14 km | Duration: 8–9 hrs | Terrain: steep snow slopes and rocky ridges, a narrow ridge at the top, long steep descent on scree and snow | Stay: Tents at Lower Dhamni
This is the day the whole trek builds towards, and the hardest. Start before dawn, around 4:00 to 5:00 AM. The early hours give safer snow conditions for the climb, and an early start gets you over the pass before the weather turns. Expect 8 to 9 hours on your feet.
The climb is steep, over snow slopes and rocky ridges. Near the top the ridge narrows and needs careful footing. Watch where you place each foot, move at the pace your trek leader sets and keep your attention on the ground until you are on safe footing. Ice axes, microspikes and ropes are part of the team's technical equipment for terrain like this.
Bali Pass at 4,950 m (16,241 ft) is the highest point of the trek. The pass links the Har Ki Dun side with the Yamunotri valley, and from the top the view runs a full 360 : the Swargarohini peaks, Bandarpoonch and Kalanag, with vast valleys stretching below. Take your photographs, but keep your time at the top within what your trek leader allows.
The descent is long and steep, on scree and snow patches. Your knees take the strain now, so use your poles and keep your steps short. Gradually you re-enter alpine meadows and then forest. By evening you reach Lower Dhamni at 3,400 m, a comfortable forest campsite, where you can finally rest after the biggest day of the trek.
What to Expect: Pre-dawn start (around 4:00–5:00 AM) for safe snow and a weather window Steep climb over snow slopes and rocky ridges, with a narrow ridge near the top Bali Pass (4,950 m / 16,241 ft): 360 views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch and Kalanag
Long, steep descent on scree and snow into alpine meadows and forest About 14 km and 8–9 hours – the longest and hardest day of the trek Overnight: Tents at Lower Dhamni (3,400 m / 11,155 ft)

itinerary.title: Lower Dhamni to Janki Chatti via Yamunotri, Drive to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 3,400 m → 2,650 m (8,694 ft) | Distance: ~8 km | Duration: 4–5 hrs | Terrain: gradual, well-marked descent through oak and pine forest | Drive: Janki Chatti → Dehradun (8–9 hrs; Dehradun 640 m)
After breakfast you start the final descent from Lower Dhamni. The trail is well marked and runs down gradually through dense oak and pine forest and past Himalayan villages on the Yamunotri side. After yesterday the walking feels easy, but stay alert on the downhill; tired legs slip more easily. Keep your poles out until the very end.
The trail ends at Janki Chatti at 2,650 m, the pilgrimage town known as the base for the Yamunotri Temple trek. Your trek on foot is complete here, and the day includes the distribution of trek completion certificates and a group farewell.
From Janki Chatti a shared cab (₹1,000 per person, paid directly to the driver) takes you on the long drive of about 200 km back to Dehradun, which takes 8 to 9 hours. The road winds through hill towns, river valleys and pine-covered slopes. You reach Dehradun Railway Station by late evening. Accommodation tonight is not part of the trek.
We recommend booking your onward train, bus or flight from Dehradun for after 11:00 PM, or for the next morning, so you are not racing the clock at the end of a long mountain drive. If the buffer day is used, everything shifts by one day.
What to Expect: Gradual 8 km descent through oak and pine forest and Himalayan villages Walk ends at Janki Chatti (2,650 m / 8,694 ft), the base for the Yamunotri Temple trek Trek completion certificates and a group farewell Shared cab (not included in the trek fee, ₹1,000 per person) for the 8–9 hour drive to Dehradun
Book onward travel for after 11:00 PM or the next morning Trek ends at Janki Chatti; drop at Dehradun Railway Station by late evening

itinerary.title: Buffer Day
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Reserve day: used only for bad weather, heavy snowfall or unexpected delays | Decision: Trek Leader, based on weather and trail conditions | Charge if used: ₹2,100 + 5% GST
Day 9 is held in reserve. High passes do not keep to a fixed timetable, and bad weather or heavy snowfall can make the Bali Pass crossing unsafe on the planned day. The buffer day gives the team the flexibility to wait for a safe window instead of pushing on in poor conditions.
The Trek Leader decides whether to use it, based only on the weather and trail conditions on the ground. If the buffer day is used, trekkers pay ₹2,100 + 5% GST, which the Trek Leader collects at that point. If it is not needed, you finish on Day 8 and can return a day earlier.
We recommend keeping this day free in your travel plans anyway. With a spare day in hand, a weather delay never forces a rushed decision on the pass.
What to Expect: Reserved for bad weather, heavy snowfall or unexpected delays Time for a safe Bali Pass crossing without cutting corners Used only on the Trek Leader's assessment of weather and trail conditions Charge if used: ₹2,100 + 5% GST, collected by the Trek Leader
If not used, you return a day earlier Drop at Dehradun one day later if the buffer day is used How To Reach
By Air
By Train
By Bus
Nearest airport: Jolly Grant Airport (DED), Dehradun – about 25 km / 45–60 min from Dehradun city, with direct flights from Delhi and other metros. The cab to Sankri leaves Dehradun Railway Station at 6:30 AM, so fly in the day before and stay the night in Dehradun.
From Dehradun to Sankri: about 200 km via Mussoorie, Purola, Mori and Naitwar, 8–9 hrs by road. A shared cab leaves Dehradun Railway Station at 6:30 AM. It is not included in the trek fee and costs ₹1,000 per person each way, paid directly to the driver.
Return: The trek ends at Janki Chatti near Yamunotri, not Sankri: after the 8 km walk down, a shared cab (₹1,000 per person, paid directly to the driver) takes you on the 8–9 hr

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Cloud End and trek to Benog Tibba
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Drive: Dehradun → Cloud End (35 km, ~2 hrs) | Trek: about 4 km, 2–3 hrs | Altitude: 2,074 m → 2,216 m (7,270 ft) | Terrain: wide, shaded forest trail with a few short steep sections | Stay: Tents near the Jwala Devi temple You meet in Dehradun in the morning and drive up through Mussoorie, past Library Chowk, and on along the quieter western road towards Cloud End. Cloud End sits at about 2,074 m, at the edge of the Benog (Mussoorie) Wildlife Sanctuary. The drive takes about two hours, depending on traffic in Mussoorie. Mussoorie has the last reliable ATMs and good network; inside the sanctuary the signal is patchy.
At the forest check post the sanctuary entry permits are checked, and the trek begins, so keep your government photo ID handy. The trail is wide and well shaded, winding through deodar, oak, pine and rhododendron. There are a few short, steep sections, with plenty of level stretches in between. On the steep bits, slow down and stop as often as you need. Children can walk at their own pace here, with regular stops, and nobody needs to rush. You pass old stone ruins and small forest clearings along the way.
Walk quietly. The sanctuary is one of the best places for birdwatching near Mussoorie, and if you keep the noise down you are likely to spot several species: red-billed blue magpies, Himalayan woodpeckers, laughingthrushes and many more. This forest is also known as the last recorded home of the Himalayan quail, a bird not reliably seen in more than a century.
Natural water sources are scarce on this trail, so each person should carry at least two litres; the team brings water to camp. The path ends at the top of Benog Tibba, at 2,216 m, where the small Jwala Devi temple stands. Camp is set up close by, in 3-person tents with a dining tent and a toilet tent. In the evening you watch the sun set over the Yamuna valley, then sit down to a hot dinner. It gets cool on top even in summer, so pack a light warm jacket and a cap. For many childre

itinerary.title: Benog Tibba to Cloud End and drive to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Route Details: Altitude: 2,216 m → 2,074 m | Walk: about 4 km back to Cloud End, 1.5–2 hrs | Drive: Cloud End → Dehradun (35 km, ~2 hrs) | Stay: Trip ends in Dehradun
Wake up early for the sunrise. On a clear morning the first light falls on the snow peaks to the north: Bandarpoonch, Swargarohini, Kala Nag (Black Peak) and the Gangotri group. On exceptionally clear days you may see even further east. The Doon valley lies on one side of the hill and the Yamuna valley on the other. Keep your jacket on until the sun is up.
After breakfast you pack up the tents and walk back down through the forest to the road. It is an easy walk of about 4 km, 1.5–2 hours, and a good time for one last look at the birds and the trees. Carry your rubbish down with you.
From Cloud End you drive back through Mussoorie to Dehradun, arriving by early afternoon. That leaves plenty of time to travel home the same day, so book your return train or bus for the afternoon or evening of Day 2.
