itinerary.title: Day 1 (Friday): Mumbai Pickups and the Overnight Pune to Hampi Bus
itinerary.description: Mumbai pickups (the bus connects you to the Pune departure): 01:00 PM – Borivali (West) 02:00 PM – Andheri (East) 03:00 PM – Sion 03:30 PM – Vashi Plaza 04:00 PM – Kalamboli Pune departure: 8:00 PM from Deccan Gymkhana Bus Stop. The Pune to Hampi road trip is an overnight journey of about 585 km in a non-AC bus or tempo traveller (Mumbai to Hampi is about 725 km in total). Meet the group, settle in and get some sleep before your first full day in Hampi. Overnight: bus

itinerary.title: Day 2 (Saturday): Hippie Island, Anegundi, Coracle Ride and Sunset at Anjanadri Hill
itinerary.description: Reach Hampi between 7 and 9 am. Freshen up at the hotel and have breakfast. Rooms are ready from 12 pm, and a common room is available before that. Cross the Tungabhadra River to Hippie Island (Virupapur Gaddi) and explore by bike, past paddy fields, banana plantations and boulder hills. Take a coracle ride in Hampi’s round basket boats and try guided cliff jumping at Sanapur Lake. Visit Durga Temple, Sugriva’s Cave, Anegundi Village and Chintamani Temple, sites linked to Kishkindha in the Ramayana. Climb Anjanadri Hill (about 575 steps), believed to be the birthplace of Hanuman, for one of the best sunsets in Hampi. Dinner at a local café on Hippie Island (own expense), then a bonfire with the group or rest at the hotel. Meals: breakfast, lunch | Overnight: hotel or cottage (shared)

itinerary.title: Day 3 (Sunday): Guided Hampi Sightseeing, from Vittala Temple to Virupaksha Temple
itinerary.description: Check out after breakfast and start sightseeing with a professional local guide. Monument entry tickets are included. Vittala Temple: Vijaya Vittala Temple, known for its musical pillars, and the Stone Chariot shown on the ₹50 note. Royal Centre: Queen’s Bath, the Royal Enclosure and its Pushkarni stepped tank, Lotus Mahal, the Elephant Stables and the Underground Shiva Temple. Around Hampi Bazaar: Badavi Linga, the Narasimha monolith, Sasivekalu Ganesha and Virupaksha Temple, which is still in worship today. Watch the sunset over the Virupaksha Temple tower from Hemakuta Hill. Dinner (own expense), then board the overnight bus back. Meals: breakfast, lunch | Overnight: bus

itinerary.title: Day 4 (Monday): Arrive in Pune and Mumbai
itinerary.description: Day 4 (Monday): Arrive in Pune and Mumbai Reach Pune between 6 and 8 am. Mumbai travellers: 11 am

itinerary.title: Delhi to Shimla | Overnight Journey
itinerary.description:
Begin your winter Spiti adventure with an evening departure from Delhi. Board your scheduled AC bus or Volvo for the overnight journey to Shimla. Keep warm clothing, medicines and overnight essentials in a small bag within easy reach.
Departure: Around 9:30 PM; final boarding location and reporting time will be shared before departure.
Dinner: At your own expense during a scheduled roadside stop.
Stay: Overnight bus journey.
Important: Eat a light meal before boarding if you prefer not to depend on the dinner stop.

itinerary.title: Shimla
itinerary.description:
+
Arrive in Shimla and continue towards Kinnaur in the sightseeing vehicle. Travel through Kufri and Narkanda, following mountain roads towards the Sangla Valley. Stop for photographs near Kinnaur Gate where parking and road conditions permit.
If the approach road is open and time allows, visit Chitkul to explore the village and enjoy views of the Baspa Valley. Check in at your accommodation and rest after the long journey.
Breakfast: En route, at your own expense.
Lunch: At a roadside restaurant, at your own expense.
Dinner:

itinerary.title: Sangla
itinerary.description:
+
After an early breakfast, leave for Spiti Valley. Follow the mountain highway towards Nako, passing the winding Ka Loops where the route permits.
Take a short walk through Nako village and visit the lake if accessible. Continue towards Tabo, with stops adjusted to daylight and road conditions.
Breakfast:

itinerary.title: Tabo
itinerary.description:
+
Have breakfast and, if staying in Tabo, visit Tabo Monastery before departure, subject to opening hours. If the previous night’s stay was in Nako, continue to Tabo first.
Proceed towards Dhankar for a visit to its monastery and views over the Spiti and Pin river valleys, provided the approach road is accessible. Continue to Kaza, check in and spend the evening resting.
Breakfast:

itinerary.title: Kaza
itinerary.description:
+
After breakfast, set out to explore the villages above Kaza, subject to road access.
Visit Hikkim’s high-altitude post office, explore Komic and continue to Langza, known for its Buddha statue and mountain setting. Return to Kaza for a relaxed evening.
Breakfast:

Enjoy breakfast before leaving for Key Monastery. Explore the accessible visitor areas, respect monastery customs and take in the surrounding valley views.
Continue towards Chicham Bridge if the road is open. Stop at a safe location for photographs before returning to Kaza.
Breakfast:

itinerary.title: Kalpa
itinerary.description:
+
After an early breakfast, check out and begin the return journey through the Spiti Valley towards Kinnaur. Take short refreshment and photography stops where conditions allow.
Reach Kalpa, check in and rest after a full day on the road.
Breakfast:

itinerary.title: Shimla
itinerary.description:
+
Wake up to views of the Kinner Kailash range, weather permitting. Have breakfast, check out and depart early for Shimla.
Allow a full day for the drive, with meal and comfort stops along the way. On arrival, board the scheduled overnight bus to Delhi.
Breakfast:

Arrive in Delhi in the morning, subject to traffic and travel conditions. The trip ends at the designated drop-off point.
Breakfast: At your own expense after arrival.
Lunch: Not included.
Stay: None.
Important: Leave a generous buffer before booking onward flights or trains.
Important Winter Travel Information
Weather and access: Snowfall, ice and road closures can change sightseeing, overnight stops and travel times. Snow-covered scenery cannot be guaranteed.
Accommodation: Winter stays may offer basic facilities. Confirm room sharing, Meals:
Lunch stops depend on open restaurants. Inform the organiser about dietary requirements in advance.
Packing: Carry thermal layers, a warm jacket, gloves, a woollen cap, footwear with good grip, sunglasses, sunscreen and personal medicines.
Connectivity: Carry cash, a power bank and offline copies of booking details and identification.
Delays: Keep buffer time available. Additional accommodation, meals or transport caused by disruptions may incur extra charges under the booking terms.

itinerary.title: Mumbai to Ambala Cantt
itinerary.description:
Bandra Terminus
+
Board your train from Bandra Terminus at 10:30 AM. Settle in, meet your group over some fun games, and enjoy the journey north. Overnight on the train.

itinerary.title: Rampur Bushahr, Himachal Pradesh
itinerary.description:
+
Arrive at Ambala Cantt railway station at 8:45 AM. Board your vehicle around 9 AM and drive to Rampur via Narkanda, a scenic route lined with apple orchards, pine forests and good roadside eateries to relax along the way. Dinner and overnight stay at Rampur.

itinerary.title: Rakchham
itinerary.description:
+
Drive towards Rakchham through the beautiful Sangla Valley, passing Sarahan with its streams and orchards. En route, visit Chitkul, the last inhabited village on the Indo-Tibetan border. After soaking in the views at Chitkul, head to your hotel in Rakchham. Dinner and overnight stay at Rakchham.

itinerary.title: Kalpa
itinerary.description:
+
A day among the Kinnaur Kailash ranges. En route, stop at Reckong Peo market for snacks, visit the Kothi Temple, and take in the views from Suicide Point. Dinner and overnight stay at Kalpa

itinerary.title: Tabo
itinerary.description:
+
Drive from Kalpa to the village of Tabo, with fantastic stops along the way at the high-altitude Nako Lake and the remote Gue Monastery, home to a naturally preserved mummy. The landscape shifts to the bare, brown mountains that Spiti is famous for. Check in at Tabo. Dinner and overnight stay at Tabo.

itinerary.title: Kaza
itinerary.description:
+
Begin at Tabo Monastery, one of the oldest continuously functioning Buddhist monasteries in India, alongside the ancient Tabo caves. Then visit the dramatic Dhankar Monastery and the confluence of the Spiti and Pin rivers, before exploring the wild beauty of Pin Valley National Park. Drive on to Kaza, the main town of Spiti. Dinner and overnight stay at Kaza.

itinerary.title: Kaza
itinerary.description:
+
A full day among the highest villages in the world. Drive to Langza, where a giant Buddha statue looks out over the valley, in a region the Geological Survey of India rates as one of the most fossil-rich on earth. Send a postcard home from Hikkim, the highest post office in the world. Then visit the iconic Key Monastery and cross Chicham Bridge, the highest suspension bridge in Asia, before returning to Kaza. Evening free to explore Kaza market. Dinner and overnight stay at Kaza.

itinerary.title: Manali
itinerary.description:
+
Drive towards Sarahan, then reach the stunning Bhimakali Temple in the evening for a 1 to 2 hour stroll along itemple. Around 3 PM, the long, scenic drive to Sarahan Bushahr Dinner and overnight stay at Sarahan.

itinerary.title: Chandigarh
itinerary.description:
+
After breakfast and check-out, spend some time shopping on Manali Mall Road. Around 4 PM, drive towards Chandigarh, arriving at the railway station by around 11 PM.

itinerary.title: Chandigarh
itinerary.description:
+
Checkout after Breakfast. We will drive and stop at Narkhanda, Kufri, Shimla and leave for Chandigarh after an early dinner.
Board your train from Chandigarh at 5:40 AM. Spend the journey with your group, reliving the trip one last time before the routine of home returns.
Breakfast included.

itinerary.title: Mumbai, Bandra Terminus
itinerary.description:
+
Arrive in Mumbai around 7 AM, carrying a camera full of photos and a head full of memories from the Serene Spiti Valley tour.

itinerary.title: Day One - Delhi to Shimla
itinerary.description:
Akshardham Delhi Metro Station
+
9 pm - Akshardham Delhi Metro Station
Assemble at the boarding point in Kashmere Gate, Delhi, and meet your Trip Captain.
Depart from Delhi between 9:00 PM to 10:30 PM.
Begin your overnight journey towards Shimla.
Note: Exact boarding details will be shared with travellers 24 hours prior to departure.

itinerary.title: Shimla
itinerary.description:
+
Upon arrival in Shimla, begin your journey towards Sangla.
En route, take a refreshing breakfast halt at either Kufri or Narkanda and soak in the much-needed mountain vibes.
After breakfast, continue your scenic drive along the Indo-Tibetan Highway towards Sangla Valley.
By evening, arrive at the beautiful village of Chitkul.
Overnight stay in Chitkul.

itinerary.title: Nako
itinerary.description:
+
Wake up to a peaceful morning in Chitkul and take time to explore its scenic beauty.
Drive towards Kalpa, soaking in breathtaking views of the majestic Kinnaur Kailash Range.
Stop at Khab Sangam, where the Sutlej and Spiti rivers meet.
Continue the picturesque journey into Spiti Valley and reach the charming village of Nako.
Visit Nako Lake and enjoy the serene high-altitude landscape.
Dinner and overnight stay in Nako.

itinerary.title: Kaza
itinerary.description:
+
Nako to Kaza | Explore Gue, Tabo & Dhankar Monastery
After breakfast, journey deeper into the heart of Spiti Valley.
Visit Gue Monastery, famous for the naturally preserved mummy of a Buddhist monk.
Continue to Tabo Monastery, a 1000-year-old spiritual site renowned for its exquisite murals and rich history.
Stop at the scenic Dhankar Monastery, perched dramatically on a cliff with breathtaking valley views.
Arrive in Kaza, the vibrant hub of Spiti Valley.
Enjoy dinner and an overnight stay in Kaza.

itinerary.title: Kaza
itinerary.description:
+
KAZA EXPLORATION:- LANGZA, KOMIC, HIKKIM, KEY MONESTRY
Post breakfast, drive Towards Local Kaza Sightseeings like :-
Visit Spit's gorgeous fossil village Langza and get clicked with the iconic statue of Medicine Buddha with your clan.
Feel proud for making it to the World's highest motorable village Komic and absorb i n the jaw dropping vistas o f snow-laden Himalayas.
Head towards visiting the Highest post office in the world (Hikkim) & write to your loved ones.
Visit the iconic Key Monastery, the largest monastery in Spiti Valley.
Savour home-style cooked dinner and Overnight stay in a homestay.

itinerary.title: Chandratal
itinerary.description:
+
Wake up to a serene mountain morning in Kaza, with breathtaking views of snow-covered peaks from your cozy stay.
After breakfast, head out to explore Kibber, known for its rich wildlife, including the elusive snow leopard, Himalayan ibex, and red fox.
Capture stunning #InstaPerfect moments at Chicham Bridge, connecting Kibber to the rest of Spiti Valley.
Continue your scenic drive towards the majestic Chandratal Lake—a place whose beauty is truly beyond words.
This pristine lake is a paradise for nature lovers and adventure seekers alike.
End your day with a once-in-a-lifetime experience of camping under the stars, with an overnight stay in tents (quad/penta sharing basis).

itinerary.title: Manali
itinerary.description:
+
Wake up early and get ready to witness a magical sunrise at Chandratal Lake, then join the scenic Leh–Manali Highway.
Drive through the iconic Atal Tunnel, connecting Lahaul Valley to Manali.
Arrive in Manali, check in to your hotel, and enjoy some leisure time exploring Mall Road Manali.
Overnight stay in Manali.

itinerary.title: Manali
itinerary.description:
+
After breakfast, head out to visit the famous Hadimba Devi Temple, nestled amidst towering deodar forests.
Explore Old Manali and enjoy some leisure time soaking in its laid-back vibe.
Indulge in delicious meals at the quirky cafés of Old Manali, and later visit Mall Road Manali for street food, shopping, and souvenirs.
In the evening, board your bus for the return journey to Delhi.

itinerary.title: Akshardham Delhi Metro Station
itinerary.description:
+
The group will reach Delhi by early in the morning. End of Tour

itinerary.title: Delhi to Kasol
itinerary.description:
Reach Delhi by 01:30 PM and proceed to Kashmiri Gate.
Board a Volvo bus or cab to Kasol between 06:30 PM – 09:00 PM.
Begin your overnight journey from Delhi to Kasol.

itinerary.title: Kasol – Chalal – Kasol
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Kasol and check in to the campsite.
Enjoy a welcome drink, freshen up, and relax.
Explore Kasol with a riverside walk along the Parvati River.
Later, hike to Chalal Village, crossing the famous Kasol bridge and soaking in views of Parvati Valley.
Evening tea and snacks will be served.
Spend time café hopping in Kasol, visiting popular Israeli cafés such as Little Italy, Evergreen Café, Shiva Café, German Bakery, and Moonlight Café.
Enjoy camping under the stars, followed by a bonfire dinner, and overnight stay in camps beside the Parvati River.

itinerary.title: Kasol – Barshaini – Tosh Trek
itinerary.description:
Wake up early and have breakfast.
Travel to Barshaini (22 km from Kasol) by private vehicle.
Start the Tosh Trek from Barshaini.
Trek distance: 4–5 km Difficulty level: Moderate
Walk through scenic trails surrounded by forests and snow-capped Himalayan peaks.
Reach Tosh and check in to camps.
Dinner by the bonfire under a star-lit sky, followed by an overnight stay in Tosh.

itinerary.title: Tosh – Barshaini – Manikaran – Kasol – Delhi
itinerary.description:
Wake up early and have breakfast.
Trek back from Tosh to Barshaini.
Visit Manikaran Gurudwara Sahib, famous for its hot springs and spiritual significance.
Return to Kasol for local market exploration and last-minute shopping.
Begin your overnight journey back to Delhi.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Delhi
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Delhi by 10:00 – 11:00 AM.
If time permits, explore major attractions such as Red Fort, Humayun’s Tomb, and India Gate. ( Not included in package)

itinerary.title: Drive from Delhi/Dehradun Airport or Rishikesh to New Tehri
itinerary.description:
Drive: 315 km Altitude: 230 m to 1,750 m Accommodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Dinner
Your trek begins with a pickup from Delhi Airport, Dehradun Airport, or Rishikesh, depending on your travel arrangements. From here, drive towards New Tehri through the beautiful landscapes of Uttarakhand. Enjoy views of winding mountain roads, green valleys, and the surrounding hills along the way. After reaching New Tehri, check into your guesthouse or homestay and relax after the long drive. Spend the evening resting and preparing for the journey ahead.

itinerary.title: Drive from New Tehri to Harsil
itinerary.description:
Drive: 190 km Altitude: 1,750 m to 2,700 m Accommodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, begin your drive from New Tehri to Harsil, a beautiful Himalayan valley located along the Bhagirathi River. The route offers scenic views of mountain villages, forests, rivers, and towering Himalayan peaks. As you approach Harsil, enjoy the peaceful surroundings and fresh mountain air. Upon arrival, check into your guesthouse or homestay and spend the rest of the day relaxing. You can explore the nearby surroundings and prepare your trekking gear for the following day.

itinerary.title: Drive from Harsil to Gangotri and trek to Chirbasa
itinerary.description:
Drive: 25 km Trek: 9 km Altitude:
2,700 m to 3,600 m Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, drive approximately 25 km from Harsil to Gangotri, one of the most important pilgrimage destinations in the Indian Himalayas. After reaching Gangotri, complete the necessary preparations and begin your trek towards Chirbasa. The trail follows the Bhagirathi River and passes through rugged mountain terrain, rocky sections, and scenic valleys. As you gradually move away from Gangotri, the landscape becomes increasingly dramatic, with views of towering peaks and the surrounding wilderness. After trekking for around 9 km, reach Chirbasa, set up camp, and enjoy dinner before resting for the night in alpine tents.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chirbasa to Bhojbasa
itinerary.description:
Trek: 5 km, 3 hrs Altitude:
3,600 m to 3,800 m Accommodation:
Camping (Alpine Tents)/Aashram
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The third day of the trek involves a relatively short but steep ascent to Bhojbasa, which is situated at an altitude of 3,800 meters. The trail continues along the Bhagirathi River. The views along the trail are stunning, with towering mountains in the background and the sound of the river in the foreground. The campsite at Bhojbasa is situated at the foot of the Gangotri glacier, and trekkers can see the glacier in the distance. The campsite offers a stunning view of the Bhagirathi peaks, which are bathed in golden light during sunrise and sunset.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bhojbasa to Gaumukh to Tapovan
itinerary.description:
Trek: 6 km, 7 hrs Altitude:
3,800 m to 3,900 m to 4,335 m Accommodation:
Camping (Alpine Tents)
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The fourth day of the trek is the highlight of the journey, as trekkers visit the source of the Ganges river at Gaumukh. The trail from Bhojbasa to Gaumukh is steep and rocky, and the last stretch involves crossing the Gangotri glacier. The glacier is a surreal landscape of ice and rocks, and trekkers need to be careful while walking on it. After reaching Gaumukh, trekkers can take a dip in the icy-cold water and offer prayers at the temple. We then proceed to Tapovan from Gaumukh. The route from Gaumukh to Tapovan is a steep and short climb. It takes about 2-2.5 hrs to reach there. Set up your camps at Tapovan and enjoy the the majestic views of Meru peak, Bhagirathi I,II,III peaks. Tapovan also acts as the base camp for Shivling and Meru offers grand majestic views of Shivling peak.

itinerary.title: Day hike to Kirti Glacier or Meru Glacier and back
itinerary.description:
Trek: 12 km Altitude: 4,335 m Accommodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, set out for a day hike towards Kirti Glacier or Meru Glacier, exploring the spectacular glacial landscape surrounding Tapovan. The hike offers an opportunity to experience the rugged beauty of this high-altitude region, with views of glaciers, rocky terrain, and towering Himalayan peaks. The exact route and distance will depend on weather conditions, snow cover, and the group's fitness and acclimatisation. Spend time appreciating the remote mountain environment before returning to the Tapovan campsite. Enjoy a warm meal at camp and spend the evening resting in the peaceful surroundings of the high Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tapovan to Chirbasa
itinerary.description:
Trek: 11 km, 6 hrs Altitude:
4,335 m to 3,600 m Accommodation:
Camping (Alpine Tents)
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
This is a long walk from Tapovan to Chirbasa is over 10-11 km but since you will be going downhill, you would not take as much time as it took to climb up. You will have a packed lunch en route and reach Chirbasa by late afternoon. Camp the night under the starry skies at Chirbasa.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chirbasa to Gangotri and drive to Uttarkashi
itinerary.description:
Trek: 9 km, 5-6 hrs Drive:
100 km Altitude: 3,600 m – 1,158 m Accommodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Wake up early and enjoy breakfast before beginning the final stretch of your trek from Chirbasa to Gangotri. Follow the familiar trail alongside the Bhagirathi River, taking in the mountain scenery as you make your way back towards Gangotri. After completing the approximately 9 km trek, meet your vehicle and drive towards Uttarkashi. The drive takes you through beautiful Himalayan valleys and mountain settlements. Upon reaching Uttarkashi, check into your guesthouse or homestay, enjoy a meal, and relax after completing the trekking portion of your expedition.

itinerary.title: Drive from Uttarkashi to Rishikesh or Dehradun/Delhi Airport
itinerary.description:
Drive: 380 km Altitude: 1,750 m to 230 m Accommodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Breakfast
After breakfast, begin your return journey from Uttarkashi towards Rishikesh, Dehradun, or Delhi Airport, according to your travel arrangements. Enjoy the final views of Uttarakhand's mountain landscapes as you descend towards the plains. The journey covers approximately 380 km, depending on the destination and route. Your Gaumukh Tapovan Trek concludes upon arrival at your selected drop-off point, leaving you with unforgettable memories of the glaciers, alpine campsites, and spectacular Himalayan scenery.
Difficulty Level of Gaumukh Tapovan Trek
The Gaumukh Tapovan Trek is considered a moderate to difficult trek due to its high altitude, glacier terrain, and steep ascent to Tapovan. While the trail from Gangotri to Gaumukh is well-defined and relatively gradual, the section beyond Gaumukh becomes significantly more challenging. Trekkers must navigate rocky moraines, loose boulders, uneven glacial terrain, and a steep climb to reach the beautiful meadows of Tapovan.
The trek begins from Gangotri and gradually gains altitude through Chirbasa and Bhojbasa, allowing trekkers to acclimatize before reaching Gaumukh. These initial sections follow a clear mountain trail with moderate ascents and are suitable for anyone with a reasonable level of fitness. The real challenge starts after Gaumukh, where the route crosses the Gangotri Glacier's moraine and climbs steeply towards Tapovan. This stretch requires careful footing and is physically demanding, especially because of the thinner air at higher elevations.
The Gaumukh Tapovan Trek covers approximately 42 km in 8 days, with daily walking distances ranging between 6 and 10 km. Although the daily distances are not very long, the combination of altitude, rocky terrain, and continuous elevation gain makes the trek more demanding than many beginner Himalayan treks.

We commence our journey from Dehradun around 6:30 am, aiming to arrive in Joshimath by evening. The drive will lead us through several towns of great significance, such as Rishikesh, Srinagar, Devprayag, and Rudraprayag, two of the renowned Panchprayags, each holding its own religious and spiritual importance. Upon reaching Joshimath in the evening, we will check into our hotel. This is where we’ll make final preparations for tomorrow’s trek, ensuring that we are fully ready for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Dhak and Trek to Guling
itinerary.description:
Drive: 7 km, 15 min Trek:
5 km, 3 hrs Altitude: 6,150 ft (1,875 m) – 6,890 ft (2,100 m) – 9,186 ft (2,800 m)
Accommodation: Camping (Alpine Tents)
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, we drive to Dhak, towards the road to Tapovan. The trek begins from Dhak. The trail goes uphill towards our right away from the road. Over half of the path is open and without shade. We pass two villages on the way. We enter a forest about a kilometre before reaching the campsite of Guling. The camp has views towards the peak of Dunagiri. We can enjoy the tranquillity and natural beauty of the place once we arrive at the campsite.

itinerary.title: Trek from Guling to Khullara
itinerary.description:
Trek: 5 km, 4 hrs Altitude:
9,186 ft (2,800 m) – 10,990 ft (3,350 m)
Accommodation: Camping (Alpine Tents)
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Like in previous days, we will have a healthy breakfast in the morning and begin our today’s trek. The trail today has a gradual slope up. We walk among Oak, Rhododendron, Himalayan Birch and Pine forests. Khullara is an open meadow with astounding views of surrounding peaks like Dunagiri, Hathi and Ghodi, Nanda Devi, Trishul, Kamet, Mana, Nilgiri. We will set up our campsite at khullara and stay there for tonight.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khullara to Kuari pass and back to Taali
itinerary.description:
Trek: 10 km, 6 hrs Altitude:
10,990 ft (3,350 m) – 12,532 ft (3,820 m) – 11,515 ft (3,510 m)
Accommodation: Camping (Alpine Tents)
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
We will have an early breakfast and start walking uphill towards the pass. We will reach a ridge, cross it and take a left. The path leads us away and towards our right to the pass. We spend some time here and then head back along the same way till we reach the ridge again. From here instead of heading down towards Khullara, we walk along the ridge towards Taali. We reach a small hillock with flag, named Chitrakantha. From here we get This spot has stunning panoramic views. We can see the peaks including Chaukhambha, Neelkanth, Mana, Hathi, Ghodi and Dunagiri. We walk down the other side and proceed towards our campsite. Taali is located inside the forest and is closed from all sides.

itinerary.title: Trek from Taali to Auli via Gorson Bugyal and Drive to Joshimath
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7 km, 3-4 hrs Drive:
7 km, 15 min Altitude: 11,515 ft (3,510 m) – 6,150 ft (1,875 m)
Accommodation: Hotel/Resort
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
On this day, the walk is easy. The forest clears away soon. We pass by Taali Lake, which is often frozen in winter. As we keep traversing towards Auli, the view of Nanda Devi peak becomes clearer towards our back. After crossing Gorson Bugyal, a large meadow, we enter a forest. A short walk further, the skiing destination of Auli presents itself. A vehicle will take us back to Joshimath from here where we will check into the Hotel.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Drive: 290 km, 9-10 hrs Altitude:
6,150 ft (1,875 m) – 2,100 ft (640 m)
Meals: Breakfast
We leave from Joshimath and reach Dehradun by early evening.
As you settle back into everyday life, make sure to read our complete guide on how to recover after a Himalayan trek to properly heal muscle soreness and rehydrate.
Difficulty Level of Kuari Pass Trek
The Kuari Pass Trek is a moderate-level trek and is ideal for both beginners and experienced trekkers. The trail follows well-defined paths through forests, alpine meadows, and mountain ridges, with gradual ascents and a few steeper sections near Kuari Pass.
The trek follows the route Dhak – Guling – Khullara – Kuari Pass – Auli, covering about 28 km over 4 trekking days. The climb to Kuari Pass is the most challenging part, but it is not technically difficult and can be completed comfortably with a steady pace. Anyone with good fitness and the ability to walk 6–8 km daily can complete this trek. With a little preparation, including regular walking or cardio exercises, the Kuari Pass Trek is an excellent Himalayan adventure for first-time trekkers and nature lovers.
Kuari Pass Trek – Scenic and Good for Fit Beginners
The Kuari Pass Trek is one of the best beginner-friendly treks in Uttarakhand. With its well-defined trails, moderate altitude of 12,532 ft (3,820 m), and manageable daily walking distances, it is perfect for first-time trekkers and adventure enthusiasts. The trek takes you through dense oak and rhododendron forests, beautiful alpine meadows like Gorson Bugyal, and scenic campsites before rewarding you with breathtaking views of Nanda Devi, Dunagiri, Chaukhamba, and other Himalayan peaks. It offers the perfect balance of adventure, natural beauty, and comfort, making it an unforgettable first Himalayan trekking experience.
Who Should Do Kuari Pass Trek?
Beginners and first-time Himalayan trekkers.
Nature and mountain lovers.
Anyone with reasonable fitness who can comfortably walk 6–8 km.

Best Time to Go
May to June and September to November are the best times for this part of the GHT. The weather is good then. The sky is usually clear, so you get big, long views.
Just skip the rainy season and the coldest winter months.
This connected route is a slow, beautiful introduction to the Great Himalayan Trail. It is an easy trek in Uttarakhand to plan. It is not just about covering miles. It is about learning how every turn, every sunrise, and every ridge changes the way you see the mountains.

itinerary.description:
Altitude: 3,500 m Accommodation:
Guest House/Hotel
Meals: Evening Snacks + Dinner
After arrival at Leh Airport, our cab will pick you up and transfer you to the hotel. You will be spending the night at The Bodhi Tree, one of the best rated accommodation in Leh.
Relax and rejuvenate at the Hotel. Tomorrow we set out to explore near Leh.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization and Sightseeing
itinerary.description:
Altitude: 3,500 m Accomodation:
Guest House/Hotel
Meals: Breakfast + Dinner
After a sumptuous breakfast at the hotel restaurant, we set out to explore in and around Leh.
We start with the Leh Monastery, which is an age old monument, also known as as the Lhachen Palkhar. King Sengge Namgyal built the Leh Palace during the 16th Century and it was completed by the 17th century.
The facades of the Leh palace resemble that of the Potala Palace in Lhasa.
In the evening we can visit the Leh Market and drive to Shanti Stupa for a vivid sunset.
Dine in a local restaurant with some local chamomile tea and a variety of local cuisine.

itinerary.title: Drive from Leh to Chilling, Trek/Drive from Chilling to Skiu
itinerary.description:
Drive Distance: 65 km (2-3 hrs)
Trek Distance: 9 km (3-4 hrs)
Altitude Loss: 3,500 m to 3,400 m Accomodation:
Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The day starts with a drive from Leh, early in the morning, along the Leh – Srinagar highway which runs parallel to Indus river. After 35 KM on this well paved beautiful road, we arrive at the confluence of Indus and Zanskar rivers, where we take a discourse towards south, parallel to river Zanskar, which now runs right along the road, and will continue to, until we arrive at Chilling. From chilling we are to cross the river, by taking the recently constructed bridge. The route ahead is an unpaved road, running now along the Markha river. Having already come across 3 different rivers, it sure is a delight.
We arrive at Skiu in 3 hours. After initial climb through hairpins, the route is very gradual, henceforth. Halfway we arrive at Village Kaya, and Skiu is another 3 KM up ahead. Skiu is a beautiful village tucked amidst tall mountains, with options for Homestay, as well as camping, but the recently constructed motorable road has provided the option to trek Further up to Sara, a hamlet, as if an Oasis in a desert. We rest and relish a warm meal, preferably a dish that goes by the name of this village, i.e. “Skiu”.

itinerary.title: Trek from Skiu to Sara
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 11 km (4-6 hrs)
Altitude Gain: 3,400 m to 3,600 m Accomodation:
Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, we start our trekking journey to Sara, which is around 11 KM ahead. We continue along this well marked trail running parallel to the river Markha.
Halfway along the route we come across a Sole Tea Shop, which is women run. You can rest here, enjoy a cup of Tea or Coffee, but our favorite happened to be the fresh apricot juice which they happen to serve, although in limited quantities.
A stream cuts across the trail here, which can be used to refill your water bottles. The trail offers practically no shade except slightly ahead of the Tea Shop, where a short section of young trees render much need cool to the warm environment. To supplement yourself with water continuously is very important.
After around 3 KM we come across a bridge and cross over to the other side of the river, into a small forest patch, before the trail clears up again. The route is straight ahead along the river with only mild ascent all the way up the hamlet of Sara. The Hamlet will only appear once we are very close to the settlement, less than half a KM, where a hump in the landscape obstructs the view ahead. Once atop the feature, which is lined with a Stupa and prayer flags, we can see the beautiful settlement with 3-4 houses which all offer the option for Homestay, as we as camping. Green Fields, blossoming trees surrounding these houses are in stark contrast to the landscape all around.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sara to Markha
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 10 km (5-6 hrs)
Altitude Gain: 3,600 m to 3,700 m Accommodation:
Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The trail from Sara to Markha is again a gradual one, with no steep ascent and can be easily covered in 3-4 hours at a slow pace. After less than 2 KM from Sara we cross a bridge to our left which takes us to the true right of the river (i.e. river is now flowing on our right hand side).
Slightly further up we come across fields alongside a small village settlement, against backdrop of a steep mountain face. We continue along the trail, which slightly ascends to a higher open ground with a Stupa and Prayer stones (Mani stones), carved intricately. Take due note that you always cross these religious marking from the left (the stupa or prayer stones being on your right hand side). We quickly go downhill near the river and cross a small stream over a bridge of wooden logs.
Almost 2 KM prior to Markha village we again cross the river to our right with two bridges, one of which may be broken and will need some effort to traverse. With 1 more KM to go, we arrive at a Tea shop & Homestay with sunflowers blooming in their vicinity, offering a splendid sight with a stark contrast. A few more homestays and a campground are scattered ahead along the route, which hints at the proximity of Markha village. The last few hundered meters stretch to the village is a steep climb, which concludes in the arrival at the Monastery, followed by the village with its houses spread across the lush fields.
We can spend some time at the Monastery before we continue inwards. The village has a vivid historic past and unique culture, and the day can be spent exploring these.

itinerary.title: Trek from Markha to Hankar
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 13 km (7-8 hrs)
Altitude Gain: 3,700 m to 4,100 m Accommodation:
Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The trek from Markha village to Hankar goes through a Monastery – the Tacha Gompa and a small settlement called Umlung. There are very few houses here with a couple of tea houses. You will see a large white canvas tent from far away as you approach Umlung.
The Tacha Gompa is inhabited by a sole Buddhist monk, who resides in the Gompa situated atop a steep cliff. A very steep staircase leads to the monastery situated a few hundred feet high above the valley below.
The last stretch to the village Hankar requires crossing a couple of more tea houses and then climbing up a steep section of trail that cuts through a cliff. As we reach the top we are welcomed by panoramic views of the Hankar village and its fields to the left, as well as a millennia old fort remains on a mountain top to the right.

itinerary.title: Trek from Hankar to Nimaling
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 12 km (7-8 hrs)
Altitude Gain: 4,100 m to 4,800 m Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The trek from Hankar to Nimaling marks the transition from the green villages of Markha Valley to the vast high-altitude landscapes of Ladakh. Leaving behind the cultivated fields and mud houses of Hankar, the trail gradually climbs alongside the Markha River, offering magnificent views of rugged mountains and wide-open valleys.
Along the way, you will pass a few shepherd camps and grazing grounds where yaks, sheep, and horses can often be seen feeding on the alpine meadows. The valley becomes increasingly barren and dramatic as the snow-capped peaks of Kang Yatse begin to dominate the skyline. As the trail gains altitude, the landscape opens up into the beautiful Nimaling Plateau, one of the highest and most scenic camping grounds in Ladakh. During summer, nomadic families bring their livestock here, adding life and color to the vast grasslands.

itinerary.title: Trek from Nimaling to Chokdo via Kongmaru La and Drive to Leh
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 13 km, 7-8 hrs Drive Distance:
60 km, 3 hrs Altitude Gain & Loss:
4,800 m to 5,200 m to 3,900 m to 3,500 m Accomodation:
Hotel/Guest House
The final day of the Markha Valley Trek is both challenging and incredibly rewarding. Starting early from the vast meadows of Nimaling, the trail climbs steadily towards Kongmaru La Pass (5,260 m), the highest point of the trek. The ascent is gradual but demanding due to the high altitude, and every step offers stunning views of the surrounding peaks and the immense landscape of Ladakh.
As you reach the prayer-flag-covered summit of Kongmaru La, breathtaking panoramas unfold in every direction. On clear days, the snow-covered peaks of the Karakoram Range and Kang Yatse can be seen standing majestically against the blue skies. After spending some time at the pass, the trail begins a long descent through a dramatic canyon carved by centuries of glacial streams.
The route from Kongmaru La to Chokdo is one of the most scenic sections of the Markha Valley Trek. Narrow gorges, colorful rock formations, and towering canyon walls create an almost surreal landscape. Upon reaching Chokdo, vehicles await the drive back to Leh.

itinerary.title: Checkout from Hotel in Leh
itinerary.description:
Altitude: 3,500 m Meals: Breakfast
After breakfast you may checkout from Hotel to either return from Leh or you may extend your travel for a guided/unguided tour of Ladakh including visiting places such as Khardunga La, Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri, Nubra Valley etc.
Difficulty Level of Markha Valley Trek
The Markha Valley Trek is generally considered a moderate to difficult trek. While the trail itself is not technically demanding, the high altitude, long walking hours, and frequent river crossings make it a physically challenging adventure. The trek rewards you with breathtaking landscapes and cultural experiences, but it also demands good fitness and proper acclimatization.
One of the biggest challenges of the Markha Valley Trek is the altitude. The journey begins from Leh at an elevation of around 3,200 m and gradually ascends to Kongmaru La Pass at 5,200 m. As you gain height, the oxygen level decreases, and many trekkers may experience symptoms of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS), especially above 4,000 m.
Another factor that adds to the difficulty is the length of the trek. Covering approximately 65 km over 8 to 9 days, trekkers spend 8 to 10 hours walking on most days. Although there are no technical climbing sections, the long distances and continuous ascents and descents require good stamina and endurance. Maintaining a steady pace and staying hydrated are essential for completing the trek comfortably.
The Markha Valley Trek is also known for its numerous river crossings. During the summer months, the water level rises due to melting snow, and trekkers often have to wade through knee-deep streams. While these crossings are generally safe, the freezing-cold water can leave your feet numb for a short time, adding another layer of challenge to the experience.
Weather conditions in the high-altitude deserts of Ladakh can be unpredictable. Although Markha Valley lies in a rain-shadow region and receives very little rainfall, sudden showers and snowfall are still possib

itinerary.title: Drive from Manali to Jobra and Trek to Chika
itinerary.description:
Driving Distance: 18 km, 1 hr Trek Distance:
2 km, 1-2 hrs Altitude Gain:
6,700 ft to 10,100 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Dinner
The journey begins with a drive from Manali to Jobra via a very scenic route. The road takes you through dense Pine & Deodar trees and over several small mountain streams that are fed by the winter's melting snow.
Hampta Pass Trek begins with a gradual descent through a forest before entering a wide open valley. The trail follows a glacial stream (Rani Nallah), which begins further up the mountains (at Hampta Pass). Since this is the first time going up the mountain, there may be patches of snow on the trail early in the season.
The campsite at Chika is in a large meadow surrounded by tall ridges. This short trek allows the participants to acclimatise to the increasing elevation of the hike. Most people use the evening to stretch and receive an orientation and safety briefing about crossing the mountain passes that lie ahead on the trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chika to Balu Ka Ghera
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 5–6 kilometers, 4-5 hrs Altitude Gain:
10,100 ft to 12,400 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The trail from the beginning to end of this hike follows the Hampta River steadily uphill. The valley narrow and wooded at first becomes much wider along the way as well as the trees get smaller in height. There will be several river crossings during the course of the trek, and depending on the time of year of the crossing, you may have to watch your step carefully & have assistance from your trekking leader to assist you.
As the trek continues up into higher elevations, the ground surface becomes much rougher & rockier than what you had encountered lower down on the trek. During early June to late July, there will most likely be snow in many areas. As you are climbing higher l will see many surrounding mountains that now become clearly visible while at the same time the size of the valley you are climbing is becoming much clearer as well.
Balu Ka Ghera means "Bed of Sand" and is a level camp that is located in a very large flat area in a high-altitude basin that is completely surrounded by steep-walled mountains. Balu Ka Ghera has an incredibly beautiful view of the road to Hampta Pass. This evening will be your last night in the valley, and you will receive a detailed explanation of what will happen the next morning on our summit and some high altitude education as well.

itinerary.title: Trek from Balu Ka Ghera to Hampta Pass to Shea Goru
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 8-9 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude Gain & Loss:
12,400 ft to 14,100 ft to 12,900 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
This day is the most challenging and rewarding of the trip. The climb up to Hamta Pass has a continual uphill climb, sometimes over rock and often through snow fields (early in season) to reach Hamta Pass. The last part of the route up to Hamta Pass is usually quite steep and requires a careful pace to conserve energy. Once at the summit (14,100') the trekker will experience a unique change in the landscape: on one side of the summit lies the lush green of the Kullu Valley, and on the other side is the stark, rocky, barren mountains of Lahlul Valley. The contrast between the two valleys is dramatic and one of the most notable characteristics of this trek.
Having spent some time at the summit resting and taking photos, the trek resumes its descent to Shea Goru, which is through steep terrain and often across snow-covered areas. The campsite at Shea Goru is in the cold desert region of Lahaul Valley, and has minimal vegetation.

itinerary.title: Trek from Shea Goru to Chatru – Drive to Chandratal (Optional)
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 6–7 km, 5-6 hrs Drive (optional):
Approximately 50 km round trip Altitude Loss:
12,900 ft to 11,000 ft Accommodation:
Alpine tent Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The route for today closely follows the course taken by the Chandra River and continues along a wide-open area (similar to parts of Lahaul), with a down hill section that gradually declines but will involve a lot of traversing/stepping on unstable stones, loose rocks and across piles of river round rocks, as well as many river beds.
Chatru is a small village on the Manali - Spiti road. It is the junction for all roadways connecting Lahaul, Spiti and Kullu to each other. Weather and road/road conditions permitting, a drive to Chandratal Lake (Moon Lake) to experience the unique beauty created by the contrast of the lake’s perfect crescent form and crystal-clear blue-green waters contrasted against the harshness of the surrounding mountains. After exploring the lake, the group will return to the campsite near Chatru.

itinerary.title: Drive from Chatru to Manali
itinerary.description:
Drive Distance: 85 kilometres, 4-5 hrs Altitude Loss:
11,000 feet to 6,700 feet After breakfast, we will make our way back to Manali on the same road we used to get to Lahaul, following the Chandra River. There will be many beautiful views along this high mountain road and you will see a lot of different terrains, including barren and rugged landscapes before returning.
As you lose altitude, you will find that vegetation slowly comes back and the air is noticeably cleaner (more oxygen). When you reach Manali, your trek is completed, and you will be able to disperse and make arrangements for onward travel.
Difficulty Level of Hampta Pass Trek Himachal Pradesh
The trek through Hampta Pass is moderately challenging. It is suitable for beginners who are fit or experienced. You will reach a maximum altitude of about 14,100 ft. The trek is not technical but the high-altitude pass can make it challenging. Long hours in walking and weather conditions can increase the difficulty level. The changing terrain makes this trek moderately difficult.
The trail starts with easy forest paths and meadows. These sections near Jobra and Chika are easy. The climb gets steeper as you move toward Balu Ka Ghera. The trail becomes rocky and steep. The ascent increases the Hampta Pass trek difficulty. You might find snow early in the season. The descent toward the Shea Goru is tricky. It is often steep with loose rock or snow. The weather changes rapidly in this region. This adds to the difficulty. Daytime temperatures are comfortable from June to September. Mornings and nights are cold. Temperatures at high camps can drop to 0 or 5 degrees Celsius. It can be windy near the pass. The high altitude and changing terrain can make it moderately challenging. With proper preparation and a reasonable level of fitness, the Hampta Pass Trek is manageable for most beginners. While certain sections can feel demanding, the gradual ascent, well-defined trail, and rewarding scenery make it an excellent cho

itinerary.title: Drive from Shimla to Janglik
itinerary.description:
Drive Distance: 150 km, 7-8 hours Altitude Gain:
6,726 ft to 9,415 ft Accommodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Dinner
The base camp of Buran Ghati is Janglik, located approximately 150km from Shimla. It as an old Himalayan village with limited Airtel network.
The road from Shimla to Janglik is scenic with its winding roads, wheat fields, Himachali houses. The flowing Pabbar river joins you at Rohru. Rohru is the last place where you can find an ATM. Just after Chirgaon, you take a left turn to climb a dirt track. Two hours later you reach Tangnu and its pine forests. Driving past a police check post and a broken bridge, the car will drop you at Diude. The walk to Janglik from Diude is short.

itinerary.title: Trek from Janglik to Dayara Thatch
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 6-7 km, 5-6 hours Altitude Gain:
9,415 ft to 11,115 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
You get to witness Himachali wooden architecture as you pass through the village. The houses made of Deodar wood have artistic carvings and fascinating roofs. Within 15 minutes, you will leave the village behind.
You will find yourself on a steep trail that leads to an oak and pine forest. The path with will become gradual as you go deeper into the woods.
The trees clear unexpectedly to reveal the massive expanse of Dayara. Your heart will be filled with delight on seeing a vast, undulating green meadow with thousands of yellow wildflowers.
The meadow has small hills on one side a gorge on the other. In the middle, you will see horses galloping with abandon among herds of sheep. Spend the evening with local Himalayan shepherds. They will speak to you humorously of a difficult but content life in the mountains.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dayara Thatch to Litham
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 6-7 km, 5-6 hours Altitude Gain:
11,115 ft to 11,485 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
We recommend waking up early to witness the sunrise too. The interplay of yellow rays and grey shadows over a large carpet of grass will leave you mesmerized. If you thought you had seen all that you possibly could of meadows, you are wrong. Today you will walk across meadow after meadow with forests interspersed between them. The first forest you will cross is again of pine, followed by silver birch i.e. bhoj. The bark of the bhoj tree was used as paper in ancient times.
The trail from Dayara to Litham is almost a gentle descent throughout with multiple streams along the way. You will see Guna Pass among the now visible snow-capped Dhauladhar range. Once you hop over the Chandranahan stream, you reach the Litham campsite. Litham too has a charm at par with Dayara. To your front are the cliffs that hide Buran Pass. On your left you can see the mouth of the Chandranahan waterfall. On your right is the Pabbar river, musically flowing before the mountain range that hides the Rupin valley.
You get to spend two days at this scenic campsite, since one day is an excursion to Chandranahan lake.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation - Visit Chandranahan Lake
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 5-6 km, 4-5 hours Altitude Gain:
11,485 ft to 14,020 ft and back to 11,485 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Today you visit Chandranahan lake – the source of the river you are camping by and drive along on your way to Janglik. The lake is considered sacred because as per mythology, the moon on Lord Shiva’s head took a dip in this lake. Hence the name.
You begin the day early to get back to Litham by lunch time. It will be a strenuous day because of a steep ascent and descent. But the landscape you witness is worth the effort.
You cross the stream you hopped over on the way to Litham and make our way towards the waterfall. A shepherd’s trail will take you to ridge top. The waterfall’s snout is marked by charmingly set-up stone cairns. The lake is another hour’s walk on snow patches from here.
Chandrahan is a glacial lake perennially fed by snow. It remains frozen for most part of the year. Though the lake is small, it’s bowl-like setting between flanking mountains against a blue sky makes its size irrelevant.

itinerary.title: Trek from Litham to Dhunda
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 4-5 km, 4-5 hours Altitude Gain:
11,485 ft to 13,425 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Litham is the last meadow on this trek. You now make your way to the alpine high-altitude campsite of Dhunda. The green grass will give way to grey rocks and patches of ice.
The Dhauladhar range continues accompanying you over a well-marked trail, as does the Pabbar. But the river is flowing much faster now. As you walk along its left bank, you reach a U-shaped gorge-like valley. Here, you finally see Buran Ghati for the first time on your left.
Dhunda at 13,300 feet is set against the feet of the Pass. Unlike your first colourful campsites, this one is surrounded completely by snow during summer. The altitude and the anticipation of the Pass crossing will fill you with excitement.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dhunda to Munirang/River Campsite via Buran Pass
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 8 km, 9-10 hours Altitude Gain:
13,425 ft to 15,000 ft to 10, 745 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Today you will trek for almost 10 hours which will be both ascending and descending. In the absence of snow during autumn, the Pass is not difficult to time. In summer, you begin the climb to the Pass a little after midnight. This is because snow softens during the day, making it difficult to walk.
From the narrow ledge at the top of Buran Pass at 15,000 feet, you get a panoramic view of the Kinner-Kailash peaks. Snow-covered mountains at day-break among swirling mist is a sight that will remain with you for the rest of your life.
You will rappel down the first 100 metres of an almost vertical snow wall into the Kinnaur valley. After that, there are 4-5 patches of snow over which you can just slide down!
The descent from Buran Ghati is very quick, with you losing 3,000 feet of altitude in just 2 hours. Once out of the snow line, you will once again be greeted by flowers and shrubs.

itinerary.title: Trek from Munirang/River Campsite to Barua
itinerary.description:
Trek Distance: 6-7 km, 5-6 hours Drive Distance:
213 km, 6-7 hours Altitude Gain:
10,725 ft to 7,725 ft to 6,726 ft Meals:
Breakfast
The last day of the trek is a full descent. You will walk through receding trees that give way to diverse Himalayan vegetation. After an hour and a half, you will reach a bridge crossing over a large stream. Soon you will spot trees of apricot, pears and peaches.
An hour later, you will see apple orchards and civilization. You would have entered Barua village through an arch. You will smile at villagers going about their usual day of farming or tending to cattle. Some of them might strike up a conversation and invite you for a cup of tea.
From the heart of the village, the descent becomes even more rapid. Within half an hour you reach the road bridge over Barua Khud.
If you want to travel on your own, you can get a vehicle to Karcham junction which is 3km ahead. From this junction you can go either to Rekong Peo or Sangla. Sangla which is 17km away from Karcham is the largest village in the Baspa valley. In fact, Baspa Valley is also called Sangla valley. You could visit attractions close to Sangla like Kamru, Chansu, Basteri, Rakcham, Chitkul village and Ranikanda meadows. Or you can make your way back to Shimla, the most loved hill station in India with its colonial buildings, rhododendrons, oaks and firs.
As you settle back into everyday life, make sure to read our complete guide on how to recover after a Himalayan trek to properly heal muscle soreness and rehydrate.
Difficulty Level of Buran Ghati Trek
The difficulty level of Buran Ghati is rated moderate to difficult. The highest point of the trek is 4,550 m and the trail is around 38 km long, passing through diverse terrains. The trek takes one week (7-8 days) to complete. It is suitable for trekkers who have some high-altitude trekking experience or prior trekking experience in Himachal Pradesh.
The trek starts in the lush green meadows and pine, oak and rhododendron forests of

itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Agoda
itinerary.description:
Drive: 160 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude Gain:
2,100 ft to 7,200 ft Accomodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Dinner
We begin our journey from Dehradun and drive through the scenic hill towns of Mussoorie, Suwakholi, Chinyalisaur, Dharasu Bend, and Uttarkashi before reaching Agoda Village, the base camp for the Dodital Trek. The drive offers spectacular views of the Garhwal Himalayas, winding mountain roads, terraced fields, pine forests, and the beautiful Bhagirathi River, making the journey as enjoyable as the trek itself.
Agoda is a peaceful traditional Garhwali village surrounded by dense forests and mountain landscapes. The village is known for its warm hospitality, stone houses, and terraced farms, offering trekkers a glimpse into the simple lifestyle of the Himalayan communities. It serves as the perfect place to relax and acclimatize before beginning the trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Agoda to Manjhi
itinerary.description:
Trek: 10 km, 5-6 hrs Altitude Gain:
7,200 ft to 9,433 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, the Dodital Trek begins from Agoda Village. The trail gradually ascends through dense forests of oak, deodar, pine, and rhododendron, offering a peaceful walk surrounded by the sights and sounds of the Himalayas. Along the way, you'll cross sparkling mountain streams, wooden bridges, and small clearings that provide beautiful views of the surrounding valleys.
As you gain altitude, the fresh mountain air and lush greenery make the trek both refreshing and enjoyable. The route is well-marked with a steady ascent, making it suitable for beginners with a reasonable level of fitness.
After trekking for about 10 km, you reach Manjhi, a picturesque campsite nestled beside a mountain stream. Surrounded by dense forests and towering peaks, Manjhi is an ideal place to relax and enjoy the peaceful Himalayan wilderness. Spend the evening soaking in the tranquil surroundings before an overnight stay at the campsite.

itinerary.title: Trek from Manjhi to Dodital Lake
itinerary.description:
Trek: 6 km, 3-4 hrs Altitude Gain:
9,433 ft to 10,807 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, continue your journey from Manjhi to the beautiful Dodital Lake, the highlight of the trek. The trail gradually climbs through dense forests of oak, deodar, and rhododendron, with the soothing sound of mountain streams accompanying you along the way. The peaceful surroundings and fresh Himalayan air make this section of the trek especially enjoyable.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dodital Lake to Darwa Top and Back
itinerary.description:
Trek: 12 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude Gain & Loss:
10,807 ft to 13,600 ft, to 10,807 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Start your day early with a hearty breakfast before trekking towards Darwa Top (Darwa Pass), one of the most scenic viewpoints on the Dodital Trek. The trail climbs steadily through alpine meadows, rocky sections, and open mountain slopes, rewarding trekkers with increasingly spectacular views as they gain altitude.
After trekking for approximately 6 km, you reach Darwa Top, situated at an altitude of about 13,600 ft (4,150 m). From here, you'll be treated to breathtaking panoramic views of some of the Garhwal Himalayas' most iconic peaks, including Bandarpunch, Swargarohini, Black Peak (Kala Nag), and Draupadi Ka Danda. During the summer months, the surrounding meadows are dotted with colourful wildflowers, making this one of the most picturesque spots on the trek.
Take some time to soak in the stunning scenery, capture memorable photographs, and enjoy the peaceful mountain atmosphere before beginning the descent. Retrace your steps back to Dodital Lake, where you can relax by the lakeside and spend another peaceful night surrounded by the tranquil beauty of the Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dodital Lake to Agoda
itinerary.description:
Trek: 16 km, 6-7 hrs Altitude Loss:
10,807 ft to 7,200 ft Accomodation:
Guesthouse/Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After enjoying a peaceful morning by Dodital Lake, begin your descent towards Agoda Village. The return journey follows the same scenic trail through dense forests of oak, deodar, and rhododendron, offering another opportunity to admire the beauty of the Garhwal Himalayas. The downhill trail is comfortable and allows you to appreciate the peaceful surroundings at a relaxed pace. Along the way, you'll enjoy beautiful views of the forested valleys and may even spot a few Himalayan birds and wildlife hidden among the trees.

itinerary.title: Drive from Agoda to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Drive: 160 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude Loss:
7,200 ft to 2,100 ft Meals:
Breakfast
After breakfast, bid farewell to the peaceful Himalayan village of Agoda and begin your drive back to Dehradun. Enjoy the changing landscapes as you descend from the Garhwal Himalayas, making a few stops along the way to relax and capture the last glimpses of the mountains. The drive provides a perfect opportunity to reflect on the memorable experiences of the Dodital Trek.
Difficulty Level of Dodital Trek Uttarakhand
The Dodital Trek is an easy-to-moderate trek up to the lake and a moderate trek with the Darwa Top day, making it ideal for beginners with good fitness as well as experienced trekkers. The trail is well-marked and passes through dense forests, mountain streams, and traditional Himalayan villages, with gradual ascents and a few moderately steep sections. The trek covers approximately 44 km (round trip, including the Darwa Top day) over 4 trekking days, with 6–16 km of walking per day. The optional climb to Darwa Pass is steeper and more challenging, while the trek to Dodital Lake itself remains comfortable for most trekkers.
Overall, if you can walk for several hours a day with a backpack, the Dodital Trek is a rewarding and enjoyable Himalayan adventure suitable for families, first-time trekkers, and nature lovers.
Dodital Trek – A Beginner-Friendly Adventure in Uttarakhand
The Dodital Trek is one of the best beginner-friendly treks in Uttarakhand. With its well-defined forest trails, gradual ascent, and moderate altitude, it is an excellent choice for first-time trekkers and families. Along the way, you'll walk through dense oak and rhododendron forests, cross sparkling mountain streams, visit traditional Garhwali villages like Agoda, and finally reach the serene Dodital Lake, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Ganesha. The trek offers stunning Himalayan scenery without being overly demanding, making it a perfect introduction to trekking in the Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Pantwari and Trek to Kathain Campsite
itinerary.description:
Drive: 90 km, 3-4 hrs Trek:
4-5 km Altitude Gain: 1,480 ft to 7,506 ft Meals:
Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Your journey to the Nag Tibba Trek begins with a scenic drive from Dehradun to Pantwari, a small Himalayan village and the starting point of the trek. After reaching Pantwari, begin the trek towards Kathian Campsite. The trail gradually ascends through dense oak and rhododendron forests, traditional villages, and open meadows. Along the way, you can enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and experience the peaceful atmosphere of the lower Himalayas. Upon reaching the campsite, relax amidst the serene forest surroundings and witness a beautiful sunset over the mountains.

itinerary.title: Trek from Kathain Campsite to Pantwari via Nag Tibba Top and Drive Back to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Trek: 9.3 km Drive: 85 km, 3 to 4 hrs Altitude Gain & Loss:
7,506 ft to 9,915 ft to 1,480 ft Meals:
Breakfast + Lunch
Wake up early and begin the climb towards Nag Tibba Top, the highest point of the trek at an altitude of 9,915 ft. The trail passes through dense forests and open ridges before rewarding trekkers with breathtaking panoramic views.
Spend some time at the summit soaking in the spectacular scenery and capturing memorable photographs. After enjoying the views, start the descent towards Pantwari village. Upon reaching Pantwari, board your vehicle and drive back to Dehradun.
Difficulty Level of Nag Tibba Trek Uttarakhand
The Nag Tibba Trek is considered an easy to moderate trek, making it one of the best choices for beginners and first-time trekkers in the Himalayas. The trail is well-marked, safe, and does not involve any technical climbing, which makes the trek comfortable for most people with basic fitness. The trek includes gradual ascents through forests, open ridges, and village trails. While there are a few steep sections near the summit, they are short and manageable with slow and steady walking. Most beginners are able to complete the trek without much difficulty.
During winter, the difficulty level can increase slightly because of snow on the trail. Walking on snow may feel tiring for first-time trekkers, but the route still remains safe and achievable with proper trekking shoes and warm clothing. The trek is suitable for beginners, families, solo travelers, children with good fitness, and anyone looking for a peaceful weekend adventure in Uttarakhand.

Families with children.
People with reasonable fitness.
Who Should Avoid Nag Tibba Trek?
