itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Auli/Joshimath
itinerary.description:
Drive: 295 km, 8-9 hrs Altitude:
2,100 ft (640 m) – 6,150 ft (1,875 m)
Accommodation: Hotel/Resort
Meals: Dinner
A long yet scenic drive crosses major towns of Uttarakhand before we reach our destination of the day, Auli, Joshimath, after crossing some of the Prayags. We start early from Dehradun to reach Joshimath by late afternoon. Crossing Rishikesh, Devprayag, which happens to be the final prayag (confluence) between Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers, and consecutively Srinagar, we follow along the Alaknanda river the entire time. The distance from Dehradun to Karanprayag is 210 km which takes 7 hours to complete. We arrive at Karanprayag, which is one of the Panch (five) Prayag (confluence), where Alaknanda meets Pindar river. We continue to Auli or Joshimath and check into hotel by evening. We can explore around the town in the evening.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Govindghat & Trek to Ghangaria
itinerary.description:
Drive: 14 km, 45 min Trek:
11 km, 5-6 hrs Altitude: 6,150 ft (1,875 m) – 10,003 ft (3,049 m)
Accommodation: Camps/Guest House
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Post breakfast, we check out of the hotel and head towards Govindghat. The drive ahead to Govindghat takes about 45 minutes from where we switch vehicles and drive towards Pulna. From Pulna, we start trekking towards Ghangaria. The distance to be covered on this day is 11 km, which takes about 5-6 hours to complete. While trekking towards Ghangaria, the path is laid, which makes the trek relatively easier. However a continuous elevation may become strenuous. The trek route till Ghangaria is dotted with small dhabas, pilgrims heading towards Hemkund Sahib and a ferocious outlet of the river Pushapavati. You are also going to be surrounded by the forest the entire route, which reduces the heat and makes the hike pleasant. The route till Ghangaria is a busy one as it is also the route to Hemkund Sahib. You will spot helicopters often if the weather is clear and innumerable spots to eat. Before reaching the actual village of Ghangaria, you will hit the camps. We check into our hotel and spend the rest of the evening in leisure.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghangaria to Valley of Flowers and back to Ghangaria
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7.5 km, 6 hrs Altitude:
10,003 ft to 11,550 ft to 10,003 ft Accommodation:
Camps/Guest House
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After breakfast, we begin our trek towards the famous Valley of Flowers National Park. The distance from Ghangaria to the Valley of Flowers is around 3.7 km and takes approximately 2 to 3 hours to reach, depending on the pace. The trail gradually ascends through dense forests, wooden bridges, and rocky mountain paths alongside the beautiful Pushpawati River.
As we enter the Valley of Flowers, the landscape transforms into a breathtaking expanse of colorful alpine meadows surrounded by towering Himalayan peaks. During the blooming season, the valley is carpeted with countless varieties of wildflowers, creating one of the most spectacular natural sights in the Himalayas. The valley is also home to several streams, waterfalls, and rare Himalayan flora that make every step of the journey memorable.
After exploring the valley and spending quality time amidst nature, we begin our return journey to Ghangaria via the same route. Upon reaching Ghangaria, we relax and unwind after a memorable day in the Valley of Flowers. The evening is free, allowing trekkers to enjoy the serene surroundings.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib and back to Ghangaria
itinerary.description:
Trek: 12 km, 6-7 hrs Altitude:
10,003 ft (3,049 m) – 15,200 ft (4,632 m) – 10,003 ft (3,049 m)
Accommodation: Camps/Guest House
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
The next day we embark on a pilgrimage journey. Post breakfast, we start trekking towards Hemkund Sahib. The distance from Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib is about 6 km. The path, again, is well laid and dotted with small eating joints; which is not the case while you trek towards the Valley. The path to Hemkund sahib is also blessed with flowers that you may have seen in the Valley of flowers. The hike to Hemkund Sahib is challenging yet magnificent. You can see pilgrims all motivated to reach the gurudwara, some even complete the journey barefoot. On reaching Hemkund Sahib, you can enter the gurudwara and then enjoy some ready to eat hot Halwa and chai. You can also sit by the Sarovar for a while and enjoy the views around. After spending an hour at gurudwara, we head back towards Ghangaria taking the same route. After reaching Ghangaria, we rest for a while and spend the evening in leisure.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghangaria to Govindghat, drive to Badrinath (38 km) & return to Joshimath (42 km)
itinerary.description:
Trek: 11 km, 5 hrs Drive:
147 km, 5-6 hrs Altitude:
10,003 ft (3,049 m) – 6,150 ft (1,875 m)
Accommodation: Hotel
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After an early breakfast, begin your descent from Ghangaria. From Govindghat, drive to the sacred town of Badrinath, one of the holiest pilgrimage destinations in India. Visit the revered Badrinath Temple and seek blessings before exploring Mana Village, the last Indian village near the Indo-Tibetan border, known for its mythological significance and breathtaking Himalayan views. Later, continue your drive to Joshimath, where you will check into a comfortable guest house for an overnight stay, marking the perfect end to a day filled with natural beauty, culture, and spirituality.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Drive: 210 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude:
6,150 ft (1,875 m) – 2,100 ft (640 m)
Meals: Breakfast
After breakfast, begin your scenic drive from Joshimath to Dehradun, covering approximately 295 km through the beautiful Garhwal Himalayas. The journey follows the Alaknanda River, passing charming mountain towns, deep valleys, and famous river confluences that make the route as memorable as the trek itself. Arrive in Dehradun or Rishikesh by evening with unforgettable memories of the Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib, and the majestic Himalayan landscapes, bringing your incredible adventure to a fulfilling close.
What is the difficulty level of Valley of Flowers Trek?
The Valley of Flowers Uttarakhand trek is considered moderately difficult. It involves a gradual ascent through mountainous terrain and requires a decent level of physical fitness. The trail can be steep and uneven at times, requiring careful footing. However, with proper preparation, including regular exercise and acclimatization, most moderately fit individuals can complete the trek comfortably. It is advisable to consult with local guides and carry essential trekking gear to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience.
One of the reasons why the Valley of Flowers Trek is popular among beginners is that it does not involve any technical climbing or mountaineering skills. The trail is well-defined and remains accessible throughout the trekking season. Trekkers should be prepared for long walking hours, changing weather conditions, and high-altitude trekking.
Valley of Flowers - Where the Himalayas Bloom
The Valley of Flowers Trek is one of the most beautiful Himalayan adventures in Uttarakhand. This trek is famous for its alpine meadows, rare wildflowers, and breathtaking mountain scenery. The trek comes alive during the monsoon season. Surrounded by snow-capped peaks, waterfalls, and pristine landscapes, the Valley of Flowers offers a magical trekking experience.
Who Should Do Valley of Flower Trek?
Nature lovers who w

itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description:
Drive: 190 km, 8 hrs Altitude Gain:
1,480 ft – 6,725 ft Accommodation:
Cottages/ Guest House
Meals: Dinner
Himalaya Shelter Guest House At Sankri
We start the journey early from Dehradun and drive initially to the famous hill station of Mussoorie. After just over 100 km, we pass close to the temple of Lakhamandal. According to locals, Duryodhana of the epic Mahabharata conspired to burn the Lakshagriha house of the Pandavas in this area. Damta, Purola, Mori and Netwar are some of the other villages on the route. We follow the river Yamuna upstream.
The river Kamal Ganga merges with Yamuna near Naugaon and accompanies us till Purola. Purola is the last big settlement on the route with a large market. So, it is recommended that the trekkers can buy anything they might have missed out by Purola itself. It also is the last village where most of the mobile networks work.
The drive after Purola is through a beautiful forest of pine trees. In some distance, on top of a hill we can see the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya overlooking the valley. From near the village of Mori, the river Tons flows beside us till about Netwar. The fall in temperature can be felt from here. We officially enter Govind Pashu Vihar Wildlife Sanctuary after we cross a check post at Netwar. It can be considered the southern gateway to the sanctuary as most of the treks across the region are accessed from here onwards.
The northern border of the sanctuary merges into Himachal Pradesh. Close to here, the rivers of Rupin and Supin merge to form Tons, which is the largest tributary of Yamuna and in fact larger than Yamuna itself, in terms of volume of flow. The peak of Kedarkantha can be seen from various points along the way from here.
We reach Sankri by early evening. It is a small village with a central market lined with a few shops. The village has numerous apple orchards which are harvested starting from late summer. The market area is new compared to the old village area, a part of which is known as ‘S

itinerary.title: Drive from Sankri to Gangad and Trek to Chilurgad
itinerary.description:
Drive: 22 km, 1-1.5 hrs Trek:
4-5 km, 5 hrs Altitude Gain:
6,725 ft – 8,270 ft Accommodation:
Homestay
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Har Ki Dun Walking Trail
Since the journey is long, we start as early as we can in the morning. After breakfast, we board an SUV and drive through a forest road. The drive is quite bumpy. The vehicle crosses one or two streams on the way. We reach Gangad in about an hour.
The fragrance of cedar trees can be felt around Gangad. Sometimes during winters, or especially during periods with rather heavy spells of rain, the road to Gangad may be too dangerous for vehicles, as streams run across the road and thus one may be required to walk bit more.
We walk close to the river Supin gushing through rapids. Under the shade of walnut, pine, and cedar trees, the walk is quite pleasant. In autumn we can often find walnuts lying around. One must avoid “bichchu ghas” which literally translates to ‘scorpion grass’. A slight touch can give us a stinging sensation which lasts for about twenty to thirty minutes. This herb is also cooked as a vegetable and eaten. Often the passing villagers greet us on the way. High up above on the true left, we get to see the village of Datmer. It is lined by a series of step farms. The farms have the bright red colored Cholai growing from late monsoon to early autumn.
It is possible to come across a yellow-throated marten in the forests of this area. We can also find edible fruits of seabuckthorn. They are orange in color and grow in bunches. Also, known as ‘leh berries’, the juicy and sour fruits are a rich source of Vitamin C. We continue our trek and soon we reach the secluded campsite at Puani Garat.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chilurgad to Kalkatidhar via Osla
itinerary.description:
Trek: 5-6 km, 4-5 hrs Altitude:
8,270 ft – 10,830 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Har Ki Dun Valley In Uttarakhand
Today we start the day by heading up towards Osla village, which is located on a sloping spur about a hundred meters above the river Supin. The initial trail to Osla is the steepest section along the entire trek and can take 30-40 mins to cover. The landscape surrounding Osla is full of terraced farms. The colors of these lands differ in every season. The red farms of Cholai (Amaranth) look amazing and can be seen from the late monsoon.
This grain is a powerhouse with its rich nutritional values and a favorite among the locals. Apart from these Kidney beans in wide varieties are cultivated in the area. Osla is the last village on the route to Har ki Dun. From Osla the trail gradually rises higher and we cross a few fields, while the river can be seen far below. We come across a temple some distance below the trail towards the right. We pass through bushes of flowers like orchids, fleece flowers and sunflowers.
The journey today is rather short, which gives the opportunity to acclimatize to the high altitude and prepare for the next days journey. We can take a breather basking in the sun at the beautiful campsite of Kalkatidhar. The ban to camp at Har Ki Dun has had a rather positive outlook to the trekking itinerary, as it allows for more comfort & at the same time preserves the natural beauty of Har Ki Dun.

itinerary.title: Trek form Kalkatidhar to Har ki Dun & Marinda Tal, return to Boslo
itinerary.description:
Trek: 10.5 km, 6-7 hrs Altitude:
9,977 ft to 11,600 ft to 10,412 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Marinda Tal In Har Ki Dun Valley
The day’s trek can be considered to be rather long as we today visit Har Ki Dun and Marinda Tal, a small lake formation due to the obstructing boulder across the river stream, which lies 2 KM further ahead of Har Ki Dun. As we start the trek, at a short distance a hidden and roaring waterfall is encountered with a small tea shop beside the waterfall.
The ascending path offers stunning views above the confluence of the Supin and Ruinsara rivers. From here, you can admire the snow-clad peaks of Ruinsara Valley, notably Black Peak, the highest in the area. To the north, the Har Ki Dun valley unfolds in the distance, with a clear view of the Forest hut. Continuing higher on the right of the river, you enter a final stretch through a beautiful forest. Emerging from the woods, you arrive at Har Ki Dun’s main camping area, nestled beside a babbling stream. This panoramic spot sits at the junction of two valleys, one originating from Jaundhar Glacier and the other beyond Hata Glacier, offering a breathtaking natural spectacle.
Higher up towards the North we can spot the Forest Rest House, while the wood-crafted GMVN guest house lies further up in the distance. The Har ki Dun peak stands tall right in front of us behind the Forest Rest House. Towards its left, Hata peak which is usually snow-covered can be seen. The minor ridge to our right, lined with a few scattered Himalayan birch trees Bhojpatra separates us from the massive Har Ki Dun valley that goes up all the way to the base of Swargarohini Peak. The paper-like bark of these trees was used in ancient times to write religious scriptures.
The vast open meadows following the course of the Supin River can be explored. Further ahead of the meadows one can walk among the forests of Bhojpatra trees (Himalayan birch) or get a closer glimpse of the

itinerary.title: Trek from Boslo to Devsu Thatch
itinerary.description:
Trek: 5.1 km, 4-5 hrs Altitude Loss:
10,502 ft to 9,878 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Temple In Osla Village On Har Ki Dun Trek Route
The journey back to Osla is an easy walk. On the route we come across a good view of the trail all the way to Osla and see the valley descend towards Taluka, around the curve of the ridge where the two streams comng from Har Ki Dun and Ruinsara respectively, converge. A little short of this intersection we can get a glimpse of a trail to our left marked by a sight of a bridge down over the stream.
This trail goes to join the trail to Ruinsara lake and is rarely taken. After reaching Osla, one can roam about in the village, talk to locals and soak in the Garhwali culture. We continue our journey from here to our earlier campsite of Puani Garat where we can spend time basking in the sun.

itinerary.title: Trek from Devsu Thatch to Gangad and Drive to Sankri
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7-8 km, 5-6 hrs Drive: 20 km, 1-1.5 hrs Altitude Loss:
9,878 ft to 7,709 ft to 8,265 ft Accommodation:
Cottages/Guest House
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Seema Osla Village In Har Ki Dun Valley
Early in the morning, post breakfast we set out from this beautiful abode as we start trekking through the same trail we trekked along on Day 1, towards Taluka. Although the views seem different as the perspective changes significantly trekking downhill. The walk takes lesser time than before and is enjoyable. We walk to the true left of the River Supin until we finally arrive at Taluka, from where a vehicle takes us back to Sankri. We retire for the day in camp alongside the river or in a guest house in Sankri.

itinerary.title: Drive from Sankri to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Distance: 190 km, 8 hrs Meals:
Breakfast
Journey Ends: Arrive in Dehradun between 5 and 7 PM
View From Homestay In Sankri
The trek to Har ki Dun concludes today as we leave Sankri. The drive up to Mori through the unique lesser-touched regions is still amazing. The stretch right after crossing Mori town is still the prettiest along the entire journey, albeit the new hydel project has put the fragile environs at increased risk in this area. Rafting and Kayaking which was earlier prevalent here are no longer feasible. Regardless the beauty of the region remains to a significant degree. After crossing the towns and finally Kempty-Mussoorie, we reach Dehradun by late afternoon or early evening.
After reaching Dehradun near the railway station in the evening, your memorable alpine journey with our team officially concludes. To safely transition back to your daily routine, manage muscle soreness, and handle post-trek fatigue effectively, review our complete post-trek recovery guide .
Difficulty Level Har Ki Dun Trek Valley Uttarakhand
Har Ki Dun is considered a moderate level trek in terms of difficulty. The trail follows a well-laid path all the way to the Har Ki Dun valley, a route that the native people of the valley have used for many years. The total distance to the last village of the Har Ki Dun valley, Osla, is 14 km from the starting point of the trek. Some sections have minor steepness, and the final stretch of about 0.5 km is notably steep. During the first day of the trek, we covered only around 10 km, leaving the steep section for the second day. Overall, the trail is gradual all the way to the valley. The distance from the last village to the Har Ki Dun valley is another 11 km. Thus, the total distance of 25 km is covered in 3 days. On the third day, we go further to Marinda Tal, which is 2.5 km ahead of Har Ki Dun. The approximate walking distances for each day are as follows: An additional two days of driving to Sankri and back to Dehradun complete the enti

itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description:
Drive: 190 km, 8 hrs Altitude Gain:
1,480 ft – 6,725 ft Accommodation:
Cottages/Guest House
Meals: Dinner
Our journey begins from Dehradun, making it a good option for people looking for treks near Delhi. Driving alongside the Tons River and passing villages in Uttarakhand like Damta, Purola, Mori, and Netwar, we will reach the base camp Sankri. There is no network in this village, letting us take in the sight of the sun gloriously setting over the surrounding Greater Himalayan peaks without any distractions. We will be accommodated in hotels or homestays here.

itinerary.title: Drive from Sankri to Gangad and Trek to Seema
itinerary.description:
Drive: 22 km, 1-1.5 hrs Trek:
4-5 km, 4-5 hrs Altitude Gain:
6,725 ft to 8,202 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Your journey begins with a scenic drive from Sankri to Gangad, the last motorable village on this route. From Gangad, the trek to Seema starts on a well-defined trail that follows the crystal-clear Supin River. The path gradually ascends through thick forests of pine, deodar, walnut, and oak, offering plenty of shade and a refreshing mountain atmosphere.
By late afternoon, you'll arrive at Seema Camp, a peaceful campsite surrounded by towering conifer forests and majestic Himalayan peaks. Spend the evening relaxing in the tranquil surroundings, enjoy a warm dinner, and settle into your alpine tent for your first night in the mountains, preparing for the exciting days ahead.

itinerary.title: Trek from Seema to Waterfall Campsite
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7 km, 5-6 hrs Altitude Gain:
8,202 ft to 10,500 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Wake up to the crisp mountain air and enjoy a hearty breakfast before beginning your trek from Devsu Camp to Waterfall Campsite. Today's trail takes you deeper into the untouched wilderness of the Rupin Valley, where every turn reveals a new Himalayan landscape.
The route gradually climbs through dense forests of pine, deodar, and birch before opening into lush alpine meadows dotted with seasonal wildflowers. The soothing sound of the Rupin River accompanies you for much of the journey, while wooden bridges and small streams add to the charm of the trek. As you gain altitude, the valley becomes narrower, and the surrounding snow-clad peaks begin to dominate the skyline.
One of the highlights of the day is reaching the spectacular Waterfall Campsite, named after the cascading waterfall that tumbles down the rocky cliffs nearby. The sight of crystal-clear water crashing into the valley creates a peaceful and unforgettable setting. This campsite is one of the most scenic stops on the trek, offering incredible views of towering mountains and lush green slopes.

itinerary.title: Trek from Waterfall Campsite to Ruinsara Lake
itinerary.description:
Trek: 6 km, 5-6 hrs Altitude Gain:
10,600 ft to 12,250 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Start your day early with a nourishing breakfast as you set out for one of the most rewarding days of the trek. The trail gradually climbs through alpine meadows and rocky terrain, with magnificent views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks accompanying you throughout the journey.
After a steady ascent, you'll arrive at the breathtaking Ruinsara Lake, a pristine high-altitude lake nestled amidst towering mountains. Surrounded by lush meadows and snow-capped peaks, the emerald-green lake offers a peaceful setting that makes it one of the highlights of the trek. Take some time to soak in the scenery, capture photographs, and enjoy the serenity of this untouched Himalayan gem.
By late afternoon, you'll reach the basecamp, a beautiful campsite surrounded by open meadows and rugged mountain scenery. Relax after the day's adventure, enjoy a hot dinner, and spend the night in your alpine tent, surrounded by the peaceful wilderness of the Garhwal Himalayas, ready for the challenging ascent to come.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ruinsara Lake to Odari
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7 km, 5 hrs Altitude Gain:
12,250 ft to 13,239 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After an early breakfast, begin your trek from Ruinsara Lake to Odari, gradually ascending through rugged alpine terrain and vast high-altitude meadows. As the tree line disappears, the landscape transforms into a dramatic panorama of rocky ridges, glacial streams, and towering Himalayan peaks.
The trail offers breathtaking views of Swargarohini, Kala Nag (Black Peak), and other snow-covered summits, making today's journey one of the most scenic sections of the trek. The gradual climb helps you acclimatize while bringing you closer to the mighty Bali Pass.

itinerary.title: Trek from Odari to Bali Pass Basecamp
itinerary.description:
Trek: 3 km Altitude Gain & Loss:
13,239 ft to 15,171 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Today we will start our journey from Odari to Bali Pass Basecamp. The distance is only 3 km. You will reach the basecamp around the afternoon. Have some good rest and prepare for the tomorrow's ascent.

itinerary.title: Trek from Bali Pass Basecamp to Lower Dhamni via Bali Pass
itinerary.description:
Trek: 7-8 km Altitude Gain & Loss:
13,239 ft to 16,207 ft to 11,200 ft Accomodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Begin your day well before sunrise as you set out for the most thrilling and challenging stage of the Bali Pass Trek. The trail steadily climbs over rocky moraines and snowfields, leading to the Bali Pass (16,207 ft). From the summit, you'll be rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, Kala Nag (Black Peak), and the sacred Yamunotri Valley.
After spending some time at the pass, begin the steep descent towards Lower Dhamni. The trail passes through snow patches, loose rocks, and alpine meadows, making this section both exciting and rewarding. As you descend, the rugged high-altitude landscape gradually gives way to greener surroundings and spectacular mountain views.
By late afternoon, you'll arrive at Lower Dhamni, where you'll camp for the night in alpine tents. Enjoy a warm dinner and a well-earned rest after completing the highlight of the trek.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lower Dhamni to Yamunotri to Janki Chatti & drive to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Drive: 190 km, 6-7 hrs Trek:
8 km, 5 hrs Altitude Loss:
8,100 ft to 2,100 ft Meals:
Breakfast
Wake up to the fresh mountain air and begin your descent towards the sacred Yamunotri Temple, one of the four revered shrines of the Char Dham Yatra. The trail winds through scenic valleys, dense forests, and rocky paths, with stunning views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks along the way.
On reaching Yamunotri, take some time to visit the temple and experience the spiritual atmosphere of this holy pilgrimage site. After exploring the area, continue your trek downhill to Janki Chatti, the endpoint of your trekking adventure.
Begin your scenic drive from Janki Chatti to Dehradun. The journey winds through picturesque mountain roads, charming villages, dense forests, and river valleys, offering one last opportunity to soak in the beauty of the Garhwal Himalayas.
As you descend from the mountains, you'll pass through Barkot and Mussoorie, with beautiful views accompanying you along the way. By evening, you'll arrive in Dehradun, marking the end of your memorable Bali Pass Trek. Leave with unforgettable memories of alpine meadows, high mountain passes, pristine lakes, and breathtaking Himalayan landscapes.
Difficulty Level of Bali Pass Trek Uttarakhand
Bali pass trek difficulty/ High altitude trek at At the height of altitude of 16,207 ft. The Bali pass trek has a distance of 66 km, starting from Taluka to the endpoint at Janki Chatti. It takes 6 to 7 days to complete the trek on foot. Thus we will walk around 10 KM on average every day.
The altitude of Taluka, where the trek starts, is 6,825 ft (2080 meters). We thus have a net altitude gain of 9,250 ft (2,820 meters) over a duration of 5 days, thus climbing an average of 550 meters a day or 1800 feet. That is a considerable altitude gain. The distance, altitude gain, and finally the technical pass crossing make Bali Pass fall in the category of a Moderate-Difficult trek.
It requires physical preparation and regular exercises

itinerary.title: Drive from Dehradun to Raithal
itinerary.description:
Drive: 185 km, 8-9 hrs Altitude Gain:
1,480 ft – 7,142 ft Accommodation:
Hotel / Guest House
Meals: Dinner
We start our trip from Dehradun railway station at 6:00 am and move towards Raithal village. It takes around 8 hours to reach Raithal. Raithal village is the base camp for the Dayara Bugyal trek which is about 40 km from Uttarkashi, on the way to Gangotri. We will be passing through Mussoorie, Chamba, and Uttarkashi. There will be an Overnight stay at Raithal in a Homestay or Guest House.

itinerary.title: Trek from Raithal to Gui
itinerary.description:
Trek: 5 km, 4-5 hrs Altitude Gain:
7,142 ft – 9,630 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After early breakfast, we begin our trek. Raithal to Upper Raithal is a quick hike of simply 1 km which may be effortlessly performed in much less than an hour. It is a perfect campsite to mark the start of the trek with beautiful views of Mt. Shrikanth, Mt. Jaunli & Mt. Draupadi ka Danda.
Moving ahead you’ll witness a stunning forest full of flora and fauna. A 4 km step-by-step ascending course from Upper Raithal ends in shepherd huts at Gui, an old-fashioned little hamlet instantly out of a mythical world. We will set up our campsite at Gui. This day trek is going through open land and dense woodland at exceptional locations. You will witness igloo huts a beautiful lake(Gui taal) in Gui, a majestic landscape of Rhododendrons, and a forest covered with Silver oaks and deodar trees.
Visible peaks from the Gui base camp will be Mt.Shreekantha, Mt.Gangotri, Mt.Jaunli, and more.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gui to Chilapada
itinerary.description:
Trek: 2.5 km, 2-3 hours Altitude Gain:
9,630 ft – 10,515 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
We start our trek from Gui to Chilapada passes. The trek is relatively shorter but it takes us to higher altitudes. The trail is full of dense oak forests but as we are moving higher, the tree lines are thinning out and opening up to green meadows and the panoramic view of surrounding peaks. The campsite at Chilapada is just below the Dayara ridge and perfect to view the golden sunrise and sunset. We will acclimatize there before the summit push.

itinerary.title: Trek Chilapada to Nayanta via Dayara Top
itinerary.description:
Trek: 9.5 km, 6-7 hours Altitude:
10,515 ft up to 11,950 ft at Dayara Top, then down to 9,186 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tents
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
We start climbing early after breakfast. We are ascending towards Dayara Top, the highest point of the trek. The climb is gradual but challenging due to the high-altitude and open terrain. Once reaching the top, it's the breathtaking view that we get to see. It's a 360° view of Garhwal Himalayas. We are able to see Bandarpoonch, Black Peak (Kalanag), Srikanth and Gangotri ranges. It looks like beautiful live scenery. Spending a relishing time there, we will start descending towards Nayanta where we have to camp for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek from Nayanta to Raithal
itinerary.description:
Trek: 4 km, 4-5 hours Altitude Loss:
9,186 ft to 7,142 ft Accommodation:
Guesthouse
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
After spending night at Nayanta, we begin our descent through alpine meadows and forest trails back to Raithal. The returning journey has its own experience. We are mixed with emotions, as places are leaving behind but they are allowing us to reflect on our journey. Once back to Raithal, we will relax and comfort at the guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Drive from Raithal to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Drive distance: 185 km, 8-9 hours Meals:
Breakfast
After our breakfast, we drive back to Dehradun. We enjoy the scenic routes of Uttarkashi, Chamba and Mussoorie. Our trekking journey is going to end. These are the memories we will cherish forever.
As you settle back into everyday life, make sure to read our complete guide on how to recover after a Himalayan trek to properly heal muscle soreness and rehydrate.
Difficulty Level of Dayara Bugyal Trek
Dayara Bugyal Trek is easy to moderate level trek making it perfect for beginners. Additionally, children above 10 years of age can trek easily. Moreover, you just have to deal with and get used to the high altitude otherwise there are no such difficulties and trekking challenges during the Trek. This is also the reason this trek is preferred by families with children.
However, there can be chances that you can face some challenges mentioned below:
In the initial stage of the trek, you can face stamina tests because you have to climb to the Dayara top from base camp to the forest. Although it's not so difficult generally it depends on the stamina too.
Another challenge can be the hard snow you have to be careful while dealing with the snow because there can be chances of slipping as snow is prone to slips so, be careful and wear your microspikes while climbing the steep and firmly keep your feet.
With the high altitude trail, there can be chances of mountain sickness which can lead to symptoms of headache, weakness, nausea, and a loss of appetite. These all symptoms are rare on the trek of Dayara Bugyal, so, there is no need to worry much about.
Is Dayara Bugyal a Good First Himalayan Trek?
Yes. The trail climbs slowly, the longest day is 9.5 km and the highest point is about 11,950 ft, so most people with basic fitness manage it well, even in snow. The trail is easy to moderate, making it suitable for beginners, families, and experienced trekkers.
Who Should Do Dayara Bugyal Trek?
Beginners looking for their first Himala

itinerary.title: Drive to Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description:
Drive: 190 km, 8-9 hrs Altitude Gain:
1,480 ft to 6,400 ft Stay:
Guesthouse
Meals: Dinner
The drive from Dehradun to Sankri takes you through picturesque towns and villages like Mussoorie, Nowgaon, Purola, and Mori. The route is scenic and takes you through a dense pine forest, filling the air with the sweet aroma of pines. After driving through the forests, you’ll reach Mori, where the Tons River joins you on the route. The Tons River is the biggest tributary of Yamuna and is well-known for rafting activities. The 190 km long drive typically takes 8-9 hours to complete, so it’s advisable to start early to reach Sankri by evening. You’ll spend the night at a guesthouse before starting your hike the next day.

itinerary.title: Trek from Sankri to Juda Ka Talab
itinerary.description:
Trek: 4 km, 3-4 hrs Altitude Gain:
6,400 ft to 9,100 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Juda Ka Talab
We start our trek towards Juda Ka Talab early in the morning after breakfast from Sankri. The trek is an eventful one as we pass through local villages, such as Saud, and encounter kids heading to school and women starting their daily chores. The trail takes us through a dense pine forest, which gradually steepens until we reach a ridge. After walking on the ridge for a while, the trail evens out and widens. The thick forest provides a cool environment, shielding us from the sun’s heat. Finally, we reach the famous Juda Ka Talab, a small lake adorned with three floating landmasses. We camp by the lake, savoring a starry dinner.

itinerary.title: Trek from Juda Ka Talab to Kedarkantha Base Camp
itinerary.description:
Trek: 4 km, 2-3 hrs Altitude Gain:
9,100 ft to 11,250 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Kedarkantha Basecamp
From Juda Ka Talab, the trail leads deeper into dense pine forests until reaching a meadow with shepherd’s huts. Climbing about 2,000 feet further, trekkers will finally reach the Kedarkantha base camp, taking around 2-3 hours to complete. The trail from Juda Ka Talab to the base camp is incredibly stunning, providing an ideal setting for photographers and nature enthusiasts alike. Despite being a bit colder due to the lack of insulation, the base camp offers panoramic views of the famous peaks of Uttarakhand, making it an ideal spot for camping.

itinerary.title: Kedarkantha Summit and Back to Juda Ka Talab
itinerary.description:
Trek: 8 km, 7-8 hrs Altitude Gain & Loss:
11,250 ft to 12,500 ft to 9,100 ft Accommodation:
Alpine Tent
Meals: Breakfast + Lunch + Evening Snacks + Dinner
Kedarkantha Summit
Day 4 is the day you’ve been waiting for! The trek to the summit from the base camp is not long, and upon reaching the top, you’ll be rewarded with a jaw-dropping 360-degree view of the Uttarakhand peaks, the Chainsheel Pass, and the Kailash ranges of Himachal. You can even see the Har Ki Dun valley below. The Kedarkantha summit is marked by an arrangement of stones with a Trishul pointing to the sky. Legend has it that the peak was meant to be the original Kedarnath temple, but Lord Shiva, who was disguised as a bull hiding from the Pandavas, was disturbed during meditation by the villagers. The interruption made him change his location to the present Kedarnath temple.
After spending time on the summit, we hike back to the base camp and head towards Juda Ka Talab post-lunch.

itinerary.title: Trek from Juda Ka Talab to Sankri and drive to Dehradun
itinerary.description:
Trek: 4 km, 2-3 hrs Drive:
190 km, 8-9 hrs Altitude Loss:
9,100 ft to 6,400 ft to 1,480 ft Meals:
Breakfast
Today is the final day of our trek and we will descend from Juda Ka Talab to Sankri, which is a 4 km trek taking 2-3 hours. After reaching Sankri, we will take some rest and pack our bags for Dehradun. Going back home is always a bittersweet moment, but the journey is made easier by taking the same picturesque road back to Dehradun. As we leave behind the dense pine forests and descend towards the city, the landscape slowly changes and opens up into wider roads. Finally, we arrive in the bustling city, bidding farewell to the serene mountains and valleys of Uttarakhand.
As you settle back into everyday life, make sure to read our complete guide on how to recover after a Himalayan trek to properly heal muscle soreness and rehydrate.
Difficulty Level of Kedarkantha Trek
The Kedarkantha trek is The Kedarkantha trek is an easy to moderate trek. It suits beginners with basic fitness as well as experienced trekkers. based on the experience of the trekkers and the terrain sections, making it suitable for experienced trekkers as well as beginners. The elevation of the trail increases gradually and follows a well-defined trail that is not too technical, either. The maximum elevation is only 12,500 ft. However, the risk of AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness) is not zero, so it is important to be prepared with your AMS medicines and other essentials.
Although it does not require extreme physical fitness, and beginners can manage it with some prerequisites, there are a few notes about the difficulty factors to keep in mind. For instance, the last section, when trekkers climb to the summit, is a steep climb, heavy snowfall in extreme winters and AMS and related diseases due to low levels of oxygen at such a high altitude.

The most challenging and adventurous day of the trek. Initial ascent to reach the alpine lake followed by a glacier walk led to a steep ascent to the pass. A gently sloping, snowy 30-minute walk brings you to a sharp descent and a series of switchbacks, followed by a 2 km walk on the Bracken glacier. Trek through rocky moraines for over 3 hours before finally reaching a steady path leading to the campsite in the Kaintal meadows.

trips.title: 8 Days Exotic Bali Tour with Gili and Nusa Penida

itinerary.title: Touchdown in Bali – Welcome to Paradise!
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Bali's Denpasar Airport, meet our representative, and transfer to your hotel in Ubud.
Check in to the hotel and take some time to rest and relax.
In the evening, enjoy a special welcome dinner at an Indian restaurant.
Overnight stay in Ubud.

itinerary.title: Adrenaline in the Air – Bali Swing & ATV Adventure
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, prepare for an adventurous day in the Ubud countryside.
Experience the famous Bali Swing, soaring over lush green rice terraces with fantastic photo opportunities.
Following lunch, gear up for a thrilling ATV ride through villages, farms, and paddy fields.
Return to your hotel in the evening for an overnight stay in Ubud.

itinerary.title: Ocean Calling – Ubud to Gili Trawangan
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast, then check out and transfer to the pier.
Take a ferry across the ocean (approx. 2.5 - 3 hours) to the island of Gili Trawangan.
Upon arrival, experience a traditional Cidomo (horse cart) transfer to your hotel, as Gili is a non-motorized island.
Check in and spend the rest of the day at leisure, exploring the beautiful beaches.
Overnight stay in Gili Trawangan.

itinerary.title: Chill or Thrill – Leisure Day in Gili
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, enjoy a full day to relax or explore Gili Trawangan at your own pace.
You can rent a bicycle, go for a walk, or opt for water sports like snorkeling and scuba diving.
Enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere and a stunning sunset.
Overnight stay in Gili Trawangan.

itinerary.title: T-Rex Cliffs & Sea Breeze – Gili to Nusa Penida
itinerary.description:
Following breakfast, take a Cidomo back to the port.
Board a ferry to the spectacular island of Nusa Penida.
Enjoy a delicious Indian lunch upon arrival.
In the evening, head to the iconic Kelingking Beach to watch a breathtaking sunset.
Transfer to your hotel for an overnight stay in Nusa Penida.

itinerary.title: Sunrise Magic & Cultural Finale – Diamond Beach to Uluwatu
itinerary.description:
Start with an early morning tour of East Nusa Penida to see the sunrise at Diamond Beach.
Return to the hotel for breakfast and check out.
Board a boat back to Sanur Port on the Bali mainland.
From there, transfer directly to Uluwatu Temple on the southern coast.
Witness the famous Kecak Fire Dance against the backdrop of a beautiful sunset.
After sightseeing, transfer to your hotel in Kuta for check-in and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Slow Down & Soak It In – Leisure in Kuta
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at your hotel and spend the day at your leisure.
Explore Kuta's beaches, try surfing, indulge in a Balinese massage, go shopping, or visit the Garuda Wisnu Kencana Cultural Park.
Return to your hotel in the evening for your overnight stay in Kuta.

itinerary.title: Departure with Memories & Stories to Cherish
itinerary.description: Pack your bags and your stories. We’ll arrange your transfer to the airport as you fly back home—with new friends, unforgettable moments, and a little more wander in your soul.

trips.title: Bhutan Backpacking Trip with Phobjika Valley

itinerary.title: Arrival in Bagdogra – Transfer to Phuentsholing
itinerary.description:
Your journey begins as you arrive at Bagdogra Airport, the gateway to Bhutan. Meet our representative and start your drive towards Jaigaon, the last Indian town before Bhutan. After crossing the border, complete your permit formalities at Phuentsholing.
Once done, check into your hotel and take it slow for the rest of the day. This is your first introduction to Bhutan’s calm pace and clean surroundings.
Overnight stay: Phuentsholing

itinerary.title: Phuentsholing to Thimphu – Scenic Mountain Drive
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, begin one of the most beautiful drives of the trip towards Thimphu, Bhutan’s capital. The road winds through dense forests, waterfalls, and mountain landscapes, giving you a true feel of Bhutan’s untouched beauty.
En route, stop at Chuzom Bridge to witness the confluence of rivers. Upon reaching Thimphu, visit Simply Bhutan, a cultural museum that offers a glimpse into traditional Bhutanese life. If time permits, explore local markets or take a walk through the peaceful city streets.
Overnight stay: Thimphu

itinerary.title: Thimphu to Punakha via Dochula Pass
itinerary.description:
Start your day with a visit to the iconic Buddha Dordenma statue overlooking the Thimphu valley. From here, continue your journey to Punakha via the stunning Dochula Pass.
At the pass, take a break to soak in panoramic Himalayan views and see the 108 Druk Wangyal Chortens. As you descend into Punakha, the climate becomes warmer and the landscapes more lush.
Visit the majestic Punakha Dzong, located at the confluence of two rivers, followed by a walk across the long suspension bridge, which offers beautiful valley views.

itinerary.title: Punakha to Phobjikha Valley – Into the Wilderness
itinerary.description:
Post breakfast, begin your day with a short hike to Chimi Lhakhang, a temple known for its cultural significance and peaceful setting amidst paddy fields.
Later, drive to the stunning Phobjikha Valley, one of Bhutan’s most scenic and untouched regions. Surrounded by rolling hills and open landscapes, this valley offers a completely different vibe from the cities.
Spend your evening slowing down, enjoying the silence, fresh air, and raw beauty of nature.

itinerary.title: Phobjikha to Paro – Scenic Transfer & Leisure
itinerary.description:
Wake up to a peaceful morning in the valley before heading towards Paro. The drive takes you through winding mountain roads, traditional villages, and beautiful landscapes.
On reaching Paro, check into your hotel and take the rest of the day at your own pace. You can explore the town, visit local cafés, or simply relax and prepare for the next day’s hike.

itinerary.title: Paro Sightseeing – Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
itinerary.description:
Today is the highlight of your Bhutan trip. After breakfast, head to the base point of the Tiger’s Nest trek.
The hike takes you through pine forests with continuous views of the valley. After a steady climb of 2–4 hours, you’ll reach the Taktsang Monastery, dramatically perched on a cliffside.
Spend time exploring this spiritual site, soaking in the views, and experiencing the calm that defines Bhutan. Descend back to Paro by evening.

itinerary.title: Paro to Siliguri – Return Journey
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, begin your return journey back to India. Drive towards Phuentsholing, complete exit formalities, and continue to Siliguri.
It’s a long but scenic drive, giving you one last chance to take in Bhutan’s landscapes before re-entering India. Check into your hotel in Siliguri and rest for the night.
Highlights: Scenic return drive, Bhutan exit, cross-border journey Overnight stay:
Siliguri

itinerary.title: Bangalore to Gokarna Overnight Journey
itinerary.description:
Assemble with the group in Bangalore by evening and begin the overnight journey to Gokarna in a comfortable tempo traveller or mini bus.
Get to know your fellow travellers through fun icebreaker games and introductions. Enjoy the scenic overnight drive through winding highways and misty hill stretches as the trip officially begins.

itinerary.title: Gokarna Beaches Cafes and Sunset Views
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Gokarna and check into your accommodation.
Enjoy a refreshing breakfast before heading out to explore Gokarna’s popular beachside cafes, ideal for a relaxed lunch by the sea.
In the evening, we walk up to Kudle Hilltop to enjoy panoramic cliff views, peaceful surroundings, and a mesmerising sunset, perfect for photography and quiet moments.
Wrap up the day with a wholesome dinner at Mantra Cafe, known for its calm ambience and beautiful views, followed by a fun house party at the stay.

itinerary.title: Gokarna to Goa Coastal Road Trip
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out from the Gokarna stay and begin the scenic coastal drive to Goa.
Stop along the way for a beachside lunch while soaking in views of the Konkan coastline.
Arrive in Goa and check into your accommodation.
Spend the evening at a nearby beach with a sunset swim and relaxed downtime, followed by a lively beachside party to experience Goa’s nightlife.

itinerary.title: South Goa Beaches and Cabo de Rama
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the hotel and head to Agonda Beach, one of South Goa’s peaceful beaches known for water activities such as kayaking, paddleboarding, and surfing.
Spend time relaxing by the shore or exploring nearby beaches at your own pace.
Later in the day, visit Cabo de Rama Fort to witness a stunning sunset and enjoy panoramic views of the Arabian Sea.
Celebrate the journey with a farewell party at a vibrant venue or a laid-back beach shack.

itinerary.title: Leisure Time and Departure from Goa
itinerary.description:
Start the morning at leisure with an optional beach walk or meditation by the sea.
Enjoy your final breakfast in Goa before packing up and checking out.
Begin the return journey with a final beachside lunch, taking in Goa’s flavours one last time.
Bid goodbye to the beaches with beautiful memories of the Gokarna and Goa trip.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Bangalore
itinerary.description:
Reach Bangalore early morning around 6 to 7 am, marking the end of the Goa Gokarna road trip from Bangalore.
Return home with unforgettable memories of coastal drives, sunset viewpoints, vibrant beaches, and new friendships.

itinerary.title: Bikaner
itinerary.description:
Arrive at the designated reporting place, report to vehicle and proceed to Bikaner. The Marwad portion of Rajasthan lies partly in Thar Desert. In Sanskrit the word 'maru' means desert and 'wad' refers to region, so the word 'Marwad' literally means 'The region of Desert'. With a long, rich history and heritage and sand dunes just close by, it's not surprising that Bikaner is also called “Camel Country” .
Dinner

itinerary.title: Bikaner
itinerary.description:
Enjoy city tour of Bikaner which includes visit to Deshnok Rat temple – A unique Temple dedicated to Karni Mata of Deshnok, Junagarh Fort - one of the most decorated forts in India and houses opulent palaces that give you a peek into the lives and times of the maharajas of Bikaner. Here we also see Anup Mahal, Gaj Mandir, Sheesh Mahal, Prachina Museum, Sadul Museum. Visit Asia's biggest Camel Research Farm - where you get a chance to encounter different camel breeds. Later we view the magnificent Lalgarh Palace. Later enjoy the puppet show - An ancient art form of Rajasthan.
Extra Topping: • Bikaneri Bhujiya & Tea/ Coffee/ Soft Drink at Karni Mata Temple. • Tea / Coffee / Kulfi at Camel Research Farm.
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Bikaner – Jaisalmer
itinerary.description:
Proceed to Jaisalmer – nicknamed as the Golden city because the yellow sandstone used throughout the architecture of both the fort and the town. On arrival enjoy Camel ride, folk dance and magnificent sunset at the famous Sam Sand Dunes with dinner.
Extra Topping: Tea / Coffee en-route to Jaisalmer.
Notes: Air Cooler Tents will be provided at Jaisalmer Desert Camp.
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Jaisalmer - Desert camp Jaisalmer
itinerary.description:
Morning enjoy city tour of Jaisalmer which includes visit to Jaisalmer Fort also known as Golden Fort - A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the most prominent landmarks of the city, Jain Mandir, Patwan ki Haweli and museum - with its unique intricate carvings, architecture and design is one of the most significant Havelis in Jaisalmer and Rajasthan and Nathmalaji ki Haweli - an ornate architecture in the heart of the city. Later enjoy boating at the beautiful Gadisar Lake. In the evening enjoy Sound & Light show at Jaisalmer War Museum. Overnight at desert camp.
Extra Topping: • Soft Drink at Desert Camp, Jaisalmer. • Tea/Coffee at Jaisalmer Fort.
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Desert camp Jaisalmer – Jodhpur
itinerary.description:
Morning visit Jaisalmer War museum. Proceed to Jodhpur – Positioned in the Thar Desert's stark landscape, Jodhpur is also know as the ‘Blue city’ of Rajasthan. On arrival visit Swaminarayan (Akshardham) Temple – It is a stunning spiritual landmark known for its intricate architecture and peaceful atmosphere. Crafted from beautifully carved stone, the temple showcases exquisite detailing, majestic domes, and finely sculpted pillars that reflect traditional Indian artistry. Later enjoy free time for shopping.
Extra Topping: Tea/ Coffee en route to Jodhpur
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Jodhpur
itinerary.description:
City tour includes visit to Ummaid Bhavan Palace Museum - a magnificent piece of Rajasthan's heritage, and a symbol of new Jodhpur, Mehrangarh Fort - one of the largest forts in Rajasthan, Mehrangarh Fort holds the pride of place in Jodhpur because of its splendid architecture and the diverse history associated with it. The fort covers an area of 1200 acres and is built on 125 m high hill. Here we visit various mahals of Mehrangarh fort like Moti Mahal, Phool Mahal, Sheesh Mahal, Silah Khana, Daulat Khana and Rang Mahal. Later visit Jaswant Thada – a cenotaph built in the memory of Maharaja Jaswant Singh.. Enjoy get together with your travel companions in the evening.
Extra Topping: Kachori at Jodhpur.
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Leh
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Leh, the largest city and capital of Ladakh, surrounded by mighty Himalayas. This region is famous for its high mountain passes, dramatic landscapes, and breathtaking scenery, often called the “Paradise on Earth”.
On arrival, transfer to your hotel and take complete rest. Spend the day acclimatizing to the high altitude (cold desert region of India), as Leh is located at a very high elevation. This rest is important to adjust to low oxygen levels and enjoy a safe journey ahead.
Dinner

Today explore the beautiful city of Leh and its famous attractions. Visit the peaceful Shanti Stupa, then see the famous Magnetic Hill and sacred Pathar Sahib Gurudwara. Later, take a short nature walk for orientation, getting familiar with the surroundings, weather conditions, and tracking area. This day helps you acclimatize further and prepare for the wildlife adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Hemis National Park – Snow Leopard Spotting adventure - Uleytokpo
itinerary.description:
Spend a full day in the heart of the Himalayas, exploring one of India’s best wildlife regions for Snow Leopard tracking. The Snow Leopard, known as the “Ghost of the Mountains,” is a rare and elusive big cat, famous for its thick fur, long tail for balance, and powerful climbing ability. It is found across the high mountains of India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Mongolia, living in extreme cold and high altitudes. With the help of expert local guides and trackers, move through snowy valleys and rugged terrain in search of this magnificent animal in its natural habitat. The experience includes patient observation, short treks, and the use of binoculars to scan distant cliffs and slopes. This day offers a true wildlife adventure in extreme winter conditions, giving you a chance to witness the raw beauty of Ladakh’s high-altitude ecosystem.
Extra Topping: •Tea / Coffee during the day Notes:
Please note: Winter offers better chances to see Snow Leopards at lower altitudes, but sightings are not guaranteed. Patience is essential.
Breakfast

itinerary.description:

Later, enjoy free time in the local market, where you can shop for souvenirs, woolens, handicrafts, and experience the local culture of Ladakh.

Enjoy breathtaking views of snow-covered mountains, frozen streams, and vast white valleys along the way. On arrival at Pangong Lake, experience the magical frozen lake surrounded by dramatic Himalayan scenery. Take short walks on safe ice patches, capture stunning photographs, and enjoy the peaceful winter beauty of this high-altitude wonder. You can also experience the Frozen Pangong Lake Marathon, a rare winter event held in extreme cold conditions on the frozen lake, adding a unique and unforgettable adventure to the experience.

itinerary.title: Hyderabad
itinerary.description:

Then we proceed to enjoy boat ride in Hussainsagar lake, Buddha statue and later enjoy laser show at Lumbini Gardens.
Extra Topping: Tea / Coffee / Soft Drink at Golconda fort.
Dinner

itinerary.title: Hyderabad
itinerary.description:

itinerary.description:
Today we proceed to visit Swarnagiri Sree Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam – is famous for its grand architecture mimicking Tirumala, a gold-plated gopuram, a huge 12-foot Venkateswara idol, peaceful hilltop setting, and serene atmosphere. Later we also visit Yadagirigutta Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple – a renowned hilltop shrine in Telangana dedicated to Lord Narasimha, featuring rare, self-manifested idols of his five forms (Pancharama) within a cave. Evening return to Hyderabad.
Extra Topping: Tea/ Coffee / Soft drink en-route to Swarnagiri Temple.
Breakfast

Srisailam, also known as Sri Parvata is situated in the Rishabgiri Hills on the banks of River Krishna in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh. Also Visit Bhramaramba Devi Temple – One of the fifty two Shakti Peethas, Sakshi ganesh, Shikhareshwar.

Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Bhubaneswar
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Bhubaneswar Airport, report to the coach, and proceed to the hotel. In the evening, enjoy a temple tour of Bhubaneswar, known as the Temple City of India. Visit the revered Lingaraj Temple, the ancient Parsurameswar Temple, the intricately carved Mukteswar Temple, and the elegant Rajarani Temple, renowned for its exquisite architecture and historical significance.
Dinner

itinerary.title: Bhubaneshwar - Pipili - Dhauli - Raghurajpur - Puri
itinerary.description:
Today, proceed to Puri. En route, visit the ancient Khandagiri and Udayagiri Caves, among India's oldest rock-cut Jain cave complexes, known for their historical and architectural significance. Continue to Raghurajpur, a heritage artisan village celebrated for its traditional Pattachitra paintings and handicrafts. Later, visit Pipili, renowned for its vibrant appliqué work, and Dhauli Peace Pagoda, a symbol of peace marking the site where Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War. Arrive in Puri, one of India's holiest coastal pilgrimage destinations, renowned for the revered Jagannath Temple, golden beaches, and rich cultural heritage.
Extra Topping: Tea / Coffee enroute to Puri
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Puri
itinerary.description:
Visit the sacred Jagannath Temple in Puri, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites in India, known for its spiritual importance and rich traditions. Also, visit Rosasala, the temple’s traditional kitchen, famous for preparing Mahaprasad and recognised as one of the largest temple kitchens in the world. Later, explore the Sudam Sand Art Museum and admire beautiful sand sculptures by local artists. In the evening, enjoy free time at Puri Beach, where you can relax by the shore and enjoy the soothing sea breeze.
Extra Topping: Coconut Water at Puri Beach.
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Puri - Chilika - Puri
itinerary.description:
Today, proceed to Chilika Lake at Satpada, the most popular gateway to Asia's largest brackish water lagoon. Enjoy a scenic boat ride on the lake, offering an opportunity to spot the rare Irrawaddy Dolphins, renowned for their distinctive rounded foreheads and playful behaviour, in their natural habitat (subject to sighting) while taking in the tranquil beauty of the lagoon. Later, return to Puri.
Extra Topping: Tea / Coffee en-route to Chilika. Coconut water at Chilika
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Puri - Konark - Bhubaneswar
itinerary.description:
Today, proceed to Konark to visit the magnificent Konark Sun Temple, a 13th-century architectural masterpiece dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, renowned for its unique chariot-shaped design and intricate stone carvings. En route, visit the serene Ramachandi Temple, dedicated to Goddess Ramachandi and located on the scenic banks of the Kushabhadra River.
Extra Topping: Khaja at Puri. Tea / Coffee / Soft drink en-route to Bhubaneshwar
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Diamond Triangle
itinerary.description:
Today, enjoy a guided tour of Odisha's renowned Diamond Triangle, a celebrated circuit of ancient Buddhist heritage sites. Visit Ratnagiri, known for its rich collection of Buddhist monasteries, stupas, and exquisite sculptures; Lalitgiri, the oldest Buddhist centre in Odisha and an important archaeological site believed to house sacred relics of Buddha; and Udayagiri, one of the largest and most significant Buddhist monastic complexes in the state, offering a glimpse into Odisha's glorious Buddhist past.
Extra Topping: Tea/ Coffee at Diamond Triangle
Breakfast
Lunch
Dinner

itinerary.title: Departure from Bhubaneswar
itinerary.description:
Today, visit Nandankanan Zoological Park, a unique forest-based zoo known for its White Tigers, safari rides and natural wildlife habitats. Later, visit the Odisha State Museum, one of the important museums in Bhubaneswar, showcasing Odisha's rich history, archaeology, art, tribal culture and traditions through its collection of sculptures, coins, manuscripts and other artefacts. Later, proceed to the airport to board your flight to your hometown.
Breakfast

En-route enjoy shopping at Pipli and visit Dhauli - it is presumed to be the area where Kalinga War was fought. See the famous Shanti Stupa and inscription carved by King Ashoka. En-route visit Konark Sun Temple - a World Heritage Site.

Meals

Campsite, Shitkhadi

We drive about 90 km (3 hrs) from Srinagar to Shitkadi. You climb from about 5,200 ft to 8,500 ft, a gain of about 3,300 ft. You stay at Shitkhadi campsite tonight. Meals today: evening snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. Please reach the meeting point on time. Eat well, drink water and sleep early.

Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude

Campsite, Nichnai

After an early breakfast we start walking. Today's walk is about 12 km (7 hrs) from Shitkadi to Shekdur. You climb from about 8,500 ft to 11,000 ft, a gain of about 2,500 ft. You stay at Nichnai campsite tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. The upper part of the climb, close to 11,500 ft, is where most trekkers slow down, and that is normal.

Meals

You stay at Vishansar lake campsite tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. Expect to feel the height from about 11,750 ft onwards, so slow your steps and breathe deeply.

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Pipalkoti
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 215 km, Rishikesh to Pipalkoti (9 to 10 hrs)
Meals
Evening tea, snacks and dinner Altitude
Rishikesh about 1,100 ft to Pipalkoti about 4,200 ft Stay
Hotel, Pipalkoti
Leader tip: Drink plenty of water on the drive and walk a little in the evening.
We pick you up from Natraj Chowk, Rishikesh, and drive about 215 km to Pipalkoti. The road follows the Ganga and Alaknanda rivers through Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Karnaprayag. The drive takes 9 to 10 hours with stops, and rain can slow it.
We reach Pipalkoti in the evening and check in at the hotel. You get evening tea, snacks and dinner. Your trek leader gives a briefing and checks your documents and gear.

itinerary.title: Pipalkoti to Govindghat, then trek from Pulna to Ghangaria
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 52 km, Pipalkoti to Govindghat, then 4 km to Pulna (about 3 to 3.5 hrs)
Trek
About 9 to 10 km, Pulna to Ghangaria (4 to 5 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
Govindghat about 6,000 ft to Ghangaria about 10,500 ft Stay
Guesthouse, Ghangaria
Leader tip: Walk slowly and keep your rain jacket at the top of your daypack. Mules and porters are available if you need them.
After breakfast we drive about 52 km to Govindghat and on to Pulna, where the walk begins. The path climbs along the Lakshman Ganga river for about 9 to 10 km to Ghangaria, and takes 4 to 5 hours with rests. The path is wide and made of stone, and it is busy with pilgrims, ponies and porters.
We reach Ghangaria at about 10,500 ft and check in at the guesthouse. Your trek leader checks everyone's health. Rest, drink water and sleep early.
That works out to roughly 1000 ft of climbing an hour over 4 to 5 hours, a pace you can hold all day if you keep it even.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to the Valley of Flowers and back
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 7 to 8 km there and back (6 to 7 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, packed lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
Ghangaria about 10,500 ft up to about 11,500 ft in the valley Stay
Guesthouse, Ghangaria
Leader tip: Start early. Entry to the park is from 7 AM, and you must leave the park by 5 PM.
After an early breakfast we walk about 3.7 km from Ghangaria to the entrance of the Valley of Flowers National Park, where our permits are checked. The valley is a wide, U-shaped meadow with the Pushpawati river running through it. The path inside is gentle, and we spend several hours walking and stopping for photos. Peak flowers are from late July to August.
We eat our packed lunch in the valley and walk back to Ghangaria before the park closes. The park does not allow camping, drones or plastic, so please carry your waste back. If the rain is heavy, your leader may shorten the walk.
That works out to roughly 150 ft of climbing an hour over 6 to 7 hours, a pace you can hold all day if you keep it even.
Highest point of the trek

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib and back
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 12 km there and back (7 to 8 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch (langar at the gurdwara), evening snacks and dinner Altitude
Ghangaria about 10,500 ft up to Hemkund Sahib about 14,100 ft Stay
Guesthouse, Ghangaria
Leader tip: This is the hardest day. Start early, walk slowly and use your poles on the steps.
We start early with breakfast. The path to Hemkund Sahib is about 6 km each way and climbs about 3,600 ft in a series of switchbacks and steps. The air is thin and the day is tiring, so we walk slowly with rests.
At the top, the gurdwara sits beside a glacial lake with snow peaks around it. Cover your head and take off your shoes before you go inside. We have a simple lunch at the gurdwara (langar) and walk back to Ghangaria for dinner. If the weather turns bad, your leader may turn the group back. Safety comes first.
At 14,100 ft the air is about 7.1°C cooler than at 10,500 ft, so keep your warm layer at the top of your daypack.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Pulna, then Badrinath and Pipalkoti
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 9 to 10 km, Ghangaria to Pulna (3 to 4 hrs)
Drive
About 95 km, Govindghat to Badrinath and Pipalkoti (4 to 5 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, packed lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
Ghangaria about 10,500 ft down to Pulna, then Badrinath about 10,200 ft, then Pipalkoti about 4,200 ft Stay
Hotel, Pipalkoti
Leader tip: Use your trekking poles on the steep descent. Keep your boots and socks dry for the drive.
After breakfast we walk down from Ghangaria to Pulna, about 9 to 10 km and 3 to 4 hours. Our vehicle then takes us to Govindghat and on to Badrinath, about 24 km, where we visit the temple. We then drive about 70 km to Pipalkoti.
If rain, a landslide or time is against us, your trek leader may skip the Badrinath visit so that the group reaches Pipalkoti safely. We check in at the hotel and have dinner.
Going down 300 ft is easier on your breathing, but harder on the knees, so keep your steps short and your boots snug.

itinerary.title: Pipalkoti to Rishikesh
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 215 km, Pipalkoti to Rishikesh (9 to 10 hrs)
Meals
Morning tea or coffee only Altitude
Pipalkoti about 4,200 ft to Rishikesh about 1,100 ft Leader tip:
Book your onward travel for the next day. Mountain roads can run late.
After morning tea or coffee we drive about 215 km back to Rishikesh. The drive takes 9 to 10 hours with a lunch stop at your own cost, and rain can slow it. We drop you at Natraj Chowk in the evening, so please book your onward travel for the next day.

itinerary.description:
Altitude

After an early breakfast we fly from Kathmandu to Lukla (about 9,400 ft) or, in the busy season, from Ramechhap. The flight is short and gives you your first view of the Himalaya. From Lukla we walk down through Cheplung and Ghat to Phakding (about 8,600 ft), about 9 km in 3 to 4 hours. It is an easy first day, with prayer wheels, mani walls and suspension bridges over the Dudh Kosi. Flights to Lukla depend on the weather and can be delayed, which is why we keep spare days in the plan. You stay in a teahouse at Phakding tonight. All meals are pure vegetarian.

itinerary.title: New Jalpaiguri to Sepi
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 130 km, NJP to Sepi (about 7 hrs)
Meals
Evening tea, snacks and dinner Altitude
NJP about 374 ft to Sepi 6,400 ft Stay
Teahouse, Sepi
Leader tip: Drink water on the drive and sleep early. Day 2 is a long walk.
We pick you up from New Jalpaiguri and drive about 130 km to Sepi, a small village in the hills. The drive takes about 7 hours with stops.
We reach Sepi in the evening and check in at the teahouse. You get evening tea, snacks and dinner. Your trek leader gives a briefing and checks your documents and gear.
Sepi is at about 6,400 ft, so drink water and sleep early.

itinerary.title: Sepi to Gorkhey via Raman and Samanden
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 15 km (7 to 8 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
6,400 ft to 7,000 ft Stay
Teahouse, Gorkhey
Leader tip: This is a long first walking day. Start at an easy pace and carry a warm layer and rain gear.
After breakfast we walk from Sepi through Raman and Samanden to Gorkhey. The trail follows the hillside with ups and downs and crosses a river in the valley. The altitude gain is small, but the distance is about 15 km and the walk takes 7 to 8 hours.
We reach Gorkhey, a Himalayan village, in the evening. You sleep in a teahouse, and the night is warmer than the ridge above.
That works out to roughly 80 ft of climbing an hour over 7 to 8 hours, a pace you can hold all day if you keep it even.

itinerary.title: Gorkhey to Phalut
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 15 km (7 to 8 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
7,000 ft to 11,800 ft Stay
Teahouse, Phalut
Leader tip: Walk slowly. This is the biggest climb of the trek. Drink water often and tell your leader how you feel.
We leave Gorkhey early and climb through forest of rhododendron and bamboo and then onto open ridge slopes. The day is about 15 km and 7 to 8 hours, and the climb is about 4,800 ft.
We reach Phalut at about 11,800 ft, on the border with Nepal. On a clear evening you see Kanchenjunga and the great peaks. It is cold and windy, so put on your warm layers as soon as you arrive.
That works out to roughly 640 ft of climbing an hour over 7 to 8 hours, a pace you can hold all day if you keep it even.

itinerary.title: Phalut to Thakom
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 10 km (5 to 6 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
11,800 ft to 11,300 ft Stay
Teahouse, Thakom
Leader tip: Start early for the sunrise view from Phalut, then walk at an easy pace along the ridge.
If the sky is clear, we see the sunrise over the Kanchenjunga range from Phalut. After breakfast we walk along the ridge to Thakom. The trail goes down and up through forest and meadow, and the day is about 10 km and 5 to 6 hours.
We reach Thakom in the afternoon. Rest well, because the next two days are long.
Loose stones and steep steps are common on a 500 ft descent, so walk behind your trek leader and keep your poles ready.

itinerary.title: Thakom to Aal
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 11 km (6 to 7 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
11,300 ft to 11,500 ft Stay
Teahouse, Aal
Leader tip: Keep your layers handy. The wind on the ridge is cold.
From Thakom the trail follows the ridge to Aal, through forest and open slopes. The day is about 11 km and 6 to 7 hours, with small ups and downs. You are close to Sandakphu now, and the views keep opening up.
We reach Aal in the afternoon and stay in a teahouse.
You stay near 11,500 ft all day, so the effort comes from distance and terrain, not from height.
Highest point of the trek

itinerary.title: Aal to Timbure via Sandakphu
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 14 km (7 to 8 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner Altitude
11,500 ft up to Sandakphu at about 11,950 ft, then down to Timbure 6,550 ft Stay
Teahouse, Timbure
Leader tip: Start before sunrise for the best view of the peaks, and use trekking poles on the long descent.
We start early and walk to Sandakphu, the highest point of the trek at about 11,950 ft. On a clear morning you see Kanchenjunga, Everest, Lhotse and Makalu from one place, which is the reason most people do this trek.
After the sunrise we walk down towards Timbure, a descent of about 4,950 ft. The day is about 14 km and 7 to 8 hours, and the descent is hard on the knees.
At 11,950 ft the air is about 0.9°C cooler than at 11,500 ft, so keep your warm layer at the top of your daypack.

itinerary.title: Timbure to Srikhola, then drive to NJP
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 3 km (2 hrs)
Drive
About 130 km, Srikhola to NJP (about 7 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast only Altitude
6,550 ft to 6,900 ft at Srikhola, then the drive down Leader tip:
Book your onward travel for the next day. Mountain roads can run late.
After breakfast we walk about 3 km to Srikhola, which takes about 2 hours. From there our vehicle takes us about 130 km back to NJP. The drive takes about 7 hours with a lunch stop at your own cost. We reach NJP in the evening, so please book your onward travel for the next day.

itinerary.title: Drive from Rishikesh to Joshimath
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 247 km (9 to 10 hrs)
Meals
Evening snacks and dinner Altitude
1,200 ft to 6,150 ft Stay
Hotel, Joshimath
Leader tip: Drink plenty of water on the drive and take a short walk in the evening.
We drive about 247 km (9 to 10 hrs) from Rishikesh to Joshimath. The road follows the Ganga and Alaknanda rivers through Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Karnaprayag to Joshimath, the gateway to Badrinath and Auli. You stay at Joshimath hotel tonight.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Tugasi Village & trek from Tugasi to Gulling Top
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 35 km Trek
About 3 to 4 km Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude
6,150 ft to 8,000 ft to 8,000 ft to 9,600 ft Stay
Campsite, Gulling Top
Leader tip: Carry your medical certificate and ID for the local check.
Today's walk is about 3 to 4 km from Tugasi to Gulling Top. You climb from about 6,150 ft to 9,600 ft, a gain of about 3,450 ft. After a medical check at Joshimath, we drive 35 km to Tugasi village. From there we trek through oak forest to Gulling Top. You stay at Gulling Top campsite tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. At 8,000 ft the air is about 3.7°C cooler than at 6,150 ft, so keep your warm layer at the top of your daypack.

itinerary.title: Trek from Gulling Top to Khullara
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 4 km (5 to 6 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude
9,600 ft to 11,000 ft Stay
Campsite, Khullara
Leader tip: Walk slowly. The climb is steady and the height begins to tell.
After an early breakfast we start walking. Today's walk is about 4 km (5 to 6 hrs) from Gulling Top to Khullara. You climb from about 9,600 ft to 11,000 ft, a gain of about 1,400 ft. The trail climbs steadily through forest and meadow to Khullara, a high camp near the tree line. You stay at Khullara campsite tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. The upper part of the climb, close to 11,000 ft, is where most trekkers slow down, and that is normal.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khullara to Kuari and back to Khullara
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 7.5 km (6 to 7 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude
11,000 ft to 12,500 ft to 11,000 ft Stay
Campsite, Khulara
Leader tip: Rest well after the Kuari walk. The summit day is long.
After an early breakfast we start walking. Today's walk is about 7.5 km (6 to 7 hrs). We walk up to the Kuari meadows and return to Khullara. This day helps your body get used to the height before the summit day. You stay at Khulara campsite tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian. At 12,500 ft the air is about 3.0°C cooler than at 11,000 ft, so keep your warm layer at the top of your daypack.
Highest point of the trek

itinerary.title: Trek from Khullara to Pangarchulla & then back to Khullara
itinerary.description:
Trek
About 14 km (11 to 12 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude
11,000 ft to 15,100 ft to 11,000 ft Stay
Campsite, Khullara
Leader tip: Start in the dark with a headlamp, wear all your warm layers and walk at a steady pace. The leader decides if the group goes on, depending on weather and snow.
After breakfast we walk about 14 km (11 to 12 hrs). This is the summit day and the hardest of the trek. We start in the dark, climb the snow slope and ridge to Pangarchulla Peak, and return to Khullara. The day lasts 11 to 12 hours. You stay at Khullara campsite tonight. The upper part of the climb, close to 15,100 ft, is where most trekkers slow down, and that is normal.

itinerary.title: Trek from Khullara to Tugasi Village & drive to Joshimath
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 35 km Trek
About 11 km (7 to 8 hrs)
Meals
Breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner Altitude
11,000 ft to 8,000 ft to 6,150 ft Stay
Guesthouse, Joshimath
Leader tip: Use your poles on the steep descent, because it is hard on the knees.
Today's walk is about 11 km (7 to 8 hrs) from Khullara to Tugasi Village. You descend from about 11,000 ft to 6,150 ft, a drop of about 4,850 ft. We walk down through forest to Tugasi and drive to Joshimath. You stay at Joshimath Guesthouse tonight. Meals today: breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. All meals are pure vegetarian.

itinerary.title: Drive from Joshimath to Rishikesh
itinerary.description:
Drive
About 247 km (9 to 10 hrs)
Altitude
6,150 ft to 1,200 ft Leader tip:
Book your onward travel for the next day, because mountain roads can run late.
We drive about 247 km (9 to 10 hrs) from Joshimath to Rishikesh. You descend from about 6,150 ft to 1,200 ft, a drop of about 4,950 ft. We drive back to Rishikesh along the same river valleys.
