trips.title: Bucketlist Roadtrip in Sri Lanka: Coast to Hills

itinerary.title: The night the strangers meet
itinerary.description:
Your ExCo host meets you at Bandaranaike airport and drives you the forty-five minutes into Colombo, where the only job for the afternoon is to drop your bags, shower off the flight, and slow down to island time.
As the light goes, the twelve of you sit down to the first dinner together, phones away and no job-title introductions, the quiet ExCo ritual that turns a table of strangers into people who actually know each other by dessert.
You go to bed knowing the faces you'll be catching waves and hunting forts with all week, which is the real reason the trip starts here and not at the beach.

itinerary.title: Hunt the fort, find the tribe
itinerary.description:
Drive south along the coast road to Galle, where a 1600s Dutch sea fort sits behind ramparts you can walk end to end, all lighthouse, ocean on three sides, and lanes full of cafes and old villas.
Then the treasure hunt begins on WhatsApp: split into teams and race the tribe to light a candle in the old church, drive a tuk-tuk yourselves for a full minute, hunt down a vintage car for the group photo, and earn a juice break, the fastest way twelve strangers become a team that's laughing at itself.
Check into your beachside boutique near Mirissa as the sun drops, with the first proper dinner by the water and the whole coast still ahead of you.

itinerary.title: First wave, first party
itinerary.description:
Morning at Weligama Bay, one of the top five beginner surf breaks on earth, soft sandy bottom and gentle rollers, where a certified instructor has the whole tribe standing up and catching a first wave before lunch.
After the surf, pull on a mask and drop straight off Mirissa's reef, where green turtles graze in the shallows close enough to swim beside, everyone in the water, no one just watching from a boat.
As night falls the first party lands right on the sand, the beat where the tribe stops being polite and starts being friends.

itinerary.title: The road that climbs into cloud
itinerary.description:
Leave the coast behind and climb inland, the drivers doing the work while the window fills with paddy fields, waterfalls and the first tea slopes, with a real pitstop for lunch so the journey feels like part of the trip, not a slog.
Arrive in Ella, a hill town wrapped in tea estates, and stretch the drive out of your legs on the easy golden-hour walk up Little Adam's Peak for the view back over the valley.
Check into your tea-estate stay with the mist rolling in, a very different Sri Lanka from the beach you woke up on, and dinner with the whole hill country quiet around you.

itinerary.title: The train everyone films
itinerary.description:
This is the one everyone comes for: reserved seats on the hill-country train out of Ella, doors open and feet dangling, rolling through tunnels and over the misty tea slopes on the stretch of track that fills half of Sri Lanka's postcards.
The tribe rides it together, cameras out one minute and just watching the clouds the next, the kind of slow shared hour that turns into the story everyone tells over coffee back home.
Back in Ella the rest of the day stays unhurried, a cafe, the Nine Arch Bridge, a tea shop, whatever the group drifts into, with no schedule to chase.

itinerary.title: Tea in your hands, then stillness
itinerary.description:
Drive toward Kandy and stop on a working tea estate to do it hands-on, pluck the two-leaves-and-a-bud yourself, walk the factory floor where it's rolled and dried, and taste the difference between a good cup and a great one.
Arrive at your rustic tea-estate hideaway above Kandy, seventeen acres of river, garden and quiet, where the plan is deliberately nothing: an Ayurvedic spa treatment, a swim in the river, a book on a deck.
This is the slow middle of the ending on purpose, the tribe worn in and comfortable, saving its energy for one last night together tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Cook, feast, and one last night
itinerary.description:
Roll up your sleeves for a Sri Lankan cooking class, grinding spice and tempering curry the way it's done at home, then sit down to a village lunch that is entirely what the tribe just made together.
The rest of the day eases toward the farewell party, seeded the night before so nobody's caught off guard, the last long table where a group that met as strangers a week ago swaps numbers and plans the next one.
Depending on your flight home, tonight or tomorrow morning the cars run you back down to Colombo, three to four hours of tea country giving way to city, with the whole loop behind you.

itinerary.title: Konnichiwa, Strangers
itinerary.description:
Land, drop your bags at Gracery in Asakusa and meet the faces you'll know by heart in a week. Intros at 4.
By 7:30 we're in Shinjuku, working through an izakaya crawl one plate and one highball at a time. Dinner's on us.
Bucketlist: the first kampai, with people who were strangers this morning.

itinerary.title: Future, Then Past, Then Sumo
itinerary.description:
Morning starts barefoot at teamLab Planets, knee-deep in water and light.
Then incense smoke at Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest temple, and the snack stalls of Nakamise on the way out.
Bucketlist: ringside at SUMOLAND in Ryogoku, close enough to feel the stomp.

itinerary.title: First big hit: Lake Kawaguchiko—Fuji reflections, lakeside air, and that calm-before-the-wow.
itinerary.description:
A Postcard Day out to Mt. Fuji
We kick off from Tokyo (easy meet-up points like Tokyo Station / Shinjuku) and head out towards Fuji-country—watch the city fade into wide skies and mountain roads.
Then we take a Quick, iconic stop: the Lawson photo spot—Japan’s most accidentally-famous convenience store view, where Mt. Fuji shows up like the main character. Grab a snack, click your best shots, move on.
Slow it down at Oshino Hakkai—a charming village with crystal-clear spring ponds fed by Mt. Fuji’s snowmelt. Then we head back to Tokyo by evening, full camera roll, fuller hearts.
As evening hits, we’ll meet at the Hachiko statue, cross the legendary Shibuya Crossing, and wrap with a final Kampai dinner. If you still have energy, Shibuya jazz bars are the perfect late-night cherry on top.

itinerary.title: 285 km/h to Stillness
itinerary.description:
Shinkansen to Kyoto at up to 285 km/h. Drop your bags and wander Nishiki Market, Kyoto's kitchen.
By evening, a calligraphy master puts a brush in your hand and asks you to slow down.
Bucketlist: your name in ink, then Pontocho's lantern-lit alleys after dark.

itinerary.title: Find your Zen in Kyoto’s Timeless Sunset
itinerary.description:
Kyoto slows the clock, but today, time truly stands still. As the sun sets, we’ll watch from a 1,200-year-old temple terrace(Kiyomizu-dera 🧧) - a vantage point that has seen history unfold for centuries.
This isn’t just a sunset; it’s a portal to the past, a golden moment shared with generations before us. If Japan was calling you to find Zen, this is where you’ll feel it.

itinerary.title: Osaka Eats First
itinerary.description:
Fifteen minutes by Shinkansen and Kyoto's calm becomes Osaka's noise.
Tonight we eat our way through the backstreets: takoyaki, okonomiyaki and a round of sake, maybe three.
Bucketlist: Osaka's motto is kuidaore, eat till you drop. We take it literally.

itinerary.title: Bow to the Deer
itinerary.description:
Day trip to Nara, where the deer bow back if you bow first. Then freshly pounded mochi, still warm.
Back in Osaka for our last dinner together.
Bucketlist: the final kampai, with people who were strangers seven days ago.

itinerary.title: Mata Ne, Japan
itinerary.description:
Last breakfast, last look, then checkout and on to Kansai or Itami.
Bucketlist: the group chat that keeps going long after you land.

itinerary.title: Rovaniemi's First Northern Lights
itinerary.description:
Arrive independently in Rovaniemi and settle into Lapland Hotels Ounasvaara Chalets, where the Kemijoki River and Ounasvaara slopes frame your first afternoon.
Meet the tribe over an included welcome dinner, trading names and winter nerves before everyone pulls on layers for the night outside.
Follow your guide beyond Rovaniemi's city lights for an included Northern Lights hunt, knowing the sky decides what appears above you.

itinerary.title: Santa Claus Village and Huskies
itinerary.description:
Walk into Santa Claus Village and send a postcard home from Santa's post office, with the tribe beside you for the full Rovaniemi Christmas moment.
Meet the huskies for an included sled ride across the Lapland snow, with paws, runners and cold air setting the day's tempo.
Return to Ounasvaara with wind-reddened faces and an early night, because the sunrise snowmobile ride is waiting tomorrow morning.

itinerary.title: Sunrise Snowmobiles in Lapland
itinerary.description:
Head out early for an included snowmobile ride as the February sun comes up over the Lapland forest.
Keep the afternoon for yourself in Rovaniemi, whether that means a warm café, the Arktikum museum or a long nap.
Spend one last evening at Ounasvaara before the road turns towards quieter Posio tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Posio Road, Lake Livo Night
itinerary.description:
Leave the Rovaniemi chalets and take the road to Posio, trading three days of Lapland firsts for the stillness of Lake Livo, where a single Arctic night waits at Livo Arctic Resort.
Check into Livo Arctic Resort beside Lake Livo, where an aurora igloo gives the tribe one night built around stillness and sky.
Settle in early and let Posio go quiet around you, with no scheduled chase and no promise beyond the view outside.

itinerary.title: Scenic Train to Oulu
itinerary.description:
Have breakfast at Livo, then take the included cab back to Rovaniemi station.
Board the included train to Oulu and watch the Lapland forest give way to the coast of the Gulf of Bothnia.
Check in at Original Sokos Hotel Arina in central Oulu and keep the evening easy.

itinerary.title: Chocolate and the Frozen Sea
itinerary.description:
Start with breakfast at Arina and a slow Oulu morning.
Join an included chocolate workshop with a local chocolatier and make your own chocolates to take home.
Walk out onto the frozen sea at Nallikari beach in your own time, then pick a spot in town for dinner.

itinerary.title: Train South to Helsinki
itinerary.description:
Check out of Arina after breakfast and board the included train south to Helsinki.
Watch the snow country roll past for most of the day, with time to read, nap or swap photos.
Check in at Hotel F6 on Fabianinkatu and take a first walk through central Helsinki in the evening.

itinerary.title: Espoo Ski Turns, Sauna, Last Table
itinerary.description:
Take the included cab to Espoo for a beginner ski or snowboard session, your first careful runs on Finnish snow.
Come back to Helsinki for an included Finnish sauna, letting the warmth work through tired ski legs.
Close the week at an included farewell dinner, where the people from Rovaniemi's first table now feel entirely familiar.

itinerary.title: One Last Helsinki Morning
itinerary.description:
Check out of Hotel F6 on Fabianinkatu, packing two Helsinki nights and the whole route from Rovaniemi through Posio and Oulu into one last morning.
Make your own way from Hotel F6 to Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, roughly twenty-five to thirty minutes across the city, carrying the husky ride, the Lake Livo igloo night, the Espoo snow and the Helsinki sauna home with you.
Fly out of Helsinki with the tribe's messages already waiting, plus huskies, Lake Livo, Espoo snow and a Finnish sauna behind you.

trips.location: Hanoi, Ha Giang, Dong Van, Hanoi, Lan Ha Bay, Hanoi
trips.title: Bucketlist Roadtrip in Vietnam: The Ha Giang Loop & Halong Bay Cruise

itinerary.title: The night before the road
itinerary.description:
Land in Hanoi and settle into La Siesta Premium, a boutique hotel two minutes from Hoan Kiem Lake in the heart of the Old Quarter.
Meet the twelve strangers you'll spend the week with over a street-food walk through the lantern-lit lanes, tasting your way from bun cha to egg coffee.
No early start is tomorrow's problem, tonight is just the group finding its feet before the mountains.

itinerary.title: The long drive into the north
itinerary.description:
Leave Hanoi after breakfast for the six-to-seven-hour drive north to Ha Giang City in a private air-conditioned car, comfort breaks along the way.
Watch the flat rice country slowly buckle into limestone hills as you reach the mouth of the loop by late afternoon.
Check into the Yen Bien Luxury Hotel for a warm dinner and a real bed before the road turns wild tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Onto the karst plateau
itinerary.description:
Climb to the Quan Ba Heaven Gate for your first look at the karst, the Twin Mountains and Tam Son town laid out far below.
Wind up the Tham Ma Pass and stop at the H'Mong King's Palace, once home to the powerful Vuong dynasty who ruled these hills.
Reach Dong Van by evening and check into cliffside bungalows on the edge of the plateau, the ancient town's stone streets a short walk away.

itinerary.title: The Road of Happiness and the river below
itinerary.description:
Ride Ma Pi Leng Pass, one of the four great passes of Vietnam, carved into the cliff high above the Tu San canyon.
Drop to the water for a slow boat down the emerald Nho Que river, the limestone walls rising a thousand feet on either side.
Begin the long, scenic drive back toward Hanoi, the karst flattening out of the window one last time, and sleep in the Old Quarter.

itinerary.title: A day to breathe in Hanoi
itinerary.description:
Slow morning in the Old Quarter, Train Street coffee, the Temple of Literature, or just an unhurried walk around Hoan Kiem Lake.
The day is yours to wander, shop the lanes, or do nothing at all after the miles behind you.
Come together for a signature group dinner in the evening, mountains done and the bay ahead.

itinerary.title: Onto the water
itinerary.description:
Transfer to the coast and board a small cruise into Lan Ha Bay, the quieter, greener neighbour of Halong, away from the day-boat crowds.
Drop into a cabin with a private balcony over the water, then kayak out between limestone islands as the afternoon light softens.
Watch the sun go down from the deck over a signature dinner, the bay glassy and yours, the loudest thing the clink of glasses.

itinerary.title: One last morning on the bay
itinerary.description:
Wake up on the water, catch the mist lifting off the islands, and take it slow over a late breakfast on deck.
Cruise back to shore late morning as the trip winds down, then transfer to Hanoi in time for evening flights home.
Say the goodbyes that are harder than you expected them to be, seven days after you were all strangers.
Stay

A small cruise on the quieter, greener side of the bay, away from the day-boat crowds. Your cabin opens onto a private balcony over the water, there's a jacuzzi on the sundeck, and the whole boat carries just a handful of guests. You kayak between the islands, eat well, and fall asleep to the sound of the bay.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Tokyo & Izakaya crawl
itinerary.description:
Welcome to the electric heart of Japan - Tokyo, where tradition meets the future.
Dive into the vibrant vibe of the city with an evening that promises the buzz of friendship and the thrill of discovery.
From sizzling Takoyaki to delicate sushi, your taste buds are in for a treat. Amidst the neon-lit streets, forge connections that turn travel companions into lifelong friends.
Your best life is about to begin.

itinerary.title: World's Largest Immersive Art Experience & Tokyo’s Glamour
itinerary.description:
The morning takes you to the most awaited photo op of the trip - TeamLab Planets. Walk through dreamlike installations & feel the art.
From there, we step into history at Sensō-ji, Tokyo’s oldest temple. Light incense, make a wish, and get your fortune told the traditional way.
Then, it’s on to Asakusa for a taste of old Tokyo - street food, tiny shops, and a slice of nostalgia.
Later, we head to Ginza - Tokyo’s hub of luxury and legendary dining. But the night truly comes alive underground, where we drink like locals in the hidden bars of a subway station.

itinerary.title: First big hit: Lake Kawaguchiko—Fuji reflections, lakeside air, and that calm-before-the-wow.
itinerary.description:
A Postcard Day out to Mt. Fuji
We kick off from Tokyo (easy meet-up points like Tokyo Station / Shinjuku) and head out towards Fuji-country—watch the city fade into wide skies and mountain roads.
Then we take a Quick, iconic stop: the Lawson photo spot—Japan’s most accidentally-famous convenience store view, where Mt. Fuji shows up like the main character. Grab a snack, click your best shots, move on.
Slow it down at Oshino Hakkai—a charming village with crystal-clear spring ponds fed by Mt. Fuji’s snowmelt. Then we head back to Tokyo by evening, full camera roll, fuller hearts.
As evening hits, we’ll meet at the Hachiko statue, cross the legendary Shibuya Crossing, and wrap with a final Kampai dinner. If you still have energy, Shibuya jazz bars are the perfect late-night cherry on top.

itinerary.title: From Speed to Stillness: Ink Your Kyoto Story
itinerary.description:
Experience the world’s fastest bullet train and race through Japan at 320 km/h!
Ease into Kyoto’s rhythm and explore at your own pace. Unwind at a cosy café or wander Nishiki Market, Kyoto’s culinary hub.
Learn the ancient art of Japanese calligraphy from true masters, turning ink and brush into a meditative experience.
Party at Kyoto’s best club and grab late-night Sojus as you walk through Pontocho’s historic alleys.

itinerary.title: Find your Zen in Kyoto’s Timeless Sunset
itinerary.description:
Kyoto slows the clock, but today, time truly stands still. As the sun sets, we’ll watch from a 1,200-year-old temple terrace(Kiyomizu-dera 🧧) - a vantage point that has seen history unfold for centuries.
This isn’t just a sunset; it’s a portal to the past, a golden moment shared with generations before us. If Japan was calling you to find Zen, this is where you’ll feel it.

itinerary.title: Osaka: Japan’s street food capital
itinerary.description:
From Kyoto’s quiet charm to Osaka’s electric energy, the shift is instant.
Welcome to Japan’s street food capital, where the real magic happens off the beaten path.
Let your taste buds lead the way through Osaka’s legendary street food scene - sizzling takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and flavours you didn’t even know you needed. Paired with a round (or three) of sake, this is the kind of night that stays with you long after it ends.

itinerary.title: Meet the Deers of Nara and One Last stroll, One last sip!
itinerary.description:
Nara feels like stepping into a softer, slower world - where ancient temples meet open parks, and the locals include the city’s playful guardians.
Meet Nara’s famous bowing deer - feed them, bow back, and try not to get out-charmed.
No visit is complete without indulging in one of Japan’s most beloved treats: freshly hand-pounded mochi. Soft, chewy, and best enjoyed with a cup of coffee - the perfect way to soak in the magic of this storybook day.
We're back to Osaka by evening. A final kampai to a week of wild adventures, late-night stories, and friendships forged in the heart of Japan. It's those countless conversations, endless laughter, and the kind of moments that stay with you long after the trip ends.

itinerary.title: Saying Sayonara: Until Next Time, Japan
itinerary.description:
Wheels up, but the adventure isn’t over - Japan has a way of calling you back.
The journey comes full circle as we pack up the memories, the moments, and maybe even a few extra souvenirs.

trips.title: Bucketlist Bali: Yacht, Jungle & Villa Week

itinerary.title: Canggu Breaks the Ice
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Bali and check in at La Sari Village from 3:00 PM.
We meet in the lobby at 4:00 PM and head to La Brisa at Echo Beach for sunset, the icebreaker and the welcome dinner at 8:00 PM.

itinerary.title: Surf, Picnic, Canggu
itinerary.description:
Take the optional group surf lesson or the morning at your own pace.
In the afternoon we do an ExCo beach picnic and volleyball. The evening is open for Canggu.

itinerary.title: Cross to Nusa Penida
itinerary.description:
Check out, take the van to the harbour and the fast boat to Nusa Penida. Luggage goes separately.
We check in at Akatara and finish the day with a beer pong night.

itinerary.title: Manta Day by Private Yacht
itinerary.description:
Board the private yacht and head for the best manta and snorkelling conditions of the morning.
Back at Akatara, rest and spend one more night on the island together.

itinerary.title: Into the Hills
itinerary.description:
Take the fast boat back to Sanur and drive north into the hills around Munduk.
Check in at Puri Lumbung, then enjoy a shared dinner at the cottages with nowhere else to be.

itinerary.title: Twin Lakes and Waterfalls
itinerary.description:
Spend the day on the Twin Lake jungle route, at Ulun Danu temple and around a waterfall.
Return to the cottages for a slower second night.

itinerary.title: Kecak, Just for the Tribe
itinerary.description:
Drive from Munduk to Ubud and check in at Arya Arkananta.
In the evening we watch a private Kecak performance for our tribe, followed by the farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: One Last Bali Morning
itinerary.description:
Share the last breakfast, pack and trade photos and recommendations.
Check out by 10:00 AM and fly home from DPS after 3:00 PM. The airport ride is self-arranged.

trips.location: Hanoi, Hue, Da Nang, Hoi An
trips.title: Bucketlist Vietnam: Hanoi to Hoi An

itinerary.title: Hanoi Starts at the Table
itinerary.description:
Arrive in Hanoi and settle into the Old Quarter before meeting the tribe.
The first shared night is a street-food and beer crawl through the Old Quarter's alleys, seven-plus tastings and a drink on Hanoi's Train Street.
The night lands on Ta Hien beer street, where the whole group settles in for the first proper hang.

itinerary.title: Limestone Valleys of Ninh Binh
itinerary.description:
Leave Hanoi early for Ninh Binh, about two hours south by private van.
Drift through Trang An's limestone waterways by rowboat, then climb the Hang Mua viewpoint steps for the valley view.
Head back to Hanoi in the evening, free to explore the Old Quarter on your own.

itinerary.title: South to the Perfume River
itinerary.description:
Group transfer from the hotel to Hanoi airport, then fly together to Hue and check into Rosaleen Boutique Hotel.
In the afternoon, board a dragon boat on the Perfume River, with stops at a riverside pagoda and a royal tomb.
Gather that evening for the first of three shared dinners.

itinerary.title: Hue's Imperial Afternoon
itinerary.description:
Walk through Hue's Imperial City and its courtyards, built to be taken slowly rather than rushed.
Continue to Khai Dinh's tomb, the most ornate of Hue's royal tombs.
Close the day on Vong Canh hill for the sunset over the Perfume River, free and open.

itinerary.title: The Coastal Train to Da Nang
itinerary.description:
Board the heritage train from Hue to Da Nang, riding the Hai Van Pass for the coastal views.
Check into Whitesand Boutique Hotel, a short walk from My Khe Beach.
Settle in with a My Khe sundowner session and the second of three shared dinners.

itinerary.title: Above the Clouds at Ba Na
itinerary.description:
Cable car up to Ba Na Hills, above the cloud line with sweeping mountain views.
The day includes the Fantasy Park rides and the Golden Bridge, at your own pace.
Move on to Hoi An in the evening and let the lantern-lit old town introduce itself.

itinerary.title: Cook the Countryside
itinerary.description:
Take a jeep out to the countryside around Hoi An and the Tra Que herb village.
Cook and share a lunch built from what the village grows, included as part of the day.
Return to Hoi An for a free afternoon and evening in the old town.

itinerary.title: Hoi An, Yours for a Day
itinerary.description:
Hoi An is home base today, a short ride from the old town and An Bang beach.
The An Hoi night market and the riverside lanes sit just across the bridge from the old town.
Come back together for the third and final shared dinner, the last proper table of the trip.

itinerary.title: One Last Vietnamese Coffee
itinerary.description:
Take the morning slowly, pack and trade the last recommendations from the week.
Make your own way to Da Nang airport (DAD) by Grab, about 30 to 45 minutes from Hoi An.
Say the goodbyes over one last Vietnamese coffee before flying home.

trips.title: Bucketlist: Blue Domes of the Silk Road

itinerary.title: The soft landing before the wonder
itinerary.description:
Land in Tashkent, where your guide meets you in arrivals and whisks the tribe to a calm design-led hotel near the old town to shake off the flight.
If the timing works, wander Chorsu Bazaar under its great turquoise dome, a riot of spice mountains, dried fruit and bread, or ride the Tashkent metro, a Soviet-era art gallery disguised as a subway.
Gather for a welcome dinner as the sun drops, meet the fourteen strangers who are about to become your Silk Road tribe, and set the tone for the six nights ahead.

itinerary.title: The first sight of the blue city
itinerary.description:
Board the Afrosiyob high-speed train and watch the steppe blur past at 210 km/h on the two-hour glide from Tashkent to Samarkand, the heart of the Silk Road.
Step into Gur-e-Amir, the tomb of Tamerlane, where a ribbed dome of deep turquoise sits over the conqueror who built an empire from this city.
Save the best for last: the Registan at golden hour, three vast tiled madrasahs facing each other across a square, then linger for the free evening light show when the crowds thin and the whole facade turns electric blue against the dark.

itinerary.title: Where the tiles tell stories
itinerary.description:
Beat the tour buses to Shah-i-Zinda at opening, a narrow avenue of blue-tiled tombs so intricate they stop you mid-step, best in the soft early light with almost nobody else there.
Stand under the enormous portal of Bibi-Khanym Mosque, then dive into Siyab Bazaar for pomegranates, non bread and the non-stop theatre of a working Uzbek market.
Sit down to a plov lunch the way locals eat it, the national rice dish slow-cooked over fire, then get your hands dirty at a Samarkand paper-making workshop where mulberry bark becomes silk-smooth paper the old way, before a last blue-hour return to the Registan.

itinerary.title: Into the city that never hurried
itinerary.description:
Take the short, scenic Afrosiyob leg from Samarkand to Bukhara, trading Timurid grandeur for a lived-in old town that has barely changed in centuries.
Check into a restored 19th-century madrasah in the heart of the old city, sleeping in what was once a Silk Road scholar's cell around a still courtyard, and let the pace drop to match the town.
As the light goes gold, walk to the Po-i-Kalyan complex and stand beneath the Kalyan minaret at dusk, the tower so beautiful that Genghis Khan reportedly spared it.

itinerary.title: Craft, tea and a merchant's table
itinerary.description:
Climb the ramparts of the Ark fortress and stand before the delicate brickwork of the Samanid Mausoleum, a thousand-year-old masterpiece that survived being buried in sand.
Lose an hour in Bukhara's covered trading domes and the suzani and ikat ateliers, where embroidery and cloth are still made by hand and a good piece follows you home.
End the day with a private merchant-house dinner in an old courtyard home, the food arc's high point, followed for anyone who wants it by a traditional hammam.

itinerary.title: One last morning on the road
itinerary.description:
Take a slow craft-and-food morning in Bukhara, a final tea in the old town, a last look at the domes, maybe the ceramics you have been circling all trip.
Board the Afrosiyob back to Tashkent, the longest and most relaxed rail leg, and let the Silk Road roll out behind you one more time.
Come together for a farewell dinner in the capital, trade the week's best moments, and swap the numbers that will keep this tribe together long after the trip.

itinerary.title: You leave, the blue stays with you
itinerary.description:
Enjoy a final Tashkent breakfast and a slow morning before your transfer, with time for any last-minute bazaar find.
Your guide runs you to the airport in a private car for the evening flights home, no scramble, no stress.
Fly out with a camera roll full of turquoise domes and a group chat full of people you did not know a week ago.

itinerary.title: Tapas, Tribes & The First Taste of Spain
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Barcelona, where life is best lived one tapa and one sip at a time.
Your journey begins in true Spanish style - go hopping from one lively tapas bar to another, indulging in sizzling patatas bravas and perfectly paired wines.
With every bite, every pour and every laugh, the city already starts feeling like home with your new tribe.

itinerary.title: A Canvas of Creativity
itinerary.description:
Start with breakfast in Barcelona — soak up the sunshine, then head out to Sagrada Família.
Walk through Gaudí’s iconic masterpiece, where every façade, tower, and stained-glass glow tells a story.
Next, we head to the Moco Museum — Barcelona’s coolest stop for modern + contemporary art.
Expect bold, immersive galleries and iconic works that’ll have your camera (and mind) working overtime.
In the evening, we hike up to a secret hideout that has the best view of Barcelona. Get your beers, vibes and cheers with your new Tribe.

itinerary.title: Party at World’s Best Clubs
itinerary.description:
Take a smooth flight and land into one of the most happening places in the world — the party island, IBIZA!
Check off partying in the most legendary clubs off your Bucketlist, groove to the tunes of famous artists & party the night away with the whole town

itinerary.title: Sundowner on a private catamaran
itinerary.description:
Wake up slowly after last night’s madness. Grab a lazy brunch, sink your feet into Ibiza sand, and let the sun do its healing.
Post-lunch, we sail out on a catamaran — one of the biggest highlights of the trip. Swim in that unreal blue, breathe it all in, and have your own “wait… I’m really in Spain” serendipity moment.
We chase an iconic Ibiza sunset and let time slow down. This is your “feel infinite” hour — golden skies, soft music, and main-character energy.
Evening is yours — go all out with another party night, or keep it slow with a cosy tribe dinner date. Whatever you choose, make it very Ibiza!

itinerary.title: Welcome to Madrid!
itinerary.description: Hola Madrid! We land in the capital city of Spain known for it's architectural marvels, culinary scenery, and ofcourse football We take over the city in style! A fun segway tour that takes you across one the best parks in Europe - ride through these stunning locations, with a dash of history and it's a day well spent In the evening, cosy it up with a hot chocolate run & a side of authentic churros - a match made in heaven

itinerary.title: Time Travel to Seville
itinerary.description:
Take a train to the Ancient town of Seville - where the old world charm is still intact, Embrace colours, European tell-tales and let your heart melt on cobblestone streets We stroll along Seville’s riverside as the city turns honey-gold — slow steps, soft chats, and the most gorgeous sunset. This city is nothing short of romance novel!
A cosy “date with the tribe” — shared plates, big laughs, and taste some local orange wine or some classic Sangrias

itinerary.title: Serendipity by Day & Flamenco by Noon
itinerary.description:
Take the day slow & make it yours — stroll, shop, sip, and let Seville surprise you.
Evening hits different: A flamenco session with most beautiful tutor, claps and heels in the room, and wine to keep the night warm.

itinerary.title: Seville Finale: Make It Yours!
itinerary.description:
It’s your last day in Seville — wide open to check off your personal bucket list. Go big with skydiving, keep it chill with souvenir shopping, or rent a convertible and take a dreamy drive to Granada — whatever you choose, own the day and make it yours and....your only!
By evening, we huddle up for one final night with the tribe — stories, a few emotional moments, and the kind of hugs and goodbyes you’ll remember long after Spain.

itinerary.title: Last Breakfasts, Tight hugs & Goodbyes
itinerary.description:
Goodbye only until we meet again! The trip ends here but your journey with your new Tribe has just begun Head back home with some unforgettable memories that will last a lifetime Stay

trips.title: Bucketlist Croatia: Seven Islands, One Boat

itinerary.title: Meet your tribe before the sea does
itinerary.description:
Land in Split and drop your bags inside the old town, a maze of marble streets built right into Diocletian's 1,700-year-old palace walls, now full of cafes, washing lines and everyday life.
Tonight we eat together inside the palace, a long welcome dinner where fourteen strangers start turning into a tribe before anyone has stepped aboard a boat.
No boat yet, and that's on purpose. The first night is on land so the sea has a tribe to sail out with tomorrow, not a plane-load of strangers.

itinerary.title: Step aboard, let the week go quiet
itinerary.description:
Move to the harbour after breakfast and settle into your own cabin, the whole Adriatic waiting off the bow and nothing left to organise.
Walk Split's Roman core with a local guide, a UNESCO site since 1979 and the old seat of Dalmatia, still lived-in rather than roped off behind glass.
Sail out as the city drops behind you, and drop anchor for the first swim of the trip in a bay you could only ever reach by boat.

itinerary.title: Wake up somewhere you didn't fall asleep
itinerary.description:
Open your eyes docked off Brac, the first morning the boat has quietly moved you somewhere new while you slept.
Go ashore in Pucisca, a steep-walled quarry harbour whose white stone built the columns of the White House and the Vienna Parliament, and home to Croatia's only stonemasonry school.
Swim in the deep, sheltered natural harbour, then watch the whole white town turn gold as the light drops behind it.

itinerary.title: The beach that changes shape
itinerary.description:
Stop at Bol for Zlatni Rat, the golden spit that tops the lists of Europe's best beaches and quietly shifts its point with every change of tide and wind.
Cruise on to Hvar, the sunniest island in Croatia and an old meeting point of the international jet set, lavender hills tumbling down to a Venetian harbour.
Walk Hvar's old town at dusk with a guide reading its millennia of history off the stone, then the evening is yours in a family-run tavern.

itinerary.title: Into the electric-blue cave
itinerary.description:
Glide by tender into the Blue Cave on Bisevo, one of the Adriatic's most famous natural sights, where light rises up through a below-sea-level mouth and turns the whole chamber cobalt.
Sail on to Vis, the island the army kept closed for decades, which is exactly why it stayed unspoilt long after the rest of the coast filled up.
Wander Vis town's stone streets and quiet beaches, or take the optional jeep run out to Komiza, a fishing village tucked under the hills with wartime tunnels in the rock.

itinerary.title: Marco Polo's island
itinerary.description:
Swim in a pristine bay on the morning crossing to Korcula, a three-course lunch cooked on board as the island grows on the horizon.
Walk the herringbone stone streets of Korcula town, angled on purpose to break the wind, in the settlement that claims Marco Polo himself as a son.
Keep the evening free to eat where the locals do, no set table, no schedule, just the town and whichever konoba pulls you in.

itinerary.title: Lakes inside an island
itinerary.description:
Explore Mljet National Park on foot, two saltwater lakes mirroring the pines and a 12th-century Benedictine monastery alone on its own islet in the middle of the water.
Take a swim in the heart of the park, in a lake ringed entirely by forest with the monastery watching from St Mary's islet.
Sail on to Slano on the Dubrovnik Riviera for the Captain's dinner and live music, the last big night of the week under pine and olive groves.

itinerary.title: The whole coast behind you
itinerary.description:
Cruise past the Elaphiti islands into Dubrovnik, the Pearl of the Adriatic rising terracotta straight out of the sea.
Walk the UNESCO city walls and fortifications with a guide, the entire coast you just sailed laid out below you in one long view.
Take the cable car up Mount Srd for a farewell dinner, the lights of the old town small and far beneath you.

itinerary.title: One last morning on the water
itinerary.description:
Wake up docked in Dubrovnik one final time, the sea flat and bright out the cabin window.
Say goodbye to fourteen people who were strangers a week ago and somehow aren't anymore.
Step off with the whole Dalmatian coast now a thing you've actually done, not a thing you always meant to.

trips.title: Bucketlist Switzerland: The Great Alpine Road Trip

itinerary.title: The night before it all begins
itinerary.description:
You land in Zurich, meet the eleven strangers you'll drive the Alps with, and collect the cars that turn this from a holiday into a road trip.
A slow, beautiful cruise carries you to Lucerne, your first lake town, chapel bridge and turquoise water, no big drive to shake off the flights.
Over a long welcome dinner by the water, twelve people who booked the same wild idea start becoming the tribe who'll actually do it together.

itinerary.title: The first pass, and you feel it
itinerary.description:
You point the cars south and climb the Susten Pass, the first ribbon of hairpins that tells your body exactly why you came all this way.
You stop where the glacier tears the mountain open, walk the roaring Aare Gorge, and let the sheer scale of the Alps land before you drive on.
By evening you roll into your Interlaken base, wedged between two lakes in the adventure capital of Switzerland, the biggest day of thrills waiting.

itinerary.title: The day you jump, fly, or fall
itinerary.description:
You wake in adventure country and choose your high: tandem paraglide off a mountain (optional add-on), canyon down a gorge, or walk a cliff path with the valley far below.
You ride a cable car to a Bond-film peak for a 360 of the Bernese Alps, or brave a cold-water dip in the glacier-fed turquoise of Lake Brienz if the day is warm enough.
You come back to the lodge for a long tribe dinner, the kind where the stories get taller by the hour and nobody wants to call it a night.

itinerary.title: Chasing the Matterhorn
itinerary.description:
You drive the Grimsel Pass, all black reservoirs and stacked hairpins, climbing toward the most famous silhouette in the Alps.
You park the cars and ride the train into car-free Zermatt, where you round a corner and the Matterhorn is just there, impossibly, standing over the town.
You settle in for a fondue night under the peak, the whole tribe glowing from a day of the kind of driving you'll be talking about for years.

itinerary.title: Sunrise, then the hero road
itinerary.description:
You rise before the light for a Matterhorn sunrise, the mountain turning gold above a silent town, the kind of morning you'll describe to people for years.
Then you drive the Furka Pass, the poster road of the Alps that James Bond raced, past the ancient blue tongue of the Rhone Glacier itself.
You land in Andermatt, your pass-country base, sitting right at the crossroads where every great Swiss drive meets, the best of the roads still to come.

itinerary.title: The dam, and the question
itinerary.description:
You drive the cobbled switchbacks of the old Tremola, the hand-laid stone road that corkscrews you down into sun-warmed, Italian-speaking Switzerland.
You stand on the Verzasca dam, the 007 GoldenEye jump, 220 metres of straight-down, and decide right there who you are today. The bungee itself is an optional add-on you book on the day.
Whether you leap or just watch someone else scream, the tribe roars them on, and dinner that night tastes a lot like victory.

itinerary.title: One last great pass
itinerary.description:
You take the Klausen Pass, the quiet stunner locals keep to themselves, your final ridge-line drive with the whole valley falling away beside you.
You wind down out of the high country as the Alps slowly hand you back to the lowlands, the passes now a thing behind you, not ahead.
You roll into Zurich and park the cars for the last time, that strange, full feeling of a big trip starting to land in your chest.

itinerary.title: The long exhale
itinerary.description:
You spend a slow day in Zurich, wandering the old town lanes and the lakefront, no cars, no passes, nothing to do but let it all settle.
Over a farewell dinner the tribe trades photos and already starts plotting the next one, because a week like this doesn't want to be the last.
You sleep easy knowing you drove some of the best roads in Europe, not alone, but with eleven people who were strangers a week ago.

itinerary.title: Until the next adventure
itinerary.description:
You fly home from Zurich with the passes still unspooling behind your eyes, every hairpin and glacier and fondue night replaying on the way.
You land back in your ordinary life a little different, a little louder, carrying a week that rewired what you thought a road trip could be.
And somewhere on the flight you start counting down to wherever this tribe decides to go next, because now you know you'll say yes.
Stay
Hotels we love for this route.
We sometimes use these hotels, or hotels like these, depending on dates, availability, and the final rooming plan.
Lakeside Chalet, Lucerne
Your first two nights, a whole chalet the tribe takes over on the edge of Lake Lucerne. Full kitchen, big shared table, mountains out every window, the place the group actually becomes a group before the driving starts.
Lake Thun Chalet, Interlaken
A whole alpine house on Lake Thun, minutes from Interlaken's adventure core. Room for everyone, a terrace over the water, and the kind of long chalet evenings that turn a paragliding day into a story you retell for years.
Monte Rosa Boutique Hotel
The house where Matterhorn mountaineering began, on Zermatt's car-free main street. Small, historic and quietly luxe, with the peak framed in the window, the tribe takes it over for the Matterhorn nights.
Alpine Lodge, Andermatt
A timber mountain lodge in pass country, the crossroads of every great Swiss drive. The whole tribe under one roof, a fire going, the Furka and Tremola waiting out the door in the morning.
25hours Hotel Zurich West
Your first landing and your last, a design hotel in Zurich's buzzing West quarter. Playful rooms, a rooftop bar over the city, and a lobby that feels more like a living room, the easy bookends to a week of hard Alpine driving.
